\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{index::doc}}


\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB is software for building databases of backgammon positions. Its main strength is providing a single place to aggregate the positions a player has encountered (online, at tournaments) and to restudy them by combining any number of filters freely. blunderDB can also be used to build catalogues of reference positions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
New here? The \sphinxstylestrong{user guide} offers five end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end tutorials (first import, studying a match, an Anki session, directing a tournament, server mode) and a “how to improve” page — the most worthwhile read before diving in.

\sphinxAtStartPar
What changed from one version to the next is in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{historique:historique}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Version history}}}}}.

\sphinxstepscope


\chapter{Download and Installation}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:telechargement-et-installation}}\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:telecharge-install}}\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB is a single executable that requires no installation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latest version of blunderDB is available under the MIT license:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
for Windows: \sphinxurl{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/releases/latest/download/blunderDB-windows-0.59.0.exe}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On first launch, Windows displays a SmartScreen warning (“Windows protected your PC”). This is expected: the executable is not digitally signed. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{annexe_windows_securite:annexe-windows-malware}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{what to do}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
for Linux: \sphinxurl{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/releases/latest/download/blunderDB-linux-0.59.0}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
for Mac: \sphinxurl{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/releases/latest/download/blunderDB-macos-0.59.0.zip}

\sphinxAtStartPar
macOS issues a comparable warning, for the same reason: see {\hyperref[\detokenize{annexe_mac_securite:annexe-mac-malware}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{what to do}}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB uses Webview2 for rendering the graphical interface. It is likely that Webview2 is already present natively on your operating system. If not, the first execution of blunderDB will offer to download and install it. No user action is required.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Still on first launch, blunderDB computes the two bearoff tables used by the Eval panel in the background: about six seconds on one core, without asking anything, and the application can be used normally in the meantime. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:configuration}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{the Bearoff tab of the configuration}}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

When in doubt, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uname \sphinxhyphen{}m}} answers: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x86\_64}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aarch64}}. The AUR package \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}bin}} covers both and picks on its own.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The other files on the page are the raw Linux binaries (see below), the winget and Homebrew manifests (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{telecharge_install:install-winget-homebrew}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{winget and Homebrew manifests}}}}}), the documentation as PDF in nine languages, and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sha256}} checksums.


\section{Verifying a download}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:verifier-un-telechargement}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The two checks described here are \sphinxstylestrong{optional} and intended for advanced users: they are done from the command line and are not part of the installation. Skipping this section does not prevent anything.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every published file comes with its SHA\sphinxhyphen{}256 checksum, in a file of the same name followed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sha256}}. Download both into the same folder and check that the file you received is the one that was published:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sha256sum\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}c\PYG{+w}{ }blunderdb\PYGZus{}x.y.z\PYGZus{}amd64.deb.sha256\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Linux}
shasum\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}a\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{256}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}c\PYG{+w}{ }blunderDB\PYGZhy{}macos\PYGZhy{}x.y.z.zip.sha256\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} macOS}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nb}{Get\PYGZhy{}FileHash} \PYG{p}{.}\PYG{p}{\PYGZbs{}}\PYG{n}{blunderDB}\PYG{n}{\PYGZhy{}windows}\PYG{n}{\PYGZhy{}x}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{y}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{z}\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{exe} \PYG{n}{\PYGZhy{}Algorithm} \PYG{n}{SHA256}   \PYG{c}{\PYGZsh{} Windows}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
On Linux and macOS the command prints \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{OK}}; on Windows, compare the value shown with the content of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sha256}} file. This check is the guarantee available in the absence of code signing (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{annexe_windows_securite:annexe-windows-malware}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Windows Annex: what to do if Windows blocks the launch}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{annexe_mac_securite:annexe-mac-malware}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Mac Annex: Possible Blocking of blunderDB}}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every published file is also accompanied by a build\sphinxhyphen{}provenance attestation (SLSA, via Sigstore), proving it was genuinely produced by the repository’s official GitHub build run, with no key to manage:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
gh\PYG{+w}{ }attestation\PYG{+w}{ }verify\PYG{+w}{ }blunderdb\PYGZus{}x.y.z\PYGZus{}amd64.deb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}repo\PYG{+w}{ }kevung/blunderDB
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\section{Installing on Linux}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:installation-sous-linux}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Several formats are available for Linux. The packages and archives below \sphinxstylestrong{make blunderDB executable automatically}: unlike the raw binary downloaded through a browser, they avoid having to run \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chmod +x}} after every download or update. They also add an entry to the applications menu.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.deb}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.rpm}} packages associate the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dbx}} extension (a database exported with a password, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_partage:diffusion-controlee}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Handing out a database: origin and password}}}}}) with blunderDB: double\sphinxhyphen{}clicking a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dbx}} file received from someone opens it directly. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} extension of an ordinary database is deliberately \sphinxstylestrong{not} associated — it is too generic and shared with other software — but such a file still opens normally from blunderDB’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{Open} menu.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Native packages (.deb / .rpm)}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:paquets-natifs-deb-rpm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recommended method on Debian, Ubuntu and Linux Mint (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.deb}}) as well as Fedora and openSUSE (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.rpm}}). The package manager automatically installs the appropriate webkit2gtk dependency. Replace \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x.y.z}} with the downloaded version:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }./blunderdb\PYGZus{}x.y.z\PYGZus{}amd64.deb\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Debian / Ubuntu / Mint}
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }dnf\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }./blunderdb\PYGZhy{}x.y.z.x86\PYGZus{}64.rpm\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Fedora / openSUSE}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Arch Linux (AUR)}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:arch-linux-aur}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}bin}} package is available on the AUR and updated automatically by AUR helpers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
yay\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}S\PYG{+w}{ }blunderdb\PYGZhy{}bin\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ou : paru \PYGZhy{}S blunderdb\PYGZhy{}bin}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Flatpak}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:flatpak}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderDB\sphinxhyphen{}x.y.z.flatpak}} bundle works on any distribution where Flatpak is installed. It relies on the GNOME 47 runtime, which Flatpak downloads from Flathub if it is missing:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
flatpak\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }./blunderDB\PYGZhy{}x.y.z.flatpak
flatpak\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }io.github.kevung.blunderDB
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The bundle is installed from the downloaded file, and updated by installing the one of the next version. The application has access to the home folder to open and save databases. The command line ({\hyperref[\detokenize{cli:cli}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Command Line Interface (CLI)}}}}}) is reached with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{flatpak run io.github.kevung.blunderDB <command>}}.


\subsection{Match videos on Linux}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:videos-de-match-sous-linux}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Matches panel plays the video attached to a match with the webview’s codecs: on Linux, those of GStreamer. To play MP4 and WebM, install \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gst\sphinxhyphen{}plugins\sphinxhyphen{}good}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gst\sphinxhyphen{}plugins\sphinxhyphen{}bad}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gst\sphinxhyphen{}libav}} for H.264 and HEVC (packages \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gstreamer1.0\sphinxhyphen{}plugins\sphinxhyphen{}good}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gstreamer1.0\sphinxhyphen{}plugins\sphinxhyphen{}bad}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gstreamer1.0\sphinxhyphen{}libav}} on Debian, Ubuntu and Mint; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gstreamer1\sphinxhyphen{}plugins\sphinxhyphen{}good}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gstreamer1\sphinxhyphen{}plugins\sphinxhyphen{}bad\sphinxhyphen{}free}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gstreamer1\sphinxhyphen{}libav}} on Fedora). The AUR package lists them as optional dependencies; the Flatpak ships the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{org.freedesktop.Platform.ffmpeg\sphinxhyphen{}full}} extension. On Windows, HEVC needs the “HEVC Video Extensions” add\sphinxhyphen{}on from the Microsoft Store; macOS plays these formats natively. A file the webview cannot play is reported in the video pane, with its format.


\subsection{.tar.gz archive}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:archive-tar-gz}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For other distributions. Extracting an archive preserves the executable bit, so no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{chmod}} is needed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
tar\PYG{+w}{ }xzf\PYG{+w}{ }blunderDB\PYGZhy{}linux\PYGZhy{}webkit2gtk\PYGZhy{}4.1\PYGZhy{}x.y.z.tar.gz
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }blunderDB\PYGZhy{}linux\PYGZhy{}webkit2gtk\PYGZhy{}4.1\PYGZhy{}x.y.z
./blunderDB
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The executable in the archive is named \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderDB}}, with capitals. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.deb}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.rpm}}, AUR and Flatpak packages also install the lowercase link \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb}}, the name the command\sphinxhyphen{}line documentation ({\hyperref[\detokenize{cli:cli}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Command Line Interface (CLI)}}}}}) uses; the archive carries the same link next to the executable. To have it on your \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PATH}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ln \sphinxhyphen{}s "\$PWD/blunderDB" \textasciitilde{}/.local/bin/blunderdb}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Raw binary (advanced method)}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:binaire-brut-methode-avancee}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The raw binary \sphinxurl{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/releases/latest/download/blunderDB-linux-0.59.0} remains available. Since a browser strips the executable bit on download, you must restore it before the first run:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
chmod\PYG{+w}{ }+x\PYG{+w}{ }./blunderDB\PYGZhy{}linux\PYGZhy{}x.y.z
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two Linux variants are published depending on the webkit2gtk library version. If you get the error \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{libwebkit2gtk\sphinxhyphen{}4.0.so.37: cannot open shared object file}}, your distribution uses webkit2gtk\sphinxhyphen{}4.1: use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.deb}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.rpm}} package, the AUR package, or download the dedicated build \sphinxurl{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/releases/latest/download/blunderDB-linux-webkit2gtk-4.1-0.59.0}. Native packages select the correct dependency automatically.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Docker image (server mode)}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:image-docker-mode-serveur}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The server mode ({\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Headless mode (server)}}}}}) does not need the desktop application: every version publishes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ghcr.io/kevung/blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}serve}} image on the GitHub registry, for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{linux/amd64}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{linux/arm64}}, under the version tag and under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{latest}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
docker\PYG{+w}{ }pull\PYG{+w}{ }ghcr.io/kevung/blunderdb\PYGZhy{}serve:x.y.z
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Starting it, configuring it and the warning about the authenticating proxy are described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-docker-image}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Published image}}}}}.


\section{winget and Homebrew manifests}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:manifestes-winget-et-homebrew}}\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:install-winget-homebrew}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every release ships a \sphinxhref{https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/package-manager/}{winget} manifest (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderDB\sphinxhyphen{}winget\sphinxhyphen{}manifests\sphinxhyphen{}x.y.z.zip}}) and a \sphinxhref{https://brew.sh/}{Homebrew} cask (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}x.y.z.rb}}) on the releases page, for whoever wants to install blunderDB through these package managers from a local file. Neither is listed in the public winget or Homebrew repositories. Neither changes the nature of the executable: it stays unsigned, and the warnings described below apply as they are.


\section{Windows and Mac warnings}
\label{\detokenize{telecharge_install:avertissements-windows-et-mac}}
\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On Windows, it is possible that it may hesitate to run blunderDB. See: {\hyperref[\detokenize{annexe_windows_securite:annexe-windows-malware}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Windows Annex: what to do if Windows blocks the launch}}}}} for an explanation of why and how to bypass any potential blocks.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On Mac, it is possible that it may have reservations about running blunderDB. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{annexe_mac_securite:annexe-mac-malware}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Mac Annex: Possible Blocking of blunderDB}}}}} to understand why and bypass any potential blocks.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxstepscope


\chapter{User Guide}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:guide-utilisateur}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:id1}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide is a practical introduction to blunderDB for a quick start. Five end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end tutorials cover the most common uses; the rest of the guide remains a reference catalogue, gesture by gesture, to consult as needed.


\section{End\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end tutorials}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:tutoriels-de-bout-en-bout}}

\subsection{My first import}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:mon-premier-import}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:tuto-premier-import}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This tutorial starts from an eXtreme Gammon match file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xg}}) and ends at the list of positions where you lost the most.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Create a database.} “New Database” button in the toolbar (or \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}N}), choose a location and a name; the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} extension is added automatically.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Import the match.} Drag and drop the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xg}} file onto the blunderDB window (or \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}I}, then select it). blunderDB detects the format, imports the positions and the analysis already present in the XG file (plays, cube decisions, flags), and shows the matches panel once the import succeeds.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB takes over the analysis already present in the file, it does not redo one: a match never analysed in XG therefore has no error to show. If the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Automatically analyse after import} box is checked (configuration window, \sphinxstyleemphasis{gammonNet} tab), a bounded, cancellable analysis batch fills in the positions lacking an analysis in the background. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:configuration}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Configuration}}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Review the match.} Double\sphinxhyphen{}clicking the match row (or selecting it and pressing \sphinxstyleemphasis{ENTER}) opens the review on the last position visited. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{LEFT}/\sphinxstyleemphasis{RIGHT} keys (or \sphinxstyleemphasis{k}/\sphinxstyleemphasis{j}) step through the plays; \sphinxstyleemphasis{PageUp}/\sphinxstyleemphasis{PageDown} switch games.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Read the analysis.} \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}L} shows the Analysis panel: the best plays, their equity and the error of the play made (highlighted in the table). On a cube decision, the same key shows the cube equity table and the verdict.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{panel_analysis}.png}
\caption{The Analysis panel during a match review: the play made is highlighted in the candidate moves table.}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:id2}}\end{figure}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Find the biggest errors.} Open the Stats panel (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}D}), \sphinxstyleemphasis{Dashboard} tab: the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Top blunders} list gives the ten costliest errors, and clicking a row loads the position concerned into the analysis panel. For those who prefer the keyboard, the same thing works there too: the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bl}} command (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunders}}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{SPACE} to open the command line) loads these positions directly, with no search to build by hand. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_stats:stats}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Stats Panel}}}}} to narrow this down by player or date range once several matches are imported.

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{Studying a match}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:etudier-un-match}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:tuto-etudier-match}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Once several matches are imported, this tutorial details studying one match in particular — beyond the simple walkthrough of the previous tutorial.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Open the matches panel} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}Tab}). It lists every imported match, sortable by column (player, date, length, tournament, PR). PR and the MWC cost are defined in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{glossaire:glossaire}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Glossary}}}}}.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{panel_matches}.png}
\caption{The matches panel: sortable list, PR and MWC cost per match.}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:id3}}\end{figure}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Open the review} by double\sphinxhyphen{}clicking the row, or by selecting it then \sphinxstyleemphasis{ENTER}. The info bar above the board recalls both players, the tournament and the score.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Toggle checker play / cube decision} with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{d} key on the same position when both analyses are available (either one may be missing depending on what the imported file contained).

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{panel_cube}.png}
\caption{A cube decision in the Analysis panel: money equities, the error of each option, the best decision.}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:id4}}\end{figure}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Annotate} what you observe: \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}P} opens the Comments panel on the position shown — useful for noting \sphinxstyleemphasis{why} a play is a blunder, not just \sphinxstyleemphasis{that} it is one.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{panel_comments}.png}
\caption{The Comments panel: a thread of exchanges attached to the position shown.}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:id5}}\end{figure}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tag} a position to replay later: \sphinxstyleemphasis{SPACE} to open the command line, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#}} followed by a keyword (for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#blitz}}), \sphinxstyleemphasis{ENTER}. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:guide-edit-position}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Edit a position}}}}} to edit the position directly if the play made is not the one you want to study.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Leave match mode} with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}} command: the library returns to its previous state, and the last position visited in the match is remembered for next time.

\end{enumerate}


\subsection{An Anki session}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:une-session-anki}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:tuto-anki}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Anki panel turns a collection or a search into a deck of cards to review using the FSRS (spaced repetition) algorithm.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Build the deck.} Two possible starting points: a {\hyperref[\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:guide-collections}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{collection}}}}} of hand\sphinxhyphen{}picked positions, or a search (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}F}) — for example every cube decision flagged as an error. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bl 30}} command (30 worst errors) is a fine starting point for a first deck.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Create the deck.} Open the Anki panel (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}K}), “New Deck” button, name the deck; it synchronises with the search or collection chosen.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{panel_anki}.png}
\caption{The Anki panel: one deck per row, total cards, new and due today.}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:id6}}\end{figure}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Review} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{Study}): each card shows a position, you work out your answer mentally, reveal the solution (the board, the analysis and any comment), then rate your estimate from 1 (missed) to 4 (easy). FSRS spaces out the next showing accordingly. Nothing forces you to reveal the answer to move on if you are sure of yourself.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Warm up without disturbing the schedule} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{Cram} button): shows random positions from the deck without touching the FSRS schedule — handy before a tournament, or to review intensively without pushing back the other cards’ due dates.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_entrainement:panneau-anki}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Anki Panel}}}}} for the parameters in detail (limiting the session, target retention rate, resetting a deck).


\subsection{Directing your first tournament}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:diriger-son-premier-tournoi}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A club Sunday, thirty\sphinxhyphen{}two players, two hours before the first match. This tutorial goes from the empty room to the first round launched.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Create the tournament.} Tournaments panel (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}Y}), \sphinxstyleemphasis{+ New tournament} button in the header, type the tournament’s name, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Enter}. Open the row it created, then \sphinxstylestrong{Direct}: the tournament replaces the board in the middle of the window.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Choose the format.} The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Settings} tab opens on six club formats. Clicking the first — a Swiss with two lives switching to a bracket — is enough to begin; the number of tables is set just below.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Enter the players.} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Players} tab, type a name, \sphinxstyleemphasis{Enter}, again: the field keeps the focus and empties itself. If the club has already directed a tournament, the \sphinxstylestrong{directory} saves retyping everything — \sphinxstyleemphasis{Take} last month’s entrants is one click.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Launch the first round.} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Directing} tab, \sphinxstylestrong{Launch all}, then \sphinxstyleemphasis{Confirm}: the engine has drawn the pairings and put the matches on the tables.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Enter the results.} One click on a busy table, one click on the winner’s name. The score is optional. A mistake seen at once is taken back below the grid, in two clicks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Carry on.} The next proposals appear by themselves as the tables free up. The badge on the Tournaments tab warns when there is something to confirm, even while working elsewhere in blunderDB.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Close.} \sphinxstyleemphasis{Standings} tab, \sphinxstylestrong{Close the tournament}: the final standings are frozen, the prizes computed, and the CSV copied for the club’s accounts.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_tournois:diriger-un-tournoi}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Directing a tournament}}}}} for the detail of each view, the hall display, the printable pairing sheet and the settings during a tournament.


\subsection{Deploying server mode behind a proxy}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:deployer-le-mode-serveur-derriere-un-proxy}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:tuto-serveur-proxy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Server mode (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb serve}}) exposes blunderDB’s engine over HTTP + JSON. It \sphinxstylestrong{authenticates no one} (\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-serve-daemon-delegates-authentication.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0005}): it trusts the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}} header exactly as received, and so must always sit behind a reverse proxy that authenticates and sets that header itself. This tutorial deploys the published image behind a minimal nginx, with single\sphinxhyphen{}tenant HTTP Basic authentication, then shows how to give each member their own tenant. It is the simplest starting point, to adapt (SSO, client certificates) to your context.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Start the daemon}, bound to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{127.0.0.1}} (never exposed directly):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}p\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{127}.0.0.1:8080:8080\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}v\PYG{+w}{ }blunderdb\PYGZhy{}data:/data\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{BLUNDERDB\PYGZus{}BACKEND}\PYG{o}{=}sqlite\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{BLUNDERDB\PYGZus{}DSN}\PYG{o}{=}/data/blunderdb.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }ghcr.io/kevung/blunderdb\PYGZhy{}serve:\PYGZlt{}version\PYGZgt{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Create a password file} for Basic authentication:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
htpasswd\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}c\PYG{+w}{ }/etc/nginx/blunderdb.htpasswd\PYG{+w}{ }alice
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Configure nginx} to authenticate then relay, setting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}} itself — never the one sent by the client. A TLS certificate is a prerequisite for this tutorial, not its subject: obtain it beforehand (Let’s Encrypt with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{certbot}}, or your organisation’s certificate authority), then point to its two files here. Port 80 is only there to redirect to HTTPS.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{server}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{listen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{80}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{server\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{blunderdb.exemple.org}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{301}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{https://}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}host\PYGZdl{}request\PYGZus{}uri}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{k}{server}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{listen}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{443}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{ssl}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{server\PYGZus{}name}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{blunderdb.exemple.org}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{ssl\PYGZus{}certificate}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{l+s}{/etc/letsencrypt/live/blunderdb.exemple.org/fullchain.pem}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{ssl\PYGZus{}certificate\PYGZus{}key}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/etc/letsencrypt/live/blunderdb.exemple.org/privkey.pem}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{location}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/v1/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{auth\PYGZus{}basic}\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}blunderDB\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{auth\PYGZus{}basic\PYGZus{}user\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/etc/nginx/blunderdb.htpasswd}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}1\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}pass}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{l+s}{http://127.0.0.1:8080}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{proxy\_set\_header}} lines are read in this order: first clear the value received from the client, then inject the proxy’s own.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Check} with the health sub\sphinxhyphen{}command, which does not go through the proxy:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
docker\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{exec}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}container\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }healthcheck
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Several members, one tenant each.} The daemon only accepts a positive integer in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}: it is up to the proxy to map the authenticated account to that integer. A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map}} block placed in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{http}} context holds this correspondence, and falls back to the empty string for an account that is not listed — never to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{map}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}remote\PYGZus{}user}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}tenant\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{default}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{alice}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{bob}\PYG{+w}{     }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{location}} block then explicitly refuses an unmapped account, rather than letting it reach the daemon:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{location}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/v1/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{auth\PYGZus{}basic}\PYG{+w}{           }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}blunderDB\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{auth\PYGZus{}basic\PYGZus{}user\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/etc/nginx/blunderdb.htpasswd}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{(}\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}tenant\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{})}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{403}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}set\PYGZus{}header}\PYG{+w}{   }\PYG{l+s}{X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{\PYGZdl{}tenant\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{k+kn}{proxy\PYGZus{}pass}\PYG{+w}{         }\PYG{l+s}{http://127.0.0.1:8080}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
One tenant per member assumes the PostgreSQL backend: on SQLite, as in step 1 of this tutorial, the daemon only answers for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID: 1}} and rejects any other value. The repository provides this complete setup in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deploy/nginx\sphinxhyphen{}tenant\sphinxhyphen{}proxy.conf}}, and its Caddy equivalent in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deploy/Caddyfile}}.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Headless mode (server)}}}}} for the full surface (routes, multi\sphinxhyphen{}tenant PostgreSQL backend with Row\sphinxhyphen{}Level Security, migration from SQLite) and the published Docker image.


\section{How to improve with blunderDB}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:comment-progresser-avec-blunderdb}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Beyond the tutorials above, a simple weekly routine gets the most out of blunderDB to improve:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Import} the week’s matches (drag and drop, or recursive folder import for several files) as soon as possible after playing them — the memory of the context fades fast.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Filter the costliest decisions}: the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bl}} command (worst errors), or the Stats panel filtered on the period and the decision type (checker / cube) that weighs most in the PR.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Comment} on every position reviewed: what was missed, the structure at fault. A written comment forces an explanation — a position merely reviewed without a word is forgotten as fast as it was missed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Build an Anki deck} from these commented positions: spaced repetition brings the same patterns back until they become reflexes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Track PR per tournament} in the Progression tab of the Stats panel ({\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_stats:stats}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Stats Panel}}}}}): a curve that goes down tournament after tournament is the only signal that never lies.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This routine is only worth it if it is kept up — ten minutes a week, sustained, beats a one\sphinxhyphen{}off review that gets abandoned.


\section{Create a new database}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:creer-une-nouvelle-base-de-donnees}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To create a new database, click the “New Database” button in the toolbar. Choose a path and a name for the database, then confirm saving in the system window.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The file extension for blunderDB databases is \sphinxstyleemphasis{.db}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyboard shortcuts: \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}N}. Command: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Open an existing database}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:ouvrir-une-base-de-donnee-existante}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To load an existing database, click the “Open Database” button in the toolbar. Browse to where the database is, select the \sphinxstyleemphasis{.db} file and confirm opening in the system window.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keyboard shortcuts: \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}O}. Command: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{o}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To keep the current database open next to the new one, use \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}SHIFT\sphinxhyphen{}O}, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{⧉ Another library} button at the right of the tab bar, or the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{og}} command: each database then forms its own tab group, and a click switches from one to the other (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:groupes-bibliotheques}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Open libraries}}}}}).


\section{Merge a database}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:fusionner-une-base-de-donnees}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:guide-fusionner-base}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To merge another blunderDB database into the one currently open, click \sphinxstylestrong{Merge a database} in the toolbar. Pick the \sphinxstyleemphasis{.db} file and confirm.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is also blunderDB’s answer to “how do I synchronise my database across two machines?”: a database is \sphinxstylestrong{a single file}, two databases that have diverged are merged rather than reconciled, and deduplication by Zobrist hash does the work. See the FAQ, “Can I synchronise my database across several machines?”, for what file\sphinxhyphen{}synchronisation services can and cannot do — and for the case where several machines must work at the same time, which is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{serve}} mode’s.

\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB will intelligently merge the two databases:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Positions that do not exist in the current database will be added with their analyses and comments.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Positions that already exist will be updated: analyses will be completed if missing, and comments will be merged (adding new comments without duplicating existing ones).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Matches arrive with their games, moves and analyses; a match the current database already holds — same fingerprint — is not copied again. A tournament joins the one of the same name, which keeps its event date, or is created with the date it bore in the imported database; its matches are filed in it in the imported database’s order.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A tournament’s Direction follows: journal, pairs, tables, and each imported match takes its place back in the table; the tournament’s Encounter joins the one of the same name, or is created. A match that the current database had already filed in another tournament or another slot of the table stays there. A tournament that already has its Direction in the current database keeps it and is not attached to the imported Encounter: the import does not merge two Directions, and importing the same file again doubles nothing. The output folder is not read back: it is chosen in the current database.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Transcription drafts and player and event aliases come along, with their original dates; a name the current database already decides stays decided by it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Collections, lessons and Anki decks join those of the same name or are created. The query of a living collection that names rows by number (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{like}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ma}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tn}}) is renumbered onto the current database’s rows; when a row it names is missing, the collection arrives frozen, holding what it selected in the imported database. A living collection whose name matches a manual list in the current database leaves that list as it is. The query of an Anki “search” deck is renumbered the same way.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before anything is written, the preview gives the number of positions to add, merge and ignore, and the number of matches to add and matches already present. The result repeats these counts and names the living collections frozen, those left on a manual list, and the families the imported database is too old to carry.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A merge \sphinxstylestrong{adds}; it does not reconcile: nothing is removed from the current database because the imported one does not contain it.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The import requires that both databases have compatible schema versions. It is possible to import a database with a lower or equal version into a database with a higher version.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{caution}{Caution:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The import operation immediately modifies the currently open database. It is recommended to make a backup copy before importing another database.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Edit a position}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:editer-une-position}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:guide-edit-position}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To edit a position, press the \sphinxstyleemphasis{TAB} key to open the search panel and the position editor. Edit the position with the mouse:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Click on the points to add checkers. A left\sphinxhyphen{}click assigns checkers to player 1. A right\sphinxhyphen{}click assigns checkers to player 2. To insert a prime, click on the starting point, hold down the button, and release on the endpoint. Click on the bar to place checkers in the bar.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To clear the position, right\sphinxhyphen{}click on an empty area outside the board then \sphinxstyleemphasis{Clear the position}, or press the \sphinxstyleemphasis{BACKSPACE} key. The same menu offers \sphinxstyleemphasis{Starting position}, which sets up the checkers of a new game.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To send the cube to Player 1, left\sphinxhyphen{}click on the cube. To send the cube to Player 2, right\sphinxhyphen{}click on the cube.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To indicate the player who is to move, click on the designated dice area.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
to edit the dice, left\sphinxhyphen{}click to increase the value of a die, right\sphinxhyphen{}click to decrease it. If the dice faces are empty, the position is a cube decision.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To edit the players’ score, left\sphinxhyphen{}click to increase the score, right\sphinxhyphen{}click to decrease the score.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The input of the position with the mouse for the checkers is done in the same way as in XG.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Add a position to the database}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:ajouter-une-position-a-la-base-de-donnees}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After editing the position, the search panel is open.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To save the previously obtained position, press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}S} or click the “Save Position” button in the toolbar.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Open the command line and execute: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{w}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The board stays on screen in the search panel, and the status bar announces the position’s number: “Position no. 1234 added to the database”, or “Position already in the database (no. 1234)” if it was already there.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A position composed in the Eval panel is added the same way, or with the panel’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{Add to database} button: see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_eval:panneau-epc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Eval Panel}}}}}.


\section{Tag a position}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:etiqueter-une-position}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To add a tag \sphinxstyleemphasis{toto} to the current position, open the command line by pressing \sphinxstyleemphasis{SPACE}, type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#toto}}, and confirm the command by pressing \sphinxstyleemphasis{ENTER}.


\section{Delete a position}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:supprimer-une-position}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To delete the current position from the database, press \sphinxstyleemphasis{Del} or click the “Delete Position” button in the toolbar.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the command line, execute \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{d}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{caution}{Caution:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A confirmation is asked beforehand. The deletion does happen, but a copy of the position is kept for thirty days: see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_bibliotheque:corbeille}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{The trash}}}}}.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Import a position from XG}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:import-une-position-depuis-xg}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To import a position directly from XG,
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
display the position to import in XG and press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}C},

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
open blunderDB and press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}V}.

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The automatic paste detects the source format (XG, GNUbg, BGBlitz), as well as OpenGammon’s OGID identifier.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Import a match}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:importer-un-match}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB can import matches from various sources.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Supported formats:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eXtreme Gammon (XG): \sphinxstyleemphasis{.xg} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{.xgp} (positions) files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
GNUbg: \sphinxstyleemphasis{.sgf} files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Jellyfish: \sphinxstyleemphasis{.mat} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{.txt} files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
BGBlitz: \sphinxstyleemphasis{.bgf} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{.txt} files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
HedgeHog (OpenGammon): \sphinxstyleemphasis{.ogxm} files, with analysis

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{To import one or more match files:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}I} or click the “Import Position or Match” button in the toolbar.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select one or more files to import.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB automatically detects the format and imports the match.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A progress window shows how many files were imported, failed and skipped (duplicates), then an \sphinxstylestrong{import report}.

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB automatically detects duplicates and prevents importing a match already present in the database.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Import a folder of matches}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:importer-un-dossier-de-matchs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To recursively import all match files contained in a folder and its subfolders:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}SHIFT\sphinxhyphen{}F} or click the corresponding button in the toolbar.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select the folder containing the match files.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB automatically collects and imports all recognized files (\sphinxstyleemphasis{.xg}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.xgp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.sgf}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.mat}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.txt}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.bgf}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.ogxm}).

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A cancelled import is resumed with the \sphinxstylestrong{Resume} button of its window; an import cut short by the application quitting, with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resume}} command. Files already processed are not read again (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_partage:import-regles}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Import: what is written, what never is}}}}}).


\section{The import report}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:le-compte-rendu-d-import}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:compte-rendu-import}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An import ends on a report of \sphinxstylestrong{what it has just brought in}, rather than on a count of files read:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the new positions, and among them the ones the source tool had flagged for study;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxstylestrong{PR of this import} — the same figure the statistics show, computed over this batch alone. It is about your decisions when the database knows your name (the \sphinxstyleemphasis{User} field of the identity dialog), about both players otherwise, and the report says which;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the positions no engine has judged, with a button to start the analysis;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxstylestrong{five most expensive decisions}, clickable: one click opens the position.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A PR of zero over zero decisions is not a perfect game but the absence of an analysis: the report writes it that way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every import is recorded as a \sphinxstylestrong{batch}. The command line finds them afterwards:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }imports
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }imports\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}batch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The measured half of the report — positions with no analysis, PR, worst decisions — is recomputed every time it is read. A batch whose positions have since been analysed therefore returns today’s figures, not those of the day it was imported.


\section{The study queue}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:la-file-d-etude}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:file-etude}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The report answers “what just happened?”. The \sphinxstylestrong{Walk through} button answers the question that follows: “what do I look at now?”. It opens an \sphinxstylestrong{ordered queue} of this batch’s positions worth a second look, and brings them to the board one at a time:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the decisions that \sphinxstylestrong{cost something}, the most expensive first — what you came for;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the positions \sphinxstylestrong{flagged in the source tool}: you had already said, elsewhere, that this one was interesting;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxstylestrong{close cube decisions}: nothing was lost, but the right answer was not obvious.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A position appears only once, under the first reason that claims it: a flagged blunder is still a blunder, and offering it twice would make the queue lie about its own length. The walk is bounded at fifty positions — a queue nobody finishes is a queue nobody starts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A strip appears above the board while you walk: the progress (“3 / 25”), why this position is here, the match it comes from, and the gestures. Three of them simply open the panel where the gesture already lives — \sphinxstylestrong{Comment}, \sphinxstylestrong{Collection}, \sphinxstylestrong{Anki card} — because those gestures exist with their own rules, and redoing them in the strip would have made half\sphinxhyphen{}copies of them. \sphinxstylestrong{Skip} moves on, \sphinxstylestrong{Previous} corrects a click, \sphinxstylestrong{Leave} stops. The rest of the application keeps working: that is precisely what lets you act without leaving the queue.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Nothing is stored, and nothing records that a position was seen.} What you do with one — a comment, a collection, a card — \sphinxstyleemphasis{is} the record, and there is nothing else to keep. Running the same queue again later is therefore perfectly legitimate, and it will be the same queue.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The same list is available on the command line:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }imports\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}batch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}queue
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Blunders nothing has handled yet}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:les-blunders-que-rien-n-a-encore-traites}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:file-etude-transversale}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A queue covers only one import. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:study}} command (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:sq}}) opens the \sphinxstylestrong{cross\sphinxhyphen{}import} queue: your blunders from the whole database, all imports together, that have no comment, no Anki card and no collection yet, and that you have not marked as seen. “Your” means the database’s reference player, including their other spellings; the error must reach the library’s error threshold. The queue runs from the most costly to the least costly, capped at fifty positions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In this queue, the strip offers two more actions. \sphinxstylestrong{Mark seen} writes a mark on the position, which takes it out of the queue, then moves on to the next one: it is the only place where blunderDB records that a position has been seen, and it does so only on this action. \sphinxstylestrong{Unmark} removes the last mark placed, and the position returns to the queue. The mark is data in your database: it is never included in an export, and does not prevent deleting a match from purging the position.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }study\PYG{+w}{ }queue\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}limit\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }study\PYG{+w}{ }mark\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1234}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZdl{} }blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }study\PYG{+w}{ }unmark\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1234}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\section{Drag and drop}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:glisser-deposer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB supports drag and drop. You can drag and drop onto the blunderDB window:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
match or position files (\sphinxstyleemphasis{.xg}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.xgp}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.sgf}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.mat}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.txt}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.bgf}, \sphinxstyleemphasis{.ogxm}) to import them,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
database files (\sphinxstyleemphasis{.db}) to open or merge them with the current database,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
folders to recursively import all the files they contain.

\end{itemize}


\section{Navigate through a match}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:naviguer-dans-un-match}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To navigate through an imported match:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Open the match panel with \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}Tab}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Double\sphinxhyphen{}click on a match or press \sphinxstyleemphasis{ENTER}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{LEFT} / \sphinxstyleemphasis{RIGHT} keys to browse through moves.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxstyleemphasis{PageUp} / \sphinxstyleemphasis{PageDown} to switch between games.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}L} to display the analysis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Press \sphinxstyleemphasis{d} to toggle between checker move analysis and cube analysis.

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shortcut: \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}Tab} to open the match panel. Command: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB remembers the last visited position in each match. When returning to a match, the last visited position is automatically restored.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Manage the match panel}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:gerer-le-panneau-des-matchs}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The match panel (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}Tab}) allows you to:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
list all imported matches (sorted from most recent to oldest),

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sort matches by column (player 1, player 2, date, match length, tournament),

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
filter the list by a fragment of a player, event, tournament or date (the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Filter} field at the top of the panel, press \sphinxstyleemphasis{/} to go to it),

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
edit player names or the date with the ✎ icon of the row,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
edit a match’s transcription with the ⌨ icon of the row,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
swap player 1 and player 2 using the swap button,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
assign a match to a tournament by clicking its tournament cell,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
delete a match using the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Del} key.

\end{itemize}


\section{Manage collections}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:gerer-les-collections}}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:guide-collections}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Collections allow you to organize positions into custom groups. To access the collections panel, press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}B}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Create a collection:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Open the collections panel (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}B}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Click \sphinxstyleemphasis{+ New collection} in the panel header, type the collection’s name, then confirm with \sphinxstyleemphasis{ENTER}.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Add positions to a collection:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select the desired positions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add them to the collection from the collections panel.

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Browse a collection:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Double\sphinxhyphen{}click on a collection to browse its positions. The order of collections and positions can be changed by drag and drop.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{coll}}

\section{Manage tournaments}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:gerer-les-tournois}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tournaments allow you to organize imported matches by event. To access the tournaments panel, press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}Y}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Create a tournament:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Assign a match to a tournament:}

\section{Display performance statistics}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:afficher-les-statistiques-de-performance}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Stats panel lets you view your performance indicators (PR and MWC cost) from imported positions.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}D} or click the Stats tab in the bottom panel.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the filter bar to restrict the analysis by player, tournament, date range, decision type, or match length.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Click an indicator to jump directly to the corresponding positions.

\end{enumerate}


\section{Evaluating a position (Eval panel)}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:evaluer-une-position-panneau-eval}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Eval panel evaluates any position — not just a race. On a pure bearoff position, it computes the EPC (Effective Pip Count, see the {\hyperref[\detokenize{glossaire:glossaire}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Glossary}}}}}) and the other bearoff statistics; on any other position, the embedded gammonNet evaluator provides the candidate plays or the cube decision, offline, without XG or GNUbg.

\begin{figure}[htbp]
\centering
\capstart

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics[width=1.000\linewidth]{{panel_eval}.png}
\caption{The Eval panel: win/gammon/backgammon chances, equity and error of each candidate play, computed by gammonNet.}\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:id7}}\end{figure}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}E}, click the Eval tab in the bottom panel, or run the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eval}} command: the panel opens on a blank board, ready to edit.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To evaluate the position already shown (a position from the library, or one from a match under review) rather than a blank board, right\sphinxhyphen{}click the board then “Evaluate this position” — the position shown is sent as\sphinxhyphen{}is into the Eval panel.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The entire board is editable by click or keyboard: checkers, dice, score, cube position, player on roll. Editing only the checkers in the home board (last 6 points) on both sides puts the position into bearoff regime.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Results are shown in real time: in pure bearoff, EPC, average number of rolls, standard deviation, pip count and wastage, the win probability of the player on roll and, in the exact domain, the money cube verdict; on any other position with dice set, the candidate plays ranked by equity; without dice, the cube decision. See the “Methodology and assumptions of the Eval panel” section of the manual.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
To practise estimating these values, tick the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Challenge} box: results are hidden on every change and are revealed area by area, with a click.

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The panel works for both players simultaneously.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Display the analysis of a position imported from XG}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:afficher-l-analyse-d-une-position-importee-depuis-xg}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If a position analyzed by XG, GNUbg, or BGBlitz has been imported into blunderDB, the analysis can be displayed by pressing \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}L}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the position corresponds to a checker decision, each recorded candidate move is displayed on its own line. For each line, the information provided is in this order: the associated checker move, the normalized equity, the equity error of the move, the winning, gammon and backgammon chances of the player, the winning, gammon and backgammon chances of the opponent, the level of analysis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the position corresponds to a cube decision, the cost of each decision is displayed along with the winning chances of the position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When multiple analysis engines are present for the same position (for example XG and GNUbg), an additional column indicates the source engine of each analysis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When navigating a match, the actually played move is highlighted in the move list. If the position was encountered in multiple matches, all played moves are indicated.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{tip}{Tip:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By clicking on a move in the analysis panel, the corresponding arrows are displayed on the board.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:exporter-une-position-vers-xg}}

To export a position from blunderDB to XG,
\begin{enumerate}

\item {}

display the position to export in blunderDB and press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}C},

\item {}

open XG and press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}V}.

\end{enumerate}


\section{View the different positions}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:visualiser-les-differentes-positions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To view the different positions in the current library, use the \sphinxstyleemphasis{LEFT} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{RIGHT} keys. The \sphinxstyleemphasis{HOME} key allows you to go to the first position, and the \sphinxstyleemphasis{END} key lets you go to the last position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To display the bearoff on the left, press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}LEFT}. To display the bearoff on the right, press \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}RIGHT}.


\section{Search for positions based on criteria}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:rechercher-des-positions-selon-des-criteres}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To search for types of positions,
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
press \sphinxstyleemphasis{TAB} to open the search panel,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
edit the structure of the position to search for. blunderDB will filter positions that have at least the entered checker structure. If unsure, to maximize results, clear the position by pressing the \sphinxstyleemphasis{BACKSPACE} key. Edit the cube position and the score if necessary.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The search panel offers two checker structures, selected with the \sphinxstyleemphasis{At least} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{Except} tabs at the top of the panel:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{At least} (default): blunderDB filters positions that have at least the entered checker structure;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Except}: blunderDB excludes positions that contain one of the entered checkers. The board is outlined in red while editing this structure. A position is rejected if it contains \sphinxstyleemphasis{at least one} of the drawn elements (for example, drawing a checker on points 1, 3 and 5 keeps only positions with no checker on any of these points). The number of checkers per point is not limited: setting 3 checkers on a point excludes positions with 3 or more checkers there (useful to search for a made point without a spare). Two quick clicks on a point mark it as required to be empty (a red hatched cell, no checker of any colour); a single click on that point unblocks it.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When a point belongs to both structures, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Except} criterion prevails if it contradicts the \sphinxstyleemphasis{At least} criterion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Method 1 (simple):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Open the search window (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}F})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add and set the search filters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Confirm by clicking on “Search”.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Method 2 (advanced):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
open the command line by pressing \sphinxstyleemphasis{SPACE},

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
type \sphinxstyleemphasis{s}, and add any additional filters (for example, \sphinxstyleemphasis{cube} or \sphinxstyleemphasis{score} to consider the cube and score, respectively. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{cmd_mode:cmd-filter}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Search Filters}}}}} for a comprehensive list of available filters).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
confirm the request by pressing \sphinxstyleemphasis{ENTER}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The displayed positions are those from the database that meet the search criteria entered by the user.


\section{Going further}
\label{\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:pour-aller-plus-loin}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide covers the most common uses. blunderDB offers several further features, detailed in the manual:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Spaced repetition (Anki)} — the Anki panel (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}K}) turns a collection or a search into a deck of cards to review under the FSRS algorithm, with a free practice mode (\sphinxstyleemphasis{cram}) that leaves the schedule untouched. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_entrainement:panneau-anki}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Anki Panel}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Transcription} — the Transcription panel (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}SHIFT\sphinxhyphen{}T}) types in a match you have in front of you (score sheet, video) to turn it into a library match. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_matchs:panneau-transcription}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Transcription Panel}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Training} — the Training panel (\sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}J}) exercises, against the clock, what can be computed. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_entrainement:panneau-entrainement}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Training Panel}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Rollouts} — the Analysis panel rolls out a position to separate two choices that direct evaluation barely tells apart. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_bibliotheque:rollouts}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Rollouts}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Lessons} — a coach writes a sequence of steps and hands it to a student in a database file; the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{le}} command opens them. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_bibliotheque:lecons}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Lessons}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Command palette} — \sphinxstyleemphasis{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}SHIFT\sphinxhyphen{}P} finds a command, a tab, a filter or a match by an approximate name. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:palette-commandes}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{The command palette}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple views} — a tab bar under the toolbar keeps several independent workspaces open side by side (a search and the navigation through a match, say), each with its own position list and its own context. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:onglets-vues}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{View Tabs}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Watermarked distribution} — an export can be signed with your issuer identity (a tamper\sphinxhyphen{}proof watermark stating where the file came from) and password\sphinxhyphen{}protected for transport. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_partage:diffusion-controlee}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Handing out a database: origin and password}}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Load the worst errors} — the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bl}} command (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunders}}) loads the worst errors (equity or MWC) straight into the analysis view, under the Stats panel’s current filter, with no manual search. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_stats:stats}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Stats Panel}}}}}.

\end{itemize}
