\sphinxAtStartPar
A roll that allows no play records the dance on its own, with no extra keystroke.

\sphinxAtStartPar
With a video attached, only an explicit validation (\sphinxstyleemphasis{ENTER}, a double\sphinxhyphen{}click on a candidate, the move completed on the board) sets the action instant. The next roll digit, or a cube gesture, validates without an instant; \sphinxstyleemphasis{v} sets it afterwards. The arrows are read by their place on the keyboard, whatever its layout; \sphinxstyleemphasis{{[}} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{{]}} are read by the character typed, \sphinxstyleemphasis{ALTGR} included on a keyboard that places them that way. Without a video, these keys keep their usual meaning.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A permanent indicator, above the triangle and on the theatre\sphinxhyphen{}mode bar, says the effect of ENTER and the digits at the moment. No key is blocked:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Entry} — the cursor is at the end of the document, or on an insertion. The first line of the analysis is preselected and drawn; the digit validates the selected move before opening the next roll: the best move played costs the two dice and nothing more, its validation being carried by the first key of the following turn.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Editing move N} — the cursor is on an action already written. \sphinxstyleemphasis{j}/\sphinxstyleemphasis{k}, the arrows, the board and clicks on the analysis correct it; the digit retypes its roll in place and ENTER validates the correction, the cursor moving on to the next decision. End returns to Entry.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
What is being typed is drawn in the transcript, in dashes, in the place where it will be written: a correction covers the cell it replaces, an insertion opens a cell between its two neighbours, and the side is read from the column. Nothing is recorded before the validation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An insertion in the middle of the document goes on inserting: the validation opens an empty cell after it, and the next action is inserted in its turn instead of overwriting the one that follows. The end of the game or moving the cursor puts an end to it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A gesture with nothing to do says so, once, in the status bar: “nothing to undo” on an empty stack, “no action under the cursor” at the end of the document. The sentence clears itself and gives the place back to the expected action.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Moving the cursor back onto an action, reopening it and then retyping it corrects it \sphinxstylestrong{in place}: validating replaces the action and the cursor moves on to the next decision — after the last action, to the end of the document, where the transcription continues. If the dice are corrected and the recorded play is still a legal play of the new roll, it is kept; otherwise the first candidate of the new roll is proposed and the play is flagged “to review” until it is validated. Moving the cursor forward or back after changing something records the correction on the way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nothing is refused and nothing is deleted: inserting an action of the same side as its neighbour creates a double turn, deleting an action may create another one, changing a side may make the plays that follow illegal. These inconsistencies are marked in the transcript, never corrected on your behalf, and the cursor lands on the first of them after every gesture that writes — except where you carry on: after a correction, a deletion, an insertion or a reopened game, it stays where you are typing. Moving around or typing a die never moves it. The turn a double turn has lost is a cell of the transcript: h and l stop on it, and a roll typed there is inserted for the side it was missing from. The undo stack lives in memory: it is lost when the draft is closed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The panel itself — the list of drafts, the creation, the entry, the transcript and the draft bar — is described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_matchs:panneau-transcription}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Transcription Panel}}}}}.

\chapter{Command Line Interface (CLI)}
\label{\detokenize{cli:interface-en-ligne-de-commande-cli}}\label{\detokenize{cli:cli}}\label{\detokenize{cli::doc}}

\section{Introduction}
\label{\detokenize{cli:introduction}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
blunderDB ships a full command line interface (CLI) in the same executable as the graphical interface. The CLI is especially useful for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{bulk import} of matches: import an entire directory of match files (XG, SGF, MAT, BGF…) in a single command,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{automation}: integrate blunderDB into shell scripts for regular backups, scheduled exports, or processing pipelines,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{server usage}: manage databases on machines without a graphical environment,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{quick inspection}: check the contents or integrity of a database without launching the graphical interface.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The CLI shares exactly the same database format as the graphical interface: both write the same file, there is nothing to synchronise.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{If the application is open while a script writes.} The file is in WAL mode: a read never blocks a write, and the two programs work on the same database without getting in each other’s way. Two writes, however, queue up — the second waits for the write lock (ten seconds per statement, plus a few retries) and only fails once the wait is exhausted, with a message naming SQLite:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Error: failed to import match: sqlite: save match: database is locked (5) (SQLITE\PYGZus{}BUSY)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The graphical interface does not watch the file: it keeps displaying what it had loaded until \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}R}} reloads the positions. Nothing is lost, but the screen lags behind the database.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{General syntax}
\label{\detokenize{cli:syntaxe-generale}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The mode is detected automatically: if the first argument is a CLI command, blunderDB launches in headless mode, otherwise it launches the graphical interface.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} GUI}
./blunderdb

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} CLI}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}command\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The examples on this page write \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{./blunderdb}}: the binary as downloaded, called from the folder it sits in. Installed by a package, or linked from a folder on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PATH}} (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{telecharge_install:telecharge-install}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Download and Installation}}}}}), it is simply called \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Boolean options announced “default: yes” are turned off with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}option=false}} form — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}recursive=false}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analysis=false}}. The space\sphinxhyphen{}separated form does not exist: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}recursive false}} leaves the option at its default value and treats \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} as a stray argument.

\subsubsection{create — Create a database}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:create-creer-une-base-de-donnees}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a new database file with optional metadata.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }create\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}user\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}name\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}description\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}text\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}force\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} — Path to the database file to create (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}user}} — Database owner name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}description}} — Database description.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}force}} — Overwrite the file if it already exists.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} (default) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (path, version, user, description, creation date).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} extension is added automatically if missing. Parent directories are created as needed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }create\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }mes\PYGZus{}matchs.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}user\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Jean\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}description\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Matchs de tournoi 2025\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{import — Import data}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:import-importer-des-donnees}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Import match or position files into the database.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}type\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} — Path to the database (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type}} — Import type: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{batch}} (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}file}} — File to import (for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dir}} — Directory to import (for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{batch}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}recursive}} — Recursively scan subdirectories (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watch}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type batch}}: does not stop, and imports each match file \sphinxstylestrong{as it appears} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dir}} (Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}C to stop).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watch\sphinxhyphen{}every}} — How often \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watch}} looks (default: 10s, floor 2s).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}resume}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type batch}}: resumes the batch with this number (shown when the import starts, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{batch\_id}} in JSON). Files with the same path, size and date as in its log are skipped without being read, those with the same content are read but not analysed; files in error are retried.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} (default) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}fail\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}error}} — Fails if at least one item (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{batch}}) could not be imported, even when others succeeded.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}skip\sphinxhyphen{}duplicates}} — Skips a match already in the database without taking its deeper analyses (study marks are still applied). By default, a duplicate replaces each stored analysis with its own when it is strictly deeper, and the line says so: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DUPLICATE (N analyses deepened)}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A decision whose analysis holds a value that is not a finite number (NaN or infinity) is imported without that analysis, and the rest of the match comes in as usual; the batch report gives their number (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Decisions imported without their analysis}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The exit code follows four rules:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{nothing was recognised} — every file failed — : error, whether \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}fail\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}error}} is passed or not;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{only duplicates} — every file was already in the database — : success. A directory re\sphinxhyphen{}run with no new file, a script’s ordinary night, exits with 0 and only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicates}} non\sphinxhyphen{}zero;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{partial failure} (some items imported, others rejected): error only if \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}fail\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}error}} is passed;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
at least one new item imported, without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}fail\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}error}}: success, with the rejected files listed in the table.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Watching a folder}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:surveiller-un-dossier}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watch}} turns the directory import into a watch: the command does not return, and imports each match file that \sphinxstylestrong{appears} in the folder. It is the headless form of the application’s {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:dossier-surveille}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{watched folder}}}}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Importer ce que le dossier contient déjà, puis surveiller ce qui arrive}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }batch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZti{}/XG/Matches
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }batch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZti{}/XG/Matches\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}watch
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only files that appear are imported: whatever the folder holds at start\sphinxhyphen{}up is recorded as known and left alone — pointing a watch at four years of matches must not import all of them. The two commands above therefore compose exactly as one would hope.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A file is imported only once its \sphinxstylestrong{size has settled}, that is, seen twice unchanged: a match another program is writing grows from one look to the next, and importing it half\sphinxhyphen{}written would give a syntax error nobody can act on. The folder is not walked recursively. A network share that has become unreadable does not stop the watch, and its contents do not pass for new when it comes back.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} database that appears in the folder is merged as by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{import \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type database}}: this is how the incremental export of another machine arrives (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:synchroniser-deux-machines}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Synchronising two machines}}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}C stops between files, never inside one: the file being imported finishes and its report is printed before the command returns.


\paragraph{Import a match}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:import-d-un-match}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Supported formats: eXtreme Gammon (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xg}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xgp}}), GNUbg (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sgf}}), Jellyfish (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.txt}}), BGBlitz (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.bgf}}) and HedgeHog (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ogxm}}).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }match\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }match.xg

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Successfully imported match (ID: 1)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Match Details:}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   Players: Kévin Unger vs Maxence Job}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   Event: HSBT Paris 2023}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   Match Length: 7}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   Games: 7}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}} delivers the same fields in a single document:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}type\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}match\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}match\PYGZus{}id\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}player1\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Kévin Unger\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}player2\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Maxence Job\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}event\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}HSBT Paris 2023\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}location\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Paris, Fédération Française de Bridge\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}match\PYGZus{}length\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{7}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}games\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{7}
\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Import positions}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:import-de-positions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Imports positions from a text file, \sphinxstylestrong{one JSON position per line}. This is exactly what \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type positions}} writes: the two commands answer each other, an export re\sphinxhyphen{}imports as is, with nothing to touch up.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }position\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }positions.txt

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Successfully imported 4 positions}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A line, as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export}} produces it — the board takes up most of it, twenty\sphinxhyphen{}six points followed by the checkers off:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}id\PYGZdq{}:1,\PYGZdq{}board\PYGZdq{}:\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}points\PYGZdq{}:[\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}checkers\PYGZdq{}:0,\PYGZdq{}color\PYGZdq{}:0\PYGZcb{},\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}checkers\PYGZdq{}:1,\PYGZdq{}color\PYGZdq{}:1\PYGZcb{},…],\PYGZdq{}bearoff\PYGZdq{}:[0,0]\PYGZcb{},\PYGZdq{}cube\PYGZdq{}:\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}owner\PYGZdq{}:\PYGZhy{}1,\PYGZdq{}value\PYGZdq{}:0\PYGZcb{},\PYGZdq{}dice\PYGZdq{}:[0,0],\PYGZdq{}score\PYGZdq{}:[7,7],\PYGZdq{}player\PYGZus{}on\PYGZus{}roll\PYGZdq{}:0,\PYGZdq{}decision\PYGZus{}type\PYGZdq{}:1,\PYGZdq{}has\PYGZus{}jacoby\PYGZdq{}:0,\PYGZdq{}has\PYGZus{}beaver\PYGZdq{}:0,\PYGZdq{}individually\PYGZus{}imported\PYGZdq{}:true,\PYGZdq{}flagged\PYGZdq{}:false\PYGZcb{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The analysis and the comments do not travel through this format: it carries the position, nothing else. To move an entire library, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type database}} is the one to use.


\paragraph{Importing a database}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:import-d-une-base}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Merges another blunderDB database (\sphinxstyleemphasis{.db}) into the one given by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}}, by the rules of the desktop application’s merge and of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.db}} in server mode ({\hyperref[\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:guide-fusionner-base}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Merge a database}}}}}): positions, matches, tournaments, collections, lessons, Anki decks, drafts and aliases, as well as the tournaments’ Direction and their Encounter. Importing the same file twice changes nothing. The text output counts the matches added and already present, the Directions and Encounters read back, and names the living collections frozen or left on a manual list, and the families the database is too old to carry.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analyze}} counts what the file would bring — its positions and those the database already holds, its new or already present matches, its collections, lessons and Anki decks — without importing anything; it is the same computation as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.dbAnalyze}} in server mode. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}max\sphinxhyphen{}positions N}} brings in at most \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}} positions, taken among the first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{N}} of the file in the order of their original identifier. A match, a collection, a lesson or a deck that touches a position left out is left out entirely; so is a position that nothing would hold after the import (no match or collection brought in, no lesson, no deck, no individual import, no user comment, no study mark). So a later import without a cap brings in complete what was missing. The output counts, family by family, what was left out. An error or an interruption during the import writes nothing: the whole merge fits in one transaction.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }database\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }club.db
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }database\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }club.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }json
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }database\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }club.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}analyze
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }database\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }club.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}max\PYGZhy{}positions\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5000}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Batch import}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:import-par-lot}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Import all match files from a directory in a single operation. This is the most efficient method for importing a large number of matches.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }batch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }./matchs/
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }batch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }./matchs/\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}recursive\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{false}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }batch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }./matchs/\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }json\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}fail\PYGZhy{}on\PYGZhy{}error
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A summary table shows for each file whether the import succeeded (\(\checkmark\)), failed (✗) or was a duplicate (⊘). A duplicate is not counted as a failure, and a batch containing only duplicates is a success (see the rules above).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each file of the batch is logged (path, size, date, SHA\sphinxhyphen{}256, resulting match or error). The batch number is shown at the start; if the import is interrupted, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}resume}} continues it without analysing again what is already decided. With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}}, the final object carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{batch\_id}} and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{journal}} array.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }batch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }./matchs/\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}resume\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}} gives the same thing in a script\sphinxhyphen{}friendly form: one object per file in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{files}}, then the totals. A quiet night leaves \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicates}} alone non\sphinxhyphen{}zero and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{failed}} at zero, with the exit code at 0; only a batch where nothing was recognised exits in error.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}files\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}file\PYGZus{}path\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}02\PYGZus{}NDT\PYGZus{}FR.txt\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}success\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kc}{false}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}error\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}failed to parse file: …\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{},}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}file\PYGZus{}path\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}test.xg\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}success\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kc}{true}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}positions\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{341}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{],}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}total\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}success\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}

\subsubsection{export — Export data}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:export-exporter-des-donnees}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Export database contents to files.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}type\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}output\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} — Source database (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type}} — Export type: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{database}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mat}} (export of one or more matches as a Jellyfish \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} transcript) (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}file}} — Output file (required, except for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type mat}} used with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dir}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dir}} — Output directory for batch \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} export (several matches, one file per match; without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}ids}}, all matches are exported).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analysis}} — Include analysis (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}comments}} — Include comments (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filters}} — Include filter library (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}played\sphinxhyphen{}moves}} — Include played moves (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}matches}} — Include matches (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}transcriptions}} — Include the transcription draft of each exported match (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}aliases}} — Include the player and event aliases the exported matches write, so that the merging of players follows them (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collections}} — Include collections (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournaments}} — Include tournaments (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}decks}} — Include the Anki decks (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lessons}} — Include lessons, with the collections and positions their steps show (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}anki\sphinxhyphen{}history}} — Carry the review history of the exported decks: the state of each card and the log of its reviews (default: yes).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — IDs of the collections to export (comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated, empty = all).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — Match IDs to export (comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated, empty = all).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — IDs of the tournaments to export (comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated, empty = all).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — IDs of the Anki decks to export with their positions (comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated, empty = all).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lesson\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — IDs of the lessons to export (comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated, empty = all).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}password}} — Wraps the result in an encrypted container (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dbx}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watermark}} — Writes a \sphinxstylestrong{signed} statement of origin into the exported file (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_partage:diffusion-controlee}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Handing out a database: origin and password}}}}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watermark\sphinxhyphen{}note}} — Free text attached to the watermark (terms of use, contact); used together with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watermark}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} (default) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (a document summarising the export: path, size in bytes, counts).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}incremental}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type database}}: exports only what has entered the library since the last incremental export to the same folder, then advances that marker in the exported database. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}file}} can then be a folder, where a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sync\sphinxhyphen{}<machine>\sphinxhyphen{}<date>.db}} file is created (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:synchroniser-deux-machines}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Synchronising two machines}}}}}). A file name already taken is refused: the file in place holds the previous delta, which the other machine may not have merged yet.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sync\sphinxhyphen{}cursor}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}incremental}}: name of the marker read and advanced, in place of the destination folder.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}plan}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type database}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches}}: counts, family by family, what the export would write, without writing a file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}file}} is then optional). The counts are those that the export reports afterwards; live collections that would leave frozen and the “recherche” decks whose source would lose a part are named. With another type, the option is refused.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}plan\sphinxhyphen{}ids <famille>}} — Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}plan}}, but returns a page of the identifiers behind a count: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{comments}} (the positions that carry them), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournaments}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions}} (the tournaments whose Direction leaves with them), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres}} (the events that leave with one of their tournaments), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collections}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lessons}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ankiDecks}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transcriptions}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filters}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}offset}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}} choose the page (1000 identifiers at most).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type database}} exports the whole library, like the server export and like the export window when the displayed list is the library: positions, matches, tournaments (with their Direction: journal, pairs, tables and the filing of the exported matches; their event leaves as soon as one of its tournaments does), collections, lessons, Anki decks, transcriptions, aliases and filters. An option set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} removes its family (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collections=false}}); a list of IDs restricts it to those items and includes it. A transcription draft leaves with the match it produced; a draft that has not yet produced a match leaves only if every match does. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type matches}} also carries each match’s draft.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }database\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }sauvegarde.db
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }positions\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }positions.txt
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }matches\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }selection.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYGZhy{}ids\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1},3,5

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} .mat : un match, puis plusieurs (ou tous) dans un répertoire}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }mat\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYGZhy{}ids\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }match5.mat
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }mat\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYGZhy{}ids\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{5},9,12\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }sorties/
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }mat\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }sorties/

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Ce qui est nouveau depuis le dernier export vers ce dossier, pour une}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} autre machine qui le surveille}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }database\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}incremental\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZti{}/Sync/vers\PYGZhy{}portable/

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} .dbx : filigrané et protégé par mot de passe}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }cours.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }database\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }cours\PYGZhy{}diffusion.dbx\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}watermark\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Cours de Jean Dupont — 12 mars 2026\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}watermark\PYGZhy{}note\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Merci de ne pas rediffuser.\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}password\PYG{+w}{ }secret
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A watermark is signed with the local issuer identity (see the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{identity}} command below): it cannot be forged, but it can be removed — the file remains an ordinary SQLite database. It protects nothing; it only states where the file came from. A password protects the file’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{transport} (the stray copy, the attachment sent by mistake), not the database itself: whoever has the password can open it. blunderDB never records anything on the recipient’s side (no registry, no log) — see \sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0007-watermarks-mark-origin-and-nothing-else.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0007}.


\subsubsection{transfer — Copy from one library to another}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:transfer-copier-d-une-bibliotheque-a-une-autre}}\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:cli-transfer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Copies part of a library into another, with no intermediate file to handle. The selection is that of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type database}}; the merge is that of importing a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} database: a position the destination already holds is not added a second time (it is recognised by its hash), its analyses and comments are merged, and a match, collection, lesson or Anki deck already present is not duplicated. Copying from A to B then from B to A therefore creates no duplicate.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transfer\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}source.db\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}to\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}destination.db\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}from}} — Source library (required; it must exist and use the schema of this version of blunderDB). An older library is refused, because upgrading it would mean writing to it: open it once in blunderDB. A newer library is refused too: update blunderDB.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}to}} — Destination library (required; created if it does not exist). It cannot be the source.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analysis}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}comments}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}played\sphinxhyphen{}moves}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}matches}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}transcriptions}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}aliases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collections}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournaments}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}decks}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lessons}} — As for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export}}: an option set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} removes its family (default: yes for all).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection\sphinxhyphen{}ids}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}ids}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament\sphinxhyphen{}ids}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck\sphinxhyphen{}ids}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lesson\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — A list of IDs from the source restricts its family to those items and includes it. An ID that the source does not contain is an error, and nothing is copied.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} (default) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (what was read from the source and what the destination took from it).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Which positions are sent.} Without a list of IDs, all positions of the source are sent, filed or not. As soon as a list of IDs is given, only the positions reached by the retained families are sent (the members of a collection, the moves of a match, the steps of a lesson, the cards of a deck), with their analyses and comments. A collection always goes with its members. A match named by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} carries the record of its tournament (name, date, venue), but not the other matches of that tournament; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournaments=false}}, it arrives without a tournament.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nothing is written that says where the copy comes from: no watermark, no import log, no metadata from the source; the destination keeps its own, and the source receives nothing. The filter library and the review history of Anki decks are not copied: a deck arrives without history, and a deck of the same name already present keeps its own.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Toute une bibliothèque dans une autre}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transfer\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{+w}{ }club.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}to\PYG{+w}{ }perso.db

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Deux collections et leurs positions, rien d\PYGZsq{}autre}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transfer\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{+w}{ }club.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}to\PYG{+w}{ }perso.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}collection\PYGZhy{}ids\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3},7\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}matches\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}tournaments\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}lessons\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}decks\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{false}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Un match, ses positions et son tournoi, en retour}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transfer\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{+w}{ }perso.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}to\PYG{+w}{ }club.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYGZhy{}ids\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}collections\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}lessons\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{false}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}decks\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{false}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The server offers the same transfer between two tenants, pulled by the receiving tenant (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:mode-headless-transfert}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Pulling a copy from a read tenant}}}}}).


\subsubsection{identity — Issuer identity}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:identity-identite-d-emetteur}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shows or moves your \sphinxstylestrong{issuer identity}: the Ed25519 key that signs every watermark. It is created on its own the first time a watermark is applied; there is nothing to configure. It belongs to a person, not to a database: everything you mark carries a single public fingerprint.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }identity
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }identity\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Jean Dupont\PYGZdq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }identity\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}export\PYG{+w}{ }jean.bdbid\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}passphrase\PYG{+w}{ }pw
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }identity\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}import\PYG{+w}{ }jean.bdbid\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}passphrase\PYG{+w}{ }pw
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}name}} — Changes the identity’s display name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}export}} — Exports the identity to a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.bdbid}} file.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}import}} — Imports an identity from a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.bdbid}} file.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}passphrase}} — Optional passphrase protecting the exported/imported file (the local identity itself is deliberately left unprotected).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} (default) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (name, fingerprint, storage path).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The exported file lets anyone holding it sign in your name — do not share it. Renaming changes a label and nothing else: files already marked keep the name they were sealed under, and still verify.


\subsubsection{open — Opening a protected file}
\label{\detokenize{cli_import_export:open-ouvrir-un-fichier-protege}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Turns a password\sphinxhyphen{}protected file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dbx}}) into an ordinary database. The password is asked once; after that it is a normal file.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }open\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }cours.dbx\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}password\PYG{+w}{ }secret
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }open\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }cours.dbx\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}password\PYG{+w}{ }secret\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{+w}{ }./mon\PYGZhy{}cours.db
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} — The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dbx}} file to open (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}password}} — The container’s password (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}file}} — Output path for the ordinary database (default: same name, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} extension).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
What the password protects: the file’s \sphinxstyleemphasis{transport} — the copy left in a downloads folder, the attachment sent by mistake. Not the database: whoever has the password can open it. The container’s header is in the clear, so \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb info}} reads the origin of a protected file without its password.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Library: search, lists, collections}
\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:bibliotheque-recherche-listes-collections}}\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:cli-bibliotheque-chapitre}}\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque::doc}}

\subsubsection{search — Search positions}
\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:search-rechercher-des-positions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Search positions in the database using combinable criteria.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Main options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} — Database (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xgid}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}} — Maximum number of results (0 = unlimited).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}offset}} — Skip the first n results before starting to count; together with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}}, this is pagination.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}export}} — Export results to a new database.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query\sphinxhyphen{}help}} — Shows the list of tokens \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query}} understands, and stops there. No database is opened: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} is unnecessary.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Available filters:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}decision}} — Decision type: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{checker}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cube}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dice}} — Dice roll. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5,3}} matches positions where both dice match (any order). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5}} matches positions where a 5 appears on either die (the second die value is ignored). Implies \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}decision checker}} when no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}decision}} value is given.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pip\sphinxhyphen{}min}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pip\sphinxhyphen{}max}} — Pip count difference range.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}winrate\sphinxhyphen{}min}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}winrate\sphinxhyphen{}max}} — Win rate range (\%).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}cube}} — Cube value.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}score1}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}score2}} — Player scores.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}length}} — Match length.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}error\sphinxhyphen{}min}} — Threshold on what \sphinxstylestrong{a mistake in the position costs}: the gap between the best move and the second\sphinxhyphen{}best one, or the largest of the three cube errors. In \sphinxstylestrong{equity points} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}error\sphinxhyphen{}min 0.1}} keeps positions where a mistake costs at least a tenth of a point. It says nothing about what was actually played there.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}move\sphinxhyphen{}error\sphinxhyphen{}min}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}move\sphinxhyphen{}error\sphinxhyphen{}max}} — Threshold on the error of the move \sphinxstylestrong{actually played} by player 1. In \sphinxstylestrong{thousandths of equity} (millipoints): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}move\sphinxhyphen{}error\sphinxhyphen{}min 50}}, i.e. a twentieth of a point. This is the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{E}} token of the search grammar, written as is.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}has\sphinxhyphen{}analysis}} — Only positions with analysis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}off1\sphinxhyphen{}min}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}off2\sphinxhyphen{}min}} — Minimum checkers off (player 1/2).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — Filter by match IDs (comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — Filter by tournament IDs (comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}position\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — Filter by position IDs: range \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2,7}} (positions 2 to 7) or explicit semicolon\sphinxhyphen{}separated list \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5;10;15}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}individual}} — Only positions imported on their own, that is, the ones you added yourself and not the ones a match import brought in.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}flagged}} — Only the positions flagged for study in the originating software (eXtreme Gammon flags). Not retroactive: matches already imported must be imported again to yield their flags.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}has\sphinxhyphen{}comment}} — Only the positions carrying a comment. The origin makes no difference: a note typed by hand and a comment brought in by a match import both count. Match or tournament comments are not consulted.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}no\sphinxhyphen{}comment}} — Only the positions without a comment. Mutually exclusive with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}has\sphinxhyphen{}comment}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}comment\sphinxhyphen{}origin <o1,o2>}} — Only positions carrying a comment from these origins: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{user}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xg}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gnubg}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bgf}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unknown}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{co:}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}comment\sphinxhyphen{}author <name>}} — Only positions carrying a comment attributed to this name (full name, case ignored).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}phase <p1,p2>}} — Only positions in these game phases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opening}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{middlegame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{race}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bearoff}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ph:}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}game\sphinxhyphen{}type <t1,t2>}} — Only positions of these game plans: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{race}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bearin}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{crunch}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{backgame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{acepoint}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blitz}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{primevprime}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mutualholding}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{holding}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{contact}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gt:}}). Phase and plan are labels derived from the board, which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb repair}} recomputes; an unknown value makes the command fail.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Corpus filters apply to the match where the position was encountered; each one is equivalent to a token of the query language ({\hyperref[\detokenize{cmd_mode:cmd-filter}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Search Filters}}}}}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}player <nom>}} — Matches in which this player played, on either side; case is ignored and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}} stands for any sequence of characters (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pl"…"}}). With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}seat\sphinxhyphen{}only}}, only the decisions made by this player (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pl!"…"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}opponent <nom>}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}player}}, matches against this opponent; alone, a name on either side (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op"…"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament\sphinxhyphen{}name <nom>}} — Matches from tournaments of this name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tn"…"}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}round <r1,r2>}} — Matches from these rounds (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rd:}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}lengths <expr>}} — The match length: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{5,9}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{>5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<9}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ml}}). Not to be confused with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}length}}, which goes with the position’s score.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}away <expr>}} — The points the player still needs, whatever the match length: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2,5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{>3}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<5}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aw}}). Crawford and post\sphinxhyphen{}Crawford count as 1; money play never matches.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}opponent\sphinxhyphen{}away <expr>}} — The points the opponent still needs, in the same forms (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AW}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}crawford <state>}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{game}}: the Crawford game (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cr}}); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{post}}: the games after it (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pcr}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}margin <expr>}} — The margin, in millipoints, between the best choice and the next one in the stored analysis: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<20}} (close decision), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{>100}} (obvious), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{20,60}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mg}}). A position without analysis or with a single candidate never matches.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}date <expr>}} — The match date: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2024}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2024\sphinxhyphen{}01..2024\sphinxhyphen{}12}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{>2024\sphinxhyphen{}06}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<2024\sphinxhyphen{}06}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{md}}); this is not the analysis date.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pr <expr>}} — The PR of the match for the player who made the decision: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{>8}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<5}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4,9}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analysis <v1,v2>}} — Engines and depths of the recorded analysis: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xg}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gnubg}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bgblitz}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hedgehog}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3ply}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3ply+}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{book}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ad:}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}cube\sphinxhyphen{}response <type>}} — A single type of cube decision: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}} (Double / No Double) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{takepass}} (Take / Pass).

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}error\sphinxhyphen{}min}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}move\sphinxhyphen{}error\sphinxhyphen{}min}} do not measure the same thing and \sphinxstylestrong{do not take the same unit}: the factor is a thousand. The first is given in equity points (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0.1}}), the other two in thousandths (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{100}}) — one point is worth 1000 thousandths. It is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}move\sphinxhyphen{}error\sphinxhyphen{}min}} that answers “where did I go wrong”; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}error\sphinxhyphen{}min}} answers “which positions were tricky”.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What search prints:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format table}} (the default) gives one row per position: the identifier, the score, the cube value, the decision type, the dice, the best decision and its equity; these last two columns stay empty for a position without analysis. Then come \sphinxstylestrong{Error}, the equity lost by the decision played, on the position’s scale (points in money play, normalised equity at a match score): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{no analysis}} without analysis, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}}} when the decision played is not among those analysed; \sphinxstylestrong{Date}, the day of the oldest match that reaches the position, otherwise the day it entered the database; \sphinxstylestrong{Collections}, the collections that contain it; \sphinxstylestrong{Decks}, the study decks (Anki) that hold a card of the position.
