\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}} gives an array of the same positions. The fields are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xgid}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{score}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cube}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decision\_type}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{checker}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cube}}) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dice}}, always present; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{best\_move}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{equity}} appear only if the position carries an analysis that fills them in. The list fields follow: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{analysed}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{played\_error}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null}} without analysis, or when the decision played is not among those analysed), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collections}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decks}} (the names, an empty list if none). The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Found n position(s)}} line goes to the error output: standard output carries only the JSON.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{[}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}id\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5266}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}score\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{],}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}cube\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}decision\PYGZus{}type\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}checker\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}dice\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{],}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}best\PYGZus{}move\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}10/3\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}equity\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.565}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}analysed\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kc}{true}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}played\PYGZus{}error\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.042}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}date\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}2023\PYGZhy{}11\PYGZhy{}26\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}collections\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Ouvertures\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{],}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}decks\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[]}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format xgid}} prints one XGID per line, prefixed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{XGID=}}, and \sphinxstylestrong{nothing else} on standard output. The XGID recorded with the analysis is preferred, because it carries the match length of the source; failing that, it is regenerated from the board. The same XGID appears in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xgid}} field of the JSON.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The query language:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The flags above cover only some of the filters. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query}} gives access to the application’s query language — the one used by the command bar — and therefore to every filter that is not drawn on the board: move pattern, comment text, date added, equity, excluded dice, zones and blots.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The grammar is written in only one place, {\hyperref[\detokenize{cmd_mode:cmd-filter}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Search Filters}}}}}. Its table gives every token, its form, and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{search}} flag it corresponds to when one exists. This page does not repeat it.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}query\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}s p\PYGZgt{}30 E\PYGZgt{}50\PYGZsq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}query\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}s m\PYGZdq{}13/11\PYGZdq{} t\PYGZdq{}blunder\PYGZdq{} pl\PYGZdq{}Alice\PYGZdq{} T\PYGZgt{}2026/01/01\PYGZsq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ranking a position’s neighbours goes through the same grammar: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query 's like42'}}, alone or followed by other tokens to narrow the ranked set.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query\sphinxhyphen{}help}} recalls the list without opening a database:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} ./blunderdb search \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}query\PYGZhy{}help
blunderdb search \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}query — the interface\PYGZsq{}s query language

A query is the same text the application\PYGZsq{}s command bar takes:
  s cube p\PYGZgt{}30 E\PYGZgt{}50        cube decisions, 30+ pips behind, 50+ millipoints of error
  s m\PYGZdq{}13/11\PYGZdq{} T\PYGZgt{}2026/01/01 played 13/11, imported this year

Flags (no value):
  cube score   match the cube / the score of the position on the board
  d            match the decision type (checker or cube)
  …

Ranges — each takes x\PYGZgt{}n, x\PYGZlt{}n or xa,b (lower\PYGZhy{}case: you; upper\PYGZhy{}case: the opponent):
  p P          pip count difference / absolute pip count
  …
  E            error of the played move, in millipoints
  T            creation date, T\PYGZgt{}2026/01/01

Values:
  t\PYGZdq{}tag\PYGZdq{}       comment text (\PYGZdq{};\PYGZdq{} separates alternatives)
  …
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query}} replaces the filter flags rather than adding to them: combining them is refused, naming the offending flag. The flags that say \sphinxstyleemphasis{where} to search and \sphinxstyleemphasis{how} to display — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}offset}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}export}} — remain valid.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A token nothing recognises fails the command rather than narrowing the search in silence. Two limits follow from having no board on the command line: the checker pattern cannot be typed, and the five tokens that read the board — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cube}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{score}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{d}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} — compare here against an empty board. A search that needs one of them is written \sphinxstylestrong{entirely} in flags, since \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query}} does not combine with them — for example, cube decisions at least 30 pips behind and wrong by at least 50 millipoints:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}decision\PYG{+w}{ }cube\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}pip\PYGZhy{}min\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}move\PYGZhy{}error\PYGZhy{}min\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}decision\PYG{+w}{ }cube
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}individual
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}error\PYGZhy{}min\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{0}.1
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}tournament\PYGZhy{}ids\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}export\PYG{+w}{ }cubes.db

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 6\PYGZhy{}5 dans les deux ordres, puis un 6 sur l\PYGZsq{}un des deux dés}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dice\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6},5
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dice\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{6}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Pagination}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }json\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}limit\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}offset\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{list — List contents}
\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:list-lister-le-contenu}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Display database contents.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}type\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}limit\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}n\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}offset\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}n\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Types:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches}} — Lists the imported matches, with their result: final score and winner, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unfinished}} when no player reached the match length.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournaments}} — List of tournaments: name, date, venue, origin when known and number of matches.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions}} — Lists the positions (10 by default; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}offset <n>}} skips the first \sphinxstyleemphasis{n}). Each position carries the error of the decision played (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{no analysis}}), its date and its collections and its study decks (a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Decks:}} line, absent when there are none), like the output of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{search}}. Only the window shown is read, whatever the size of the database. With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format csv}} it becomes a \sphinxstylestrong{tabular export}: one row per position, with its XGID, phase, score, cube, pips and the derived analysis columns.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports}} — The recorded imports, most recent first: id, date, format, source, matches imported / skipped / enriched, unreadable files and new positions. With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch <id>}}, shows the \sphinxstylestrong{full report} of one import: flagged positions, positions with no analysis, the PR over that batch and its five worst decisions (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:compte-rendu-import}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{The import report}}}}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats}} — Performance statistics report: PR / Snowie ER / MWC (overall, checker, cube), rolling PR over the last N decisions, top blunders, breakdown by cube action and error magnitude histogram.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players}} — Comparison table, \sphinxstylestrong{one row per player} in the database: matches, wins/losses, counted decisions, overall / checker / cube PR, Snowie ER, errors, blunders and luck. This is the command\sphinxhyphen{}line counterpart of the Stats panel’s Players tab.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{moves}} — \sphinxstylestrong{Tabular export} of the recorded moves, one per row, with the match they belong to repeated on every row: identifiers, date, players, length, move number and type, position, dice, played move, cube action, luck. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format csv}} required.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{analyses}} — \sphinxstylestrong{Tabular export} of the stored analyses, one per row: engine, depth, best move and its equity, played move’s error, best cube action and its error, the six win rates. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format csv}} required.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tags}} — The database’s tag vocabulary: every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#word}} written in a comment, with the number of \sphinxstylestrong{positions} carrying it, most used first. On a database with no tag at all, shows the recommended vocabulary rather than an empty list (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_bibliotheque:tags}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Tags}}}}}). Accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format csv}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{study}} — By game plan, the distinct positions reviewed in the Anki decks over the last \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}days}} days (default: 30) and the PR of the matches played before and since, each with its number of decisions; a PR based on fewer than ten decisions is shown as “—”. Three numbers side by side, not an effect: nothing accounts for opponents, format or dice. Accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format csv}}.

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Tabular exports}
\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:exports-tabulaires}}\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:export-tabulaire}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Three types — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{moves}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{analyses}} — export to CSV for a notebook, a spreadsheet or a script:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }positions\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }csv\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }positions.csv
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }moves\PYG{+w}{     }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }csv\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }moves.csv
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }analyses\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }csv\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }analyses.csv
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}} applies \sphinxstylestrong{only if you pass it}. Its default (10) exists so that a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}} printed to a terminal does not scroll the whole database past you; an export goes to a file read by a program, and silently truncating it at ten rows would be a trap nobody notices until the figures are wrong.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The columns are a contract.} A notebook or a script written against these names must keep working: columns are added at the end, never renamed and never reordered. Every equity is in \sphinxstylestrong{integer millipoints}, because that is how they are stored and because a float in a CSV invites a locale to reformat it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Parquet is not offered}, and that is measured rather than dogmatic: a columnar library weighs several megabytes in a binary whose size is a tracked concern, while everything this export is for reads CSV in one line (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pd.read\_csv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{polars.read\_csv}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{read.csv}}, a spreadsheet). Parquet earns its keep on tens of millions of rows; a ten\sphinxhyphen{}year\sphinxhyphen{}old backgammon library holds a hundred thousand. If one day the difference is measurable on a real database, that measurement is what should reopen this.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxstylestrong{example Jupyter notebook} comes with these exports (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notebooks/blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}analyse.ipynb}} in the repository): PR over time, the distribution of error magnitudes, the ten worst decisions with their XGID. It uses nothing but those three CSV files, and it is \sphinxstylestrong{executed every night in continuous integration} — a notebook nobody runs is a notebook that has stopped working without anybody noticing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats}} type only):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}metric}} — Displayed metric: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mwc}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}player}} — Restrict to the given player.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament}} — Restrict to one or more tournament IDs (comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}from}} — Start date (YYYY\sphinxhyphen{}MM\sphinxhyphen{}DD).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}to}} — End date (YYYY\sphinxhyphen{}MM\sphinxhyphen{}DD).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}decision\sphinxhyphen{}type}} — Decision type: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{all}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{checker}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cube}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{all}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}top\sphinxhyphen{}blunders}} — Number of worst errors listed (default: 10).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}engine}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}min\sphinxhyphen{}depth}} — Only counts decisions analysed by this engine (exact name, as recorded) or at this depth at least (in plies); also accepted by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players}} type.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options} (type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches}} only):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query}} — Keeps only the matches where a player, the event, the venue, the round, the tournament or the date contains this text (case\sphinxhyphen{}insensitive).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} — Keep only these match identifiers, separated by commas (those printed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats matches}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sort}} — Order: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date}} (default, most recent first), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date\_asc}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length\_asc}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{length\_desc}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{player1}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{player1\_desc}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{player2}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{player2\_desc}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournament}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournament\_desc}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opponent}}, or by PR: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr1}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr1\_desc}} (player 1), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr2}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr2\_desc}} (player 2), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr\_main}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr\_main\_desc}} (the main player, whichever seat he played, aliases included) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr\_opponent}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr\_opponent\_desc}} (his opponent). A match without that PR — no counted decision, or a match the main player did not play — comes last in both directions.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Filtering and sorting are done by the database, as in the Matches panel; the reported total is that of the retained matches. The server offers them on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/matches.list}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sort}} fields) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/matches.count}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports}} type only):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}} — A batch id: shows its full report instead of the list.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}queue}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}}: the batch’s \sphinxstylestrong{study queue} rather than its report — the positions worth a second look, in the order to walk them (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:file-etude}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{The study queue}}}}}). The decisions that cost something first, then the positions flagged in the source tool, then the close cube decisions; a position appears only once.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The measured half of the report is recomputed on every call: a batch whose positions have since been analysed returns today’s figures, not those of the day it was imported.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players}} type only):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}from}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}to}} — Date bounds (YYYY\sphinxhyphen{}MM\sphinxhyphen{}DD), for instance the days of a competition.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament}} — Restrict to one or more tournament IDs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csv}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}player}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}decision\sphinxhyphen{}type}} do \sphinxstylestrong{not} apply to this type: the table covers every player and already splits checker and cube into separate columns.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A dash “—” (an empty field in CSV) marks a value that was \sphinxstylestrong{never measured}, not to be confused with zero. That is the case for luck on any match imported before schema version 2.15.0, as well as for the formats that do not carry it (BGF, Jellyfish \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}}): re\sphinxhyphen{}import the source files to obtain it. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{luck\_rolls}} column says how many rolls the average covers.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each type prints one block per item, preceded by the total found. The final line says which window is shown, truncated by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}} (whose default value is 10 for positions) and shifted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}offset}}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Found 3859 position(s):

ID: 1
  Score: 7\PYGZhy{}7
  Player on roll: 0
  Decision: Checker play

ID: 2
  Score: 7\PYGZhy{}7
  Player on roll: 0
  Decision: Cube action

…

(Showing 1\PYGZhy{}10 of 3859 positions, use \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}offset and \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}limit to see more)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Les imports enregistrés, puis le compte rendu de l\PYGZsq{}un d\PYGZsq{}eux}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }imports
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }imports\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}batch\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}

./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }stats
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }stats\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}metric\PYG{+w}{ }mwc\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}player\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Alice\PYGZdq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }stats\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}decision\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }checker\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2026}\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}01
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }stats\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }json

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Un tableau par joueur, borné aux dates d\PYGZsq{}une compétition}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }players\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2026}\PYGZhy{}03\PYGZhy{}01\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}to\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2026}\PYGZhy{}03\PYGZhy{}08

./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }matches

\subsubsection{collection — Manage collections}
\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:collection-gerer-les-collections}}\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:cli-collection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Manages collections, those sets of positions picked by hand in the GUI’s Collections panel. Each subcommand takes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show}} accept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text}} (default), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{csv}}, like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }collection\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}subcommand\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Subcommands:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}} — List of collections: id, name, number of positions, description.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id>}} — Positions of a collection: id, index (the 1\sphinxhyphen{}based number shown in the GUI’s status bar), score, decision type and XGID.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{create \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}name <name> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}description <text>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query <query>{]}}} — Creates an empty collection or, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query}}, a living collection from the start. A query containing a token that no rule recognises is refused before anything is written.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query <query>}} — Makes a collection \sphinxstylestrong{living}: its content becomes the result of a search, re\sphinxhyphen{}evaluated every time it is opened. The query is written in the application’s own search grammar (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{cmd_mode:cmd-filter}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Search Filters}}}}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}clear}} turns it back into a hand\sphinxhyphen{}made list, keeping the positions it already held.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{freeze \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id>}} — Freezes a living collection: the positions its query selects now become its content, and the query is cleared. Refused on a collection that is not living.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{evaluate \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit <n>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — Reads the position identifiers of a collection, replaying the query of a living collection now. The response is bounded by a declared ceiling of 5,000 positions (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}} lowers it) and always gives the actual number of positions and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truncated}} flag: never a silent truncation. In text mode, the identifiers go to standard output and the count to standard error.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pile {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}position\sphinxhyphen{}id <id> | \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}xgid <XGID>{]}}} — Puts a position on the Pile (the “come back to this” collection), or takes it off when it is there; a position given by XGID that is not in the database is first written to it, as a position brought in on its own. Without a position, prints the Pile.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rename \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}name <name> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}description <text>{]}}} — Renames a collection (the description is kept if not given).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delete \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}confirm{]}}} — Deletes a collection; its positions remain in the database.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id{[},id…{]}> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}out <file.db> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analysis=false{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}comments=false{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}matches=false{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}transcriptions=false{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}aliases=false{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watermark <text>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watermark\sphinxhyphen{}note <text>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}password <password>{]}}} — Exports one or more collections to a new database file, through the same exporter as the graphical interface’s export window and as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type database}}: the file also carries the matches in which the positions were played, with their transcriptions and the aliases of their players and events (see the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export}} command for the watermark and the password).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{suggest {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}player <nom>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match <ids>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament <ids>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}from <date>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}to <date>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}decision\sphinxhyphen{}type all|checker|cube{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}size <n>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection <nom>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck <nom>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — Suggests \sphinxstylestrong{reference positions} among the errors of the filter: those whose lesson covers the most recoverable MWC of their neighbouring errors, with no near\sphinxhyphen{}duplicate and no position already handled (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_bibliotheque:positions-reference}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{positions de référence}}}}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}size}} defaults to 20, 50 at most. Nothing is written without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection}}, which files the suggested positions in a new collection, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck}}, which turns them into an Anki deck. Each line gives the family, the score of a cube reference, the errors and matches it summarises, the MWC covered and its reason (which gives the figure counted when the lesson counts for half); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}} returns the same components.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The XGID shown by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show}} is the one saved with the position’s analysis when it exists (BGF and XGP imports); otherwise it is generated from the board exactly as \sphinxstyleemphasis{Copy position} does in the GUI — the match length is then the larger of the two remaining scores, since a saved position does not retain the real one.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }collection\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Found 2 collection(s):}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ID  Name              Positions  Description}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}  \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}              \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}  \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1   Ouvertures blitz  0          À revoir}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 2   Videaux ratés     0}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A database with no collection answers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{No collections found in database}} and still exits with code 0.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }collection\PYG{+w}{ }show\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }csv

./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }collection\PYG{+w}{ }create\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Ouvertures blitz\PYGZdq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }collection\PYG{+w}{ }rename\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Ouvertures\PYGZdq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }collection\PYG{+w}{ }delete\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}confirm

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Exporter deux collections, marquées de leur origine}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }collection\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3},4\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}out\PYG{+w}{ }ouvertures.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}watermark\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Cours de Jean Dupont \PYGZhy{} 12 mars 2026\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Dix positions de référence d\PYGZsq{}Alice sur un tournoi, gardées en collection}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }collection\PYG{+w}{ }suggest\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}player\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Alice\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}tournament\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}size\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}collection\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Références : open de mars\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{comment — The comments of a position}
\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:comment-les-commentaires-d-une-position}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A position carries as many comments as you like, each attributed to its author (free text). A comment received in a watermarked export also carries its issuer’s signature: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}} shows it in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Signed by} column — name, fingerprint, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(unverified)}} if it no longer matches what was signed —, and the provenance in the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Origin} column (empty for a comment written in blunderDB).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }comment\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}sous\PYGZhy{}commande\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}chemin\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Subcommands:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}position N \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}text T {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}author A{]}}} — Adds a comment to position N, attributed to A (without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}author}}, it has no author).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}position N{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}author A{]}}} — Lists the comments of a position, or of the whole database, optionally those of a single author.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Common options:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} (required); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}} accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }comment\PYG{+w}{ }add\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}position\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{412}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}text\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Videau trop tôt\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}author\PYG{+w}{ }Alice
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }comment\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}position\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{412}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }comment\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}author\PYG{+w}{ }Alice\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }json
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{elsewhere — Elsewhere: a position in other databases}
\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:elsewhere-ailleurs-une-position-dans-d-autres-bases}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Looks up a position, by its Zobrist hash, in other database files passed to the same command, and returns for each what it knows about it: its analysis, its comments, the matches where the position was played (players, length, date, move played and its cost), and its closest positions (same ranking as the search \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{like}} token, in rolls).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The cost of a move played elsewhere is judged with the error and blunder thresholds of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} database, never with those of the database read: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{error}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunder}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{good}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unscored}} without analysis. An analysis made at a match score with a match equity table other than the current table of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} is flagged; its match costs are shown but not judged (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{other\sphinxhyphen{}met}}), as everywhere else in blunderDB. The other files are opened read\sphinxhyphen{}only: nothing is written to them, and a database in a read\sphinxhyphen{}only folder (network share, USB key, mount) is read as it stands, without creating a file beside it. A file that cannot be read (missing, of an earlier or later version, not a blunderDB database) is reported on a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Not read:}} line under its name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{error}} field in JSON) and skipped: the other files answer, and the command exits with a non\sphinxhyphen{}zero code only if none could be read. A file of an earlier version is refused (opening it once in blunderDB upgrades it), and so is a file of a later version (update blunderDB). Past 50 matches where the position was played, only the 50 latest imported are read: the output says so, with the total (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matchesTotal}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{playsTruncated}} in JSON).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }elsewhere\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}chemin\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}other\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}fichier\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}other\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}fichier\PYGZgt{}...\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}position\PYG{+w}{ }N\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}xgid\PYG{+w}{ }X\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}zobrist\PYG{+w}{ }H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYG{+w}{ }N\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}tournament\PYG{+w}{ }N\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}collection\PYG{+w}{ }N\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}lesson\PYG{+w}{ }N\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} (required) — The database that judges: its thresholds and its equity table.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}other}} (required, repeatable) — A database file to search.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}position N}} — The position, by its identifier in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}xgid X}} — The position, by its XGID.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zobrist H}} — The position, by its hash (decimal); its neighbours are then searched only in the databases that hold it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match N}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament N}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection N}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lesson N}} — Instead of a position, a match, a tournament, a collection or a lesson of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}}: the command says whether each other base holds it, under the key where a copy would merge it (the match’s fingerprint, even imported from another format; the name otherwise), with its identifier there and what it holds (games, matches, positions or steps).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}neighbours N}} — Number of neighbours per database (default: 5, 0: none, at most 50).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}max\sphinxhyphen{}distance D}} — Discards neighbours more than D rolls away (0: two rolls, the most that is served; beyond that, refused).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} (default) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The daemon serves the same lookups across tenants: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.positionElsewhere}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.objectElsewhere}} (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Headless mode (server)}}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }elsewhere\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }moi.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}other\PYG{+w}{ }club.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}position\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{412}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }elsewhere\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }moi.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}other\PYG{+w}{ }club.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}tournament\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }elsewhere\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }moi.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}other\PYG{+w}{ }a.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}other\PYG{+w}{ }b.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}xgid\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}XGID=\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}E\PYGZhy{}C\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}eE\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}c\PYGZhy{}e\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}B\PYGZhy{}:0:0:1:52:0:0:0:0:10\PYGZdq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }elsewhere\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }moi.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}other\PYG{+w}{ }club.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}zobrist\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1234567890}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }json
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{trash — The trash}
\label{\detokenize{cli_bibliotheque:trash-la-corbeille}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
What was deleted, and what it takes to put it back. A delete is still a delete: a JSON snapshot of what disappears is written first, and nothing else in the database knows that table exists — no search filter, no statistic, no retention rule.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }trash\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}sous\PYGZhy{}commande\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}chemin\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Subcommands:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}} — What is in the trash, most recently deleted first.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{restore \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N}} — Puts entry N back and removes it from the trash.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discard \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N}} — Drops entry N now, without restoring it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{empty {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}older\sphinxhyphen{}than D{]}}} — Empties the trash, or only what is older than D days.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delete \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}kind K \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N}} — Deletes an object \sphinxstylestrong{through the trash}, so the gesture can be undone. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{K}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collection}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{comment}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Common options:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} (required), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}kind}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}} (default 50), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}}). For \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}kind}} narrows the listing to one kind of object: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collection}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{comment}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki\_card}}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb delete}} still deletes with \sphinxstylestrong{no} net: a script that deletes a position expects it gone, and quietly leaving a snapshot behind would grow a file nobody asked to grow. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash delete}} is the one that keeps the undo.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Restoring a position goes back through the Zobrist deduplication: it never creates a duplicate. A restored position takes back its old number; if the same position has been saved in the meantime, that one is kept, and it receives what it lacks. A restored match also takes back its original number, with its games, its moves, its analyses and its positions; it is refused if another match holds that number or if a match with the same file fingerprint has been imported in the meantime. What a successful restore could not put back — a Direction slot taken or gone, a deleted tournament — is reported by a warning.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Anything older than thirty days is dropped by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb vacuum}} — never on opening a database.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Supprimer une position en gardant l\PYGZsq{}annulation}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }trash\PYG{+w}{ }delete\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}kind\PYG{+w}{ }position\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{412}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Voir la corbeille, puis remettre une entrée}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }trash\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }trash\PYG{+w}{ }restore\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Ne garder que ce qui a moins de trente jours}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }trash\PYG{+w}{ }empty\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}older\PYGZhy{}than\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Matches, tournaments and games}
\label{\detokenize{cli_matchs:matchs-tournois-et-parties}}\label{\detokenize{cli_matchs:cli-matchs-chapitre}}\label{\detokenize{cli_matchs::doc}}

\subsubsection{match — Display a match}
\label{\detokenize{cli_matchs:match-afficher-un-match}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shows the positions and analyses of an imported match. In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary}} output, the header repeats what the source file says about the match when it says it: each player’s Elo rating and experience, transcriber, Jacoby and Beaver rules of a money session, program that wrote the file; the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} output carries them in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{match}} object.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When the match kept the duration of its decisions (a match played against a bot, see the Duel), the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} output gives the duration of each decision, the cube decision apart, and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary}} output each player’s total and mean, with the mark of the player whose reserve ran out first, then the number of its decisions per non\sphinxhyphen{}empty duration band (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<2 s: 4, 2\sphinxhyphen{}5 s: 11}}); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/stats.matchTimeSummary}} delivers these bands (the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{histogram}} of each player, bounds in milliseconds in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{histogram\_bounds\_ms}}); the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} output carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decision\_ms}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cube\_decision\_ms}}. An unknown duration is not written. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type timeerrors}} gives, per player and duration band (under 5 s, 5 to 15 s, 15 to 30 s, over 30 s), the number of decisions, the mean error and the share of blunders; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}} delivers the rows. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}ids}} (match IDs, comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated) restricts the table to those matches: the review of a tournament or of a session.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For a match played here by a Duel, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary}} outputs add its origin: the start, the revealed dice seed and its SHA\sphinxhyphen{}256, to compare with the fingerprint published when the Duel was created, how the match ended (played to the end, stopped before the end, or lost on time and by whom), the time control, the player whose reserve ran out first and the Bot (level, gammonNet version). For a match that was not played here, they write \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Origin: not played here}}. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} output carries the origin under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{origin}} (including \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lost\_on\_time}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null}} for a match that was not played here. The server serves it through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/matches.origin}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null}} for a match without origin, 404 for a match that does not exist.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For an analysed match, each play’s loss of match\sphinxhyphen{}winning chances (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mwc\_loss}}, a fraction: 0.0123 is 1.23\%, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null}} for an unrated play) follows the same path: the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} output carries the list under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decision\_losses}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} adds an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MWC loss}} line to rated plays and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary}} gives the total per player, equal to the MWC loss in the match list. Each entry also carries its difficulty (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{difficulty}}, the expected loss of a reference player in the same position, same unit, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null}} for an unrated play) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{avoidable}} for an avoidable error; the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} output adds \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{difficulty\_summary}} (per player: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{difficulty}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{excess}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ratio}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{avoidable}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Difficulty}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Avoidable error}} lines, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary}} a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Difficulty}} section. The server serves it through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/stats.matchDecisionLosses}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} output also carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{win\_trace}}: the first player’s match winning chances before and after each move (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mwc\_before}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mwc\_after}}, as fractions), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{analysed}} for an analysed move, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null}} without analysis, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mwc\_loss}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{error}} to mark errors; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{money}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}} for a money game, none of whose moves has a value. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} adds the line \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MWC (<player 1>): 50.00\% \sphinxhyphen{}> 48.77\%}} to analysed moves ({\hyperref[\detokenize{metriques:metrique-trace-mwc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Match winning chances curve}}}}}). The server serves it through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/stats.matchWinTrace}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary}} ends with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Review}} section, the match summary ({\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_matchs:bilan-match}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{match summary}}}}}): per player, the PR and its 95 \% interval over the games, the MWC loss scaled to 7 points and its interval over the games, the luck\sphinxhyphen{}adjusted result (with the result, the net luck, the error gap and the dice coverage), the three errors to review (game, move, loss and avoidable share) and the split of errors between hasty and deliberate. The server serves it through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/stats.matchReview}}. In \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats}}, the overall PR and the rows by phase, by label and by score carry their 95 \% interval over the matches (column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{95 \% CI}}), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type players}} a column \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L7}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }match\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}id\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}format\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}file\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} — Database (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id}} — Match ID to display (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{summary}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}output}} — Output file (default: stdout).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }match\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }summary
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }match\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }text
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }match\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }match1.json
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{match repair} — Rewrites a match’s positions, analyses and errors from its source file, the one the \sphinxstylestrong{Info} tab of its card names. The match keeps its identifier, its tournament, the player names as stored (aliases, corrections, swap), its date, its comment, its video and its marks, its transcription, and the comments written on its positions: a comment left on a position the repair leaves moves to the one the file names for the same move, unless a collection, an Anki card or a lesson still holds that position; the comment then stays there and the report counts it. An analysis deeper than the file’s (a rollout run since the import) or corrected by hand stays. A match that already matches its file is not rewritten. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dry\sphinxhyphen{}run}} says what would change without writing anything. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}list}} goes through every match that names a source file and gives those that differ from it, with the number of moves whose position changes and the share of analysed moves before and after, as well as those whose file cannot be found; it writes nothing. A relative path is looked for from the database’s folder, then from the current folder. The repair is refused when the file cannot be found, no longer holds the match (its fingerprint is no longer that of the stored match), or when the stored moves do not tell which player of the file is which. The server serves it through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/matches.repair}}, with the source file sent in the request.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }match\PYG{+w}{ }repair\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}chemin\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}ID\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dry\PYGZhy{}run\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}list\PYG{o}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }text\PYG{p}{|}json\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }match\PYG{+w}{ }repair\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{42}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dry\PYGZhy{}run
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }match\PYG{+w}{ }repair\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{42}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{tournament — Read a directed tournament}
\label{\detokenize{cli_matchs:tournament-lire-un-tournoi-dirige}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads a directed tournament without a graphical interface. Directing one interactively is the job of the Nicomaque engine’s own console; these sub\sphinxhyphen{}commands \sphinxstylestrong{read}, none of them waits for input, and only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{move}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{confirm}} write.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}sous\PYGZhy{}commande\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}chemin\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Subcommands:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — The directed tournaments of the database, with their state, the engine version, the event each belongs to (empty if none) and the date of the last decision.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verify \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — Replays the direction and reports any remaining warning. \sphinxstylestrong{Exits in error} if one remains: this is the after\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fact check, and a script that runs it over a season’s databases wants a status code, not a line to filter.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{standings \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N}} — The standings as CSV, prizes included, in the language of the interface.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ranking \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}season {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rencontre N{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}from AAAA\sphinxhyphen{}MM\sphinxhyphen{}JJ{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}to AAAA\sphinxhyphen{}MM\sphinxhyphen{}JJ{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}points 25,18,15{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}participation P{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}elo{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format csv|json{]}}} — The season ranking: the closed tournaments of an event or of a period (bounds included, on the tournament date; with no filter, all the directed tournaments), each place converted into points by the scale (winner first; by default 25, 18, 15, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1), plus \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}participation}} per tournament played. Ties share the average of the places they occupy. A person is recognised from one tournament to the next by name. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}elo}} adds a club Elo replayed over the season’s matches (FIBS formula, starting at 1500). The CSV gives one row per person and one column of points per tournament; a tournament that is not closed is listed but earns nothing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{page \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N|\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rencontre N {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}out <folder>{]}}} — The HTML display page of a competition (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id}}), or an event’s wall page (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rencontre}}: one line per table, whichever competition occupies it). Exactly one of the two is required. Without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}out}} it goes to standard output; with it, the page is written into the folder, which becomes the direction’s own, or the event’s.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N}} — The raw event journal, replayable by the engine’s tools. The journal is the whole truth of a direction: the standings, the brackets and the warnings are replayed from it. A tool reading this output needs no blunderDB at all.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{move \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match M \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}table T {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — Changes the table of a running match, like dragging one cell onto another in the grid. If the target table is taken, the two matches \sphinxstylestrong{swap} tables; an out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}service table is refused. In an event, if the table is taken by another competition, the swap happens between the two competitions: a table change is written in each log. Prints the table of every running match.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hall \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rencontre N {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — All the tables of an event: one line per table, whichever competition occupies it (competition, match, players), then the proposals of every competition in a single queue (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{proposal}}), the players who have waited longest first, and lastly the matches held for want of a table or of a free player (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{held}}, with their reason). This is the grid that the \sphinxstyleemphasis{All tables} view of the Direction displays. Tables are grouped by room when the event has any, and named when they have a name.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{proposals \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — The engine’s numbered queue of proposals: matches, draws, phase change, repechage of a withdrawn pool qualifier.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{confirm \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id N \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}n K {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — Confirms proposal number K of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{proposals}}, like \sphinxstyleemphasis{Launch} in the panel, then shows the queue that follows.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tables \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rencontre N|\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament N {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — The table properties (name, room, reserved, assigned to) and the rooms each competition of an event plays in (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rencontre}}), or the properties of a competition that plays alone (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tournament}}). Read\sphinxhyphen{}only: writing goes through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{call}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.setTables}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.setEventRooms}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.setTables}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Common options:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} (required), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id}} (required except for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ranking}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{page \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rencontre}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{hall}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tables}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }verify\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }standings\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }classement.csv
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }ranking\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}season\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2026}\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}01\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}to\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2026}\PYGZhy{}12\PYGZhy{}31\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}elo\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }saison.csv
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }page\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}out\PYG{+w}{ }/tmp/affichage
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }page\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rencontre\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}out\PYG{+w}{ }/tmp/evenement
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }journal.json
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }move\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYG{+w}{ }m4\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}table\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{7}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }hall\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rencontre\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }tournament\PYG{+w}{ }tables\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rencontre\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}
