\subsubsection{transcribe — Replay a transcription}
\label{\detokenize{cli_matchs:transcribe-rejouer-une-transcription}}\label{\detokenize{cli_matchs:cli-transcribe}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Replays a transcription and reports what the replay finds in it. The source is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} file, a match of the library or a transcription draft — exactly one of the three. A match is read through the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} it would export, so what is replayed is what an export would contain.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transcribe\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}mat\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}fichier\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}check\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}render\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}sortie\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transcribe\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}id\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}check
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transcribe\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}draft\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}id\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}check
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transcribe\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}id\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}edit\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}accept\PYGZhy{}losses\PYG{o}{]}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transcribe\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}draft\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}id\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}finish\PYG{p}{|}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}abandon
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transcribe\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}materialize\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}document.json\PYGZgt{}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transcribe\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}import\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}fichier.mat\PYG{p}{|}document.json\PYGZgt{}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transcribe\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}marks\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}manifeste.jsonl\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}id\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}mat}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} file to replay.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} — Database, for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}draft}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match}} — Id of the library match to replay.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}draft}} — Id of the transcription draft to replay.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}check}} — List the inconsistencies found (the default behaviour).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}render}} — Write the transcription back as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} to this path.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} (default) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}edit}} — Opens a draft on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match}} (or returns the one already open on it).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}accept\sphinxhyphen{}losses}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}edit}} on an imported match: accepts that its analyses and comments may be lost.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}finish}} — Finishes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}draft}}: writes its match, or replaces the one it was opened from, and releases the draft.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}abandon}} — Abandons the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}draft}}: deletes it without a match; a match it was opened from stays as it is.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}yes}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}abandon}} on a draft that never produced a match: confirms that everything typed in it is lost.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}materialize}} — JSON document (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{actions}}, dice included) to write as a match in one go, or not at all.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}import}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} file or JSON transcription document to open a new draft on.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}marks}} — Writes the manifest of the local videos’ marks to this path, one JSON line per timed move (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match}} narrows it to one match).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}check}} names each inconsistency with the number of the action and the game it sits in: an illegal play, two turns in a row for the same player, an impossible cube action, an action past the end of the match, a play whose steps do not use its own dice, a game’s first play rolled as a double, which no opening roll can be, an unrecorded play — the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{???}} cell gnubg writes when it did not keep the play that was made, and which is not a dance, a declared score that does not add up — a game whose score line is not the one the previous games give, replayed at the written score.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An inconsistency is \sphinxstylestrong{reported, never held against the input}: nothing is refused for one, and the exit status stays 0 whatever the replay finds. A non\sphinxhyphen{}zero status signals a real failure — an unreadable file, a database that will not open, an output that cannot be written. A script that wants to act on the findings reads them from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}}, where a broken file and a game containing an illegal play are not confused with one another.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}render}} writes the transcription back out as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}}, which is how the round trip is checked on a real file outside the tests.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}materialize}} writes, without a draft, the match played by an actions document that came from elsewhere. The rules are applied strictly: the first refused action makes the command fail with its rank (from 0) and its reason, and nothing is written. The decision durations of the document (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decision\_ms}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cube\_decision\_ms}}) are carried over onto the moves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}import}} opens a new draft on a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} file or on a JSON transcription document (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{actions}}, and optionally \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{format\_version}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{next\_score}}, the shape a draft is stored in). The file’s inconsistencies are kept and marked, as in any draft: they are corrected before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}finish}} writes the match. A file no replay can read — unreadable JSON, unknown action kind, player, die or point off the board, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} without a game — fails the command and opens no draft.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only three other options write, through the same methods as the Transcription panel: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}edit}} opens a draft on an existing match, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}finish}} finishes it — the match is replaced under the same identifier — and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}abandon}} deletes a draft without a match, and requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}yes}} for a draft that was never finished, which takes everything typed in it along. An imported match carries analyses and comments that a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} does not: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}edit}} reports at most their count and refuses without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}accept\sphinxhyphen{}losses}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}marks}} writes a manifest and does not touch the database: one JSON line per move that carries a mark (an instant of the video), for the matches whose video is a local file only. Each line gives the video’s path, the match, the game and the move number, the player, the dice, the play, the board before and after, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{roll\_tick\_ms}} (the instant of the roll) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tick\_ms}} (the instant of the play); a move without a mark is not listed. A video that is an http(s) URL never enters it: it is counted in the summary at the end of the run. A local file missing from the disk is reported on the error output and its match left out. No image is read or written. The command exists on the command line only: the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{serve}} daemon reads no video file, and the desktop does not expose it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }transcribe\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}mat\PYG{+w}{ }match.mat\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}check

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} match.mat: 7 point match, 4 game(s), 203 action(s)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   Final score: 9\PYGZhy{}2}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Inconsistencies: none}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{duel — Play a Duel}
\label{\detokenize{cli_matchs:duel-jouer-un-duel}}\label{\detokenize{cli_matchs:cli-duel}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Plays a Duel without an interface, one Action per call. Each call is its own process: it resumes the Duel from the database, plays one Action and writes it back. The durations of the moves of a Duel played this way are unknown, never zero.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}start}} (XGID of the Start); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}name1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}name2}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}side1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}side2}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{external}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bot:<level>}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{instant}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{normal}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{thorough}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{external:<configuration>@<engine>}}, an external Side declaring the Bot that plays behind it: the Match’s origin records it as declared, not attested); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}discard\sphinxhyphen{}at\sphinxhyphen{}end}} throws the draft away at the end instead of writing the Match; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}combined\sphinxhyphen{}seed}} rolls no die before each external Side has contributed to the seed. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}away}} gives the score of the first game in points away, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{player1,player2}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}: the Crawford game, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}: one point after it), and replaces that of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}start}}; without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}start}}, the game starts from the initial position at this score. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}reroll}} has the roll carried by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}start}} drawn again; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}after\sphinxhyphen{}cube}} begins after the cube decision of the Start (the player on roll rolls at once, an offered double is taken) — by default the Duel begins before it, and an offered double waits for the opponent’s answer. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}single\sphinxhyphen{}game}} stops the Duel at the end of its first game, written alone as a Match. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}minutes\sphinxhyphen{}per\sphinxhyphen{}point}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}delay}} set the time control: each player’s reserve in minutes per point of the match (Standard 2, Speed 0.4) and the delay per move in seconds (12, 10); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}time\sphinxhyphen{}out}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{continue}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lose\_match}}) what an exhausted reserve does. A Start the rules do not admit (checkers, score beyond the length, both players in the Crawford game, cube) is refused with its reason. With two Bots, the whole match is played in this call (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}side1 bot:instant \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}side2 bot:instant}}); a money session between two Bots is refused, since it would never end, except as a single game.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show}} — The score, what the Duel is waiting for and, for a move, the legal plays. The dice seed is never shown before the end: the fingerprint stands for it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}} — The suspended Duels.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{roll}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{move}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{take}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pass}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resign}} — One Action by the Side the Duel is waiting for (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}side 1|2}} to name it); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}play}} gives the move in notation, in any order; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}level}} (1 to 3) the value of a resignation; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}revision}} refuses the Action if the Duel has moved on.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{contribute}} — An external Side’s contribution to the combined seed (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}side 1|2}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}value}}, 1 to 64 bytes), only once, before the first roll; the last contribution starts the dice. The rolls then come from the HMAC\sphinxhyphen{}SHA256 of the sealed seed over each Side’s contribution preceded by its length, and the Match’s origin carries the contributions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{forfeit}} — The Side \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}side}} (required) forfeits the match: the game in progress goes to the other Side for the points that bring it to the length (in money play, a single game at the cube’s value), and the Match is written as won by it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stop}} — Stops a money session and writes its Match as it stands, the game in progress with no winner. A match in points is refused: it is written only whole (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{forfeit}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discard}}). Stopping is not forfeiting.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{discard}} — Throws the Duel away: nothing is written.

\subsection{Analysis and engine}
\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:analyse-et-moteur}}\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:cli-analyse-chapitre}}\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse::doc}}

\subsubsection{analyze — gammonNet catch\sphinxhyphen{}up}
\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:analyze-rattrapage-gammonnet}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Writes a gammonNet analysis for every position that has none — the catch\sphinxhyphen{}up of a library built before this feature existed (\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0013-evaluations-fill-gaps-an-imported-analysis-is-never-overwritten.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0013}, \sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0015-blunderdb-serve-operates-on-a-library-it-does-not-expose-an-evaluator.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0015}). It is the same operation as the automatic run after an import and the “Positions without analysis” line of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{Maintenance} tab of the graphical interface, and as the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/gammonnet.analyzeMissing}} endpoint of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{serve}} daemon for a tenant — three different forms of the same operation, not three separate logics (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Headless mode (server)}}}}}).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }analyze\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} — Database (required).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}ply}} — Search depth (default: 2, the canonical setting).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}prune\sphinxhyphen{}k}} — Pruning width (default: 12, the canonical setting).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}candidates}} — Number of candidate moves kept per checker\sphinxhyphen{}play decision (default: 10).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}} — Number of positions analyzed in parallel (default: the number of cores of the machine). When fewer positions remain than cores (a short match, the end of the batch), each search spreads over the free cores; the result does not change by a single bit.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match}} — Restrict the sweep to the positions of a single match (0, the default, means the whole library).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare}} — \sphinxstylestrong{Writes nothing}: compares gammonNet with the imported analyses instead of filling gaps (see below).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stale}} — Re\sphinxhyphen{}analyzes the positions whose gammonNet analysis is stale — written by an earlier version of the engine, or at a depth other than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}ply}} — instead of filling gaps. A position that also carries an XG, GNUbg or BGBlitz analysis is never touched.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare}}, stops after this many positions (0 = all).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} (default, with progress) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (a single summary document, printed at the end).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rollout}} — Rolls out the positions chosen by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query}} instead of filling gaps (see below).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query}} — With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rollout}}, the positions to play, in the search query language (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{search \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query\sphinxhyphen{}help}}); empty, all of them.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{A match imported without an analysis thus gets a Performance Rating.} That is the case of a match played online, or of a Jellyfish \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}} file, that nobody ran through XG. blunderDB knew its positions and the moves played, but nothing said what they were worth; once the batch has run, the move actually played is compared with gammonNet’s ranking and the gap feeds the PR and every other indicator. The played move comes from the match’s own move table, written at import whether or not the file carried an analysis — it is never guessed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A database analysed with a version older than this one does not need to be re\sphinxhyphen{}evaluated: {\hyperref[\detokenize{cli_admin:cli-repair}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{repair}}}}} recomputes the columns from what is already stored and gives those matches their PR back.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{One match only} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match}}). With the id \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type matches}} prints, the sweep only walks the positions of that match: same gap rule, same guarantees, narrower scope. A match that has just been imported gets its analyses without the rest of the library being swept, and a match corrected then analysed a second time costs only the positions the correction created, since every other one already carries an analysis. The option combines with neither \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stale}} nor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare}}, which both look at positions that already have an analysis: asking for both is an error, rather than a silently ignored scope.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Parallelism} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}). The positions of a batch are independent — no search informs the next one — so they are spread over \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}} threads, each with its own evaluator. The analyses written are \sphinxstylestrong{identical whatever the value of} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}; only the computation time changes. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs 1}} leaves the machine free for something else. Cancellation is not affected: Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}C stops the batch before any new position, and everything already computed is written.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The hole rule} (\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0013-evaluations-fill-gaps-an-imported-analysis-is-never-overwritten.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0013}). A position that already carries an analysis — XG, GNUbg, BGBlitz, or a previous gammonNet run — is never touched, whichever engine is missing. Only a position with \sphinxstylestrong{no analysis at all} is written. The command can therefore be re\sphinxhyphen{}run at any time without risk, and interrupted cleanly: Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}C cancels without losing anything already written, and the next run resumes exactly where the previous one stopped — no journal is needed, since “the positions without analysis” is recomputed on every launch.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }analyze\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Analyzing 1204 position(s) with gammonNet (2\PYGZhy{}ply, k=12, 16 job(s))...}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   1/1204 (0\PYGZpc{})}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   61/1204 (5\PYGZpc{})}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   ...}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   1204/1204 (100\PYGZpc{})}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Done.}

./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }analyze\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}jobs\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Un seul match, celui qui vient d\PYGZsq{}être importé}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }analyze\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}match\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Batch rollouts} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rollout}}). Each position chosen by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}query}} is played by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{cli_analyse:cli-rollout}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{rollout}}}}}, one after the other on all cores, and the rollout is recorded beside its analysis, never in its place. The value is a preset — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fast}} (216 games truncated at 7) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{standard}} (1296 games truncated at 11) — or free settings: an optional preset, then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{games=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\sphinxhyphen{}games=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truncation=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{jsd=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ply=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{candidates=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed=}}, separated by commas. A position that already carries a rollout with the same settings is skipped: a run interrupted by Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}C resumes where it stopped, the position in progress being dropped entirely. A position analysed only by a rollout is found by the search through it; a position already analysed keeps the columns of its analysis.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }analyze\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rollout\PYG{+w}{ }fast\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}query\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}E\PYGZgt{}80\PYGZsq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }analyze\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rollout\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}standard,ply=1\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}query\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}c\PYGZsq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:analyze-compare}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare}}: \sphinxstylestrong{what is gammonNet worth on your library?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The engine’s accuracy is measured elsewhere against reference corpora and against the exact bear\sphinxhyphen{}off table. Neither of those measurements answers the question a user actually has, which is about \sphinxstylestrong{their} positions: on the matches imported from XG, where does the embedded engine disagree with the analysis that came in the file, and what would that disagreement cost?

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare}} answers, and \sphinxstylestrong{writes nothing}. That is not a precaution but the point of the command: ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0013 protects an imported analysis unconditionally, so the comparison can be run on a library one particularly does not want rewritten.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The report gives:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxstylestrong{agreement rate} on the best answer, split between checker plays and cube decisions — the two have nothing to do with each other and a single rate would hide which one is slipping;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxstylestrong{cost of the disagreement}, priced on the imported analysis’s own scale: what the move gammonNet prefers is worth \sphinxstyleemphasis{according to the imported engine}, minus what its own best move is worth. That direction is the only one both engines can price together; pricing a disagreement twice would invite reading the smaller of the two numbers;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the breakdown \sphinxstylestrong{by game phase}, which is what says \sphinxstyleemphasis{where} the disagreements sit;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the ten most expensive disagreements, position by position.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two engines write the same move differently — XG writes “13/7” where gammonNet writes “13/8 8/7”, hits are marked on one side and not the other, repetition is sometimes collapsed into “(2)”. Those differences are dialect, not disagreement: the comparison reduces both notations to a canonical form before comparing them. Without that, a test corpus showed 78.8 \% agreement instead of 93.2 \% — fifteen points of false disagreements.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A move the imported engine did \sphinxstylestrong{not} list cannot be priced on its scale: it counts as a disagreement of zero cost rather than of an invented one.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Comparer sur un échantillon de 500 positions}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }analyze\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}compare\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}limit\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{500}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} compared: 118 decision(s)  (refused 2, failed 0)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} same best answer: 93.2\PYGZpc{} (110/118)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   checker play:   93.7\PYGZpc{} (59/63)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   cube decision:  92.7\PYGZpc{} (51/55)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ...}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{rollout — Rollout of a position}
\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:rollout-rollout-d-une-position}}\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:cli-rollout}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Plays a position a large number of times with gammonNet, to settle what a search cannot: two moves a few thousandths apart, or a cube decision where the model hesitates. With dice, it is its moves that are played (the best ones at the rollout depth, at least 2 plies, or those named by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}move}}); without dice, its cube decision (No double and Double/Take; Double/Pass is worth exactly +1). The position comes from an XGID or an OGID, or from a database (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id}}); without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}store}}, nothing is recorded.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }rollout\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZlt{}XGID|OGID\PYGZgt{}\PYGZsq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }rollout\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}path\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}position\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}store\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}preset}} — Starting setting: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fast}} (default: 216 games truncated at 7 plies, stop at JSD 3 after 108) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{standard}} (1296 games truncated at 11, stop at JSD 3 after 324). Both play at 0 ply — the network alone, for moves, cube and leaves; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}ply 1}} or more plays deeper, for a time several times longer. The following options override it one by one.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}games}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}min\sphinxhyphen{}games}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}truncation}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jsd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}ply}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}candidates}} — The rollout parameters (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}truncation 0}} plays each game to the end, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jsd 0}} never stops before the end).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}move}} — A move to play, in blunderDB notation (repeatable).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}seed}} — Dice seed, fixed by default: the same command gives the same numbers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}} — Games played in parallel (default: one per core); only the running time changes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id}} — The database and the identifier of the position to play, instead of an XGID.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}store}} — Records the finished rollout on the position, as a second analysis carrying its own settings, beside the imported or evaluated analysis, which it never replaces. An interrupted rollout is not recorded; of two rollouts with the same settings, the longer series is kept, and a rollout with other settings is added alongside.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}list}} — Prints the rollouts stored on the position, newest first, instead of rolling one out.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All candidates play the same dice, the luck of each roll is removed from the result of each game (variance reduction), the first two rolls are stratified, and a game stops where the two\sphinxhyphen{}sided bearoff database covers it. Each line gives the equity, its 95 \% interval, the number of games played and the JSD, the gap to the best in standard deviations of the difference. The cube is played during the games: the ranking is more reliable than the absolute equity. Ctrl\sphinxhyphen{}C displays what the completed games have established.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }rollout\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}XGID=\PYGZhy{}b\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}E\PYGZhy{}C\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}eE\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}c\PYGZhy{}e\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}B\PYGZhy{}:0:0:1:31:0:0:0:0:10\PYGZsq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }rollout\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}move\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}8/5 6/5\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}move\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}24/23 13/10\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZlt{}XGID\PYGZgt{}\PYGZsq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }rollout\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{42}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}preset\PYG{+w}{ }standard\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}store
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }rollout\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{42}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}list
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:epc-calculatrice-epc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes the Effective Pip Count, the winning probability and the money cube verdict of a bearoff position given as an XGID or an OGID (OpenGammon). Pure computation: no database file is involved.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }epc\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZlt{}XGID|OGID\PYGZgt{}\PYGZsq{}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}bearoff\sphinxhyphen{}ts}} — Optional two\sphinxhyphen{}sided bearoff database (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.bd}}) widening the built\sphinxhyphen{}in TS\sphinxhyphen{}06\sphinxhyphen{}06 (also read from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BLUNDERDB\_TS\_PATH}} environment variable). The widest valid database wins; an invalid file is ignored with a warning.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Regimes.} Within the range the two\sphinxhyphen{}sided database covers, the winning probability and the money cube analysis (cubeless, ND, D/T, D/P, verdict) are \sphinxstylestrong{exact}. Outside it, the winning probability is \sphinxstylestrong{estimated} (convolution of the one\sphinxhyphen{}sided roll distributions plus a calibrated correction) and shown with its measured error margin; the cube verdict is deliberately never estimated (see \sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0009-race-win-chances-are-read-or-convolved-cube-verdicts-are-never-estimated.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0009}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Régime exact : six pions ou moins de chaque côté}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }cubematrix\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZlt{}XGID|OGID\PYGZgt{}\PYGZsq{}}

\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}match\sphinxhyphen{}length}} — Match length the grid spans, from 1 to 25 (default: 7).

\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}} output: a grid whose rows are the points still needed by the player on roll and whose columns are the opponent’s, then the legend of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ND}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DT}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DP}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{TG}} tokens and the reason for each refused cell.


\subsubsection{capture — Position from a screenshot}
\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:capture-position-depuis-une-capture-d-ecran}}

Reads the position shown by a screenshot of an eXtreme Gammon board (default theme): checkers, bar, borne\sphinxhyphen{}off checkers (what is missing from fifteen), dice, side to move and cube. The image (PNG, JPEG or GIF) can contain more than the board; larger than a 4K screen (3840×2160), it is shrunk before reading. The score is never read. What the reading cannot decide is listed as a doubt, never guessed: hidden arrow, stack taller than the five checkers XG draws side by side, unreadable dice.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }capture\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}image\PYGZgt{}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format}} — Output format: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xgid}} (default: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}save}} — Saves the position in the database as an individual position.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}score}} — The score, which the capture does not show: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{money}}, or the two players’ Away scores, player 1’s (bottom) first, for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2a/5a}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}turn}} — The side to move, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} (bottom) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}} (top), when no dice show it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}force}} — Saves despite the reading’s doubts, once the board has been checked. It replaces neither \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}score}} nor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}turn}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}save}} refuses as long as the score, or the turn without dice, is not given, and names the missing option.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }capture\PYG{+w}{ }capture.png
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }capture\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }xgid\PYG{+w}{ }capture.png
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }capture\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}save\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}score\PYG{+w}{ }2a/5a\PYG{+w}{ }capture.png
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }capture\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}save\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}score\PYG{+w}{ }money\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}turn\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }videau.png
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The daemon offers the same reading: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST /v1/positions.fromImage}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"data": "<base64 image>"\}}}. It refuses an image larger than a 4K screen instead of shrinking it, and reads only two images at a time.

./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }bearoff\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }bearoff\PYG{+w}{ }verify\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}file.bd\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }bearoff\PYG{+w}{ }delete\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}ts\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}domain\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The domain is written as under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{makebearoff}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6x9}} for the two\sphinxhyphen{}sided table at nine chequers per player, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{os8}} for the eight\sphinxhyphen{}point one\sphinxhyphen{}sided table (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{os}} alone means \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{os6}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two families do not answer the same question. A \sphinxstylestrong{two\sphinxhyphen{}sided} table widens the domain where the winning probability and the cube verdict are exact; a \sphinxstylestrong{one\sphinxhyphen{}sided} table widens how far from home a chequer may stand without the EPC going silent (up to ten points).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{generate.} States the size, the memory and the estimated time before starting, then shows the percentage and the measured remaining time.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}ts}} — Two\sphinxhyphen{}sided domain to compute, for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6x9}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}os}} — One\sphinxhyphen{}sided domain to compute, as a point count: 6 to 12. Exactly one of the two is required.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}cores}} — Cores to use (default: every core but one).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}data\sphinxhyphen{}dir}} — Where to write it (default: the application’s data directory).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}quiet}} — No progress line.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{CTRL\sphinxhyphen{}C pauses.} The signal is caught: the state is written beside the table and the same command run again continues where it stopped rather than recomputing everything. Half an hour of arithmetic is worth writing down. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bearoff delete}} throws a pending resume away. Only the two\sphinxhyphen{}sided sweep pauses; the one\sphinxhyphen{}sided one is sequential and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}cores}} buys it nothing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{list.} Prices every domain — size, memory, time on this machine — and says which are already present, with their verdict, and which have a paused run. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format json}} for a script, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}cores}} to change the estimate’s assumption.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{verify.} Answers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verified}} (the same bytes as the reference), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unverified}} (well formed, but no fingerprint is recorded for that domain) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corrupt}} (the file contradicts itself). Exits with an error in the last case: this command is made to be put in a script.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{delete.} Removes the table, the pending resume and the debris of a dead run. A default domain is recomputed at the application’s next launch; a wider one is not.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Ce que cette machine a, et ce que chaque domaine coûterait}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }bearoff\PYG{+w}{ }list

./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }bearoff\PYG{+w}{ }generate\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}ts\PYG{+w}{ }6x9\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}cores\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} OS\PYGZhy{}08 : l\PYGZsq{}EPC répond alors jusqu\PYGZsq{}à un pion sur la 8}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }bearoff\PYG{+w}{ }generate\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}os\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{8}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Sur un serveur, dans le volume que lit le démon}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }bearoff\PYG{+w}{ }generate\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}ts\PYG{+w}{ }6x11\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}data\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }/srv/bearoff

./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }bearoff\PYG{+w}{ }verify\PYG{+w}{ }/srv/bearoff/gnubg\PYGZus{}ts6x11.bd
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{openingbook — Which move at this score?}
\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:openingbook-quel-coup-a-ce-score}}\label{\detokenize{cli_analyse:cli-openingbook}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Opening} exercise of the Training panel (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_entrainement:panneau-entrainement}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Training Panel}}}}}) on the command line: the opening move (1st roll) or the reply (2nd roll) of a game at a score, drawn from the embedded opening book and judged against it. Every move tied with the best is right (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{metriques:metrique-livre-ouverture}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Opening book: gap, 95 \% CI and tie}}}}}). No database is read or written.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{openingbook status} — The number of rows in the book and its scores.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }openingbook\PYG{+w}{ }status\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}book\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}fichier\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }text\PYG{p}{|}json\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{openingbook question} — Draws a question: the opening roll and the score, with the XGID of the opening position; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}roll second}}, the reply roll in the position left by an opening move tied with the best at that score, with that move and the XGID of the reply position.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }openingbook\PYG{+w}{ }question\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}roll first|second}} — The roll to play: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{first}} (the opening, the default) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{second}} (the reply).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}score <liste>}} — Scores to draw, separated by commas: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4\sphinxhyphen{}2}} (the replier at 4 points, the opener at 2), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1\sphinxhyphen{}2}} (Crawford game), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1\sphinxhyphen{}1}} (the DMP, double match point), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{money}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}opening <liste>}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}reply <liste>}} — Opening or reply rolls to draw (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{31,65}}); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}reply}} only with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}roll second}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}seed <n>}} — Reproducible draw (0 = random).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}book <fichier>}} — A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.jsonl}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.jsonl.gz}} book instead of the embedded one.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json}} — Output format.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{openingbook answer} — Judges a move and shows every candidate against the best: gap, 95 \% CI and « tied », in score\sphinxhyphen{}normalised equity, with the number of games and the rollout setting. Without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}after}}, the move is the opening; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}reply}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}after}}, the move is the reply played after that opening move, the one named by the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}roll second}} question.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }openingbook\PYG{+w}{ }answer\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}opening\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}jet\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}score\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}score\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}reply\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}jet\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}after\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}coup\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZlt{}coup\PYGZgt{}\PYGZsq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }openingbook\PYG{+w}{ }question\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}score\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYGZhy{}2,2\PYGZhy{}4
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }openingbook\PYG{+w}{ }answer\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}opening\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{31}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}score\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYGZhy{}2\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}8/5 6/5\PYGZsq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }openingbook\PYG{+w}{ }question\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}roll\PYG{+w}{ }second\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}score\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYGZhy{}2
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }openingbook\PYG{+w}{ }answer\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}opening\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{31}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}reply\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{21}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}score\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{4}\PYGZhy{}2\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}after\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}8/5 6/5\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}13/11 6/5\PYGZsq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{Study, lessons and training}
\label{\detokenize{cli_entrainement:etude-lecons-et-entrainement}}\label{\detokenize{cli_entrainement:cli-entrainement-chapitre}}\label{\detokenize{cli_entrainement::doc}}

\subsubsection{study — The cross\sphinxhyphen{}import study queue}
\label{\detokenize{cli_entrainement:study-la-file-d-etude-transversale}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Lists the blunders of the database’s reference player, all imports together, that nothing has handled yet: no comment, no Anki card, outside any collection and without a “seen” mark (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{guide_utilisateur:file-etude-transversale}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Blunders nothing has handled yet}}}}}). Each subcommand takes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }study\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}subcommand\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Subcommands:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{queue {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit <n>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — The queue, from the most costly to the least costly; at most fifty positions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mark \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id>}} — Marks the position as seen: it leaves the queue. The mark is data in the database, never exported.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unmark \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id>}} — Removes the mark: the position returns to the queue.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{status \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id>}} — Tells whether the position carries the mark.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }study\PYG{+w}{ }queue\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}limit\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{20}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }study\PYG{+w}{ }mark\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1234}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{lesson — Manage lessons}
\label{\detokenize{cli_entrainement:lesson-gerer-les-lecons}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Manages lessons: ordered sequences of steps that a coach writes once for a student. Each step has a title, a text and can show a collection, a position, both or neither. A lesson is handed over in a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dbx}} file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export}} subcommand) and read in the graphical interface with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:le}} command. Every subcommand takes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}db}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show}} accept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text}} (default) or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{json}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }lesson\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}subcommand\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Subcommands:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list}} — Lists the lessons: id, name, number of steps.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{show \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id>}} — The steps of a lesson, in order: step id, title, text, and the collection and position shown.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{create \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}name <nom> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}description <texte>{]}}} — Creates an empty lesson.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edit \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}name <nom>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}description <texte>{]}}} — Renames a lesson or changes its description; what is not given is kept.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{delete \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}confirm}} — Deletes the lesson and its steps, permanently (lessons have no trash). The collections and positions that its steps showed remain in the database.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{add\sphinxhyphen{}step \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lesson <id> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}title <titre>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}text <texte> | \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}text\sphinxhyphen{}file <fichier>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection <id>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}position <id>{]}}} — Adds a step at the end of the lesson.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{edit\sphinxhyphen{}step \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lesson <id> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}step <id> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}title …{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}text … | \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}text\sphinxhyphen{}file …{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection <id>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}position <id>{]}}} — Edits a step; only the fields given change, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection 0}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}position 0}} remove what the step showed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{remove\sphinxhyphen{}step \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lesson <id> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}step <id>}} — Removes a step.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reorder \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lesson <id> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}steps <id,id,…>}} — Sets the order of the steps; the list gives all the steps of the lesson.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id{[},id…{]}> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}out <fichier> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analysis=false{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}comments=false{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watermark <texte>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}watermark\sphinxhyphen{}note <texte>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}password <mot de passe>{]}}} — Exports one or more lessons, with the collections and positions that their steps show, to a new database file; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}password}}, the file is a protected \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dbx}} (see the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export}} command for the watermark). With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}html}} (a single lesson, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lang fr|en|de|el|es|fi|it|ja|ru}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}out}} is a self\sphinxhyphen{}contained HTML page: title, description, each step with its text and board, the stored analysis of each position folded away like a quiz answer, and the origin of the database’s watermark at the foot, if it has one. The file holds no script and no network address.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{done \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}step <id> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}undo{]}}} — Marks a step as done in this database, or removes the mark with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}undo}}: this is the progress of the person reading the lesson, and no export carries it.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{progress \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — Shows the steps of the lesson marked as done, with the date of the gesture.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Importing a file that contains a lesson creates it with its steps; a lesson whose name already exists in the database is left untouched, so importing the same file again changes nothing. Reading a lesson records nothing on the reader’s side; only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{done}} writes its progress.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Exporting the whole library (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type database}}) carries all the lessons with what their steps show; a partial export carries only those named, through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lesson export}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }lesson\PYG{+w}{ }create\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Jouer contre un prime\PYGZdq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }lesson\PYG{+w}{ }add\PYGZhy{}step\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}lesson\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}title\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Le temps\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}text\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Comptez les pips.\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}collection\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{3}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }lesson\PYG{+w}{ }show\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Remettre la leçon à un élève, protégée et marquée de son origine}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }lesson\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{1}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}out\PYG{+w}{ }lecon.dbx\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}password\PYG{+w}{ }secret\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}watermark\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Cours du 12 mars\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{anki — Spaced\sphinxhyphen{}repetition decks}
\label{\detokenize{cli_entrainement:anki-paquets-de-repetition-espacee}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consults and maintains the spaced\sphinxhyphen{}repetition (FSRS) decks of the GUI’s Anki panel. Reviewing a card needs the board and stays in the GUI; the CLI lists, measures and resynchronises.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }anki\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}subcommand\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Subcommands:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decks {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json|csv{]}}} — List of decks: source, number of cards, due cards, new cards.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck <id> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — Review statistics for a deck: total, new, learning, review, due now, and its FSRS parameters.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{forecast {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck <id>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}days <n>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json|csv{]}}} — Cards coming due per calendar day (UTC) over the next \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}} days (default 30, maximum 365); day 0 absorbs all overdue cards; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck 0}} (default) covers all decks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sync \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck <id>}} — Adds a card for every position of the deck’s source that does not have one yet; existing cards keep their schedule.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{retention \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck <id> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — a deck’s measured retention, against the target its owner chose.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{card \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id <id> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}action suspend|unsuspend|bury|remove|undo {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — acts on one card. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Suspending} sets it aside without losing its history (it no longer comes up in a session); \sphinxstyleemphasis{burying} hides it until the next day, saying nothing about its worth; \sphinxstyleemphasis{removing} deletes it from the deck — the position itself stays in the library, a deck being only a study list laid over it. \sphinxstyleemphasis{undo} reverts the card’s last rating, which returns to its state before that rating, and shows that state. With no rating to undo, the command refuses: “the card has no review to undo”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{log {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck <id>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit <n>{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json{]}}} — the review log, most recent first (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck 0}}, the default, covers every deck; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit}} defaults to 20). The log is what the scheduler was actually told, as opposed to what it plans today: the only place a grade entered by mistake can be seen.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck <id> | \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection <id> \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}out <file.apkg> {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format apkg{]} {[}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lang <lang>{]}}} — Writes a deck, or a collection, as an Anki package \sphinxstylestrong{.apkg} that the Anki application imports on a computer or a phone: one card per position, with the board, score, cube and dice on the front, and the best move or right cube decision, its equity and the played move’s error on the back, labelled in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}lang}} language (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{en}} by default). A living collection is evaluated at export, within its ceiling. The export writes nothing to the database; a re\sphinxhyphen{}export imported into Anki updates its cards instead of duplicating them. The daemon serves the same file on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST /v1/anki.exportApkg}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A deck based on a collection re\sphinxhyphen{}reads its collection; based on a living collection, it replays its query under the same ceiling of 5,000 positions and reports a truncated source on the error output. A deck based on a search keeps the search as the GUI saved it (command, board and the identifiers of the positions found at that time): the search grammar lives in the GUI, so the CLI resynchronises from the saved identifiers and reports it on the error output — open the deck in the GUI to replay the search itself.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }anki\PYG{+w}{ }decks\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }anki\PYG{+w}{ }stats\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}deck\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }json
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }anki\PYG{+w}{ }forecast\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}deck\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}days\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{14}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }anki\PYG{+w}{ }sync\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}deck\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }anki\PYG{+w}{ }card\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}action\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{suspend}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }anki\PYG{+w}{ }card\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}action\PYG{+w}{ }undo
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }anki\PYG{+w}{ }log\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}deck\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}limit\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{50}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }anki\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{export}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}deck\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}out\PYG{+w}{ }paquet.apkg\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}lang\PYG{+w}{ }fr

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Day         Due}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}         \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 2026\PYGZhy{}09\PYGZhy{}02  12}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ...}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}

\subsubsection{training — The training log}
\label{\detokenize{cli_entrainement:training-le-journal-d-entrainement}}\label{\detokenize{cli_entrainement:cli-training}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads back the log of the Training tab (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_entrainement:panneau-entrainement}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Training Panel}}}}}) and turns missed questions into something to review. The log is written by the graphical application, or by a daemon client through the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training.save}} route; the command line does not ask questions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{training sessions} — The sessions, most recent first, with their identifier; the PR exists only for \sphinxstyleemphasis{Decision}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }training\PYG{+w}{ }sessions\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}fichier\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exercise <name>}} — A single exercise: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scores}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pips}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bearoff}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{evaluation}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decision}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit <n>}} — Number of sessions (default 20; 0 = all).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json}} — Output format.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{training missed} — The missed positions, each once, most recently missed first; a question that timed out counts as missed. Only \sphinxstyleemphasis{Decision} questions keep their position.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }training\PYG{+w}{ }missed\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}fichier\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}options\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Options:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}exercise <name>}} — The sessions of a single exercise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}session <id>}} — A single session (an identifier from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training sessions}}).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}limit <n>}} — Number of positions (default 0 = all).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deck <name>}} — Creates an Anki deck of these positions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}collection <name>}} — Creates a collection of these positions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}format text|json}} — Output format; in JSON, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PositionIDs}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{DeckID}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CollectionID}} when they are created.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }training\PYG{+w}{ }sessions\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}exercise\PYG{+w}{ }decision
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }training\PYG{+w}{ }missed\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}session\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{12}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}deck\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Ratés de lundi\PYGZdq{}}
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }training\PYG{+w}{ }missed\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }base.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}collection\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Mes ratés\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{+w}{ }json
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
