Sent back in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{If\sphinxhyphen{}None\sphinxhyphen{}Match}}, it gets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{304}} with no body as long as nothing the route reads has changed. Any write changes the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ETag}} at once: a gesture in the tournament or in a tournament of the same event, the attachment of a match, a draft started from a slot, the renaming of a tournament, a change to the event. Answering \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{304}} replays no tournament, which makes a wall page that polls every few seconds inexpensive. Only what depends on the time is an exception: proposals, the clock and pages are computed at the moment of the read, so an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ETag}} is valid for one minute at most. A client that reloads thus sees a deadline or a pause go by within the minute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These routes are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST}}. For this verb, RFC 9110 (§13.1.2) answers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{412}} to a matching \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{If\sphinxhyphen{}None\sphinxhyphen{}Match}}. The daemon answers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{304}} nonetheless: the request body carries only the parameters of a read with no effect, which behaves like a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GET}}. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{If\sphinxhyphen{}None\sphinxhyphen{}Match: *}} form is refused (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}}), because it designates no response the client would already have. An invalid request (a negative \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round}}, for example) is refused before any condition.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}si\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}X\PYG{+w}{ }POST\PYG{+w}{ }http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/rencontres.pageHtml\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 1\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}d\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}id\PYGZdq{}:1\PYGZcb{}\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }grep\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}i\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZca{}etag\PYGZsq{}}
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}si\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}X\PYG{+w}{ }POST\PYG{+w}{ }http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/rencontres.pageHtml\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 1\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}If\PYGZhy{}None\PYGZhy{}Match: W/\PYGZdq{}…\PYGZdq{}\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}d\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}id\PYGZdq{}:1\PYGZcb{}\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Like the rest of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1}}, these routes authenticate no one: behind the proxy ({\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-proxy-deployment}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Deployment behind an authenticating proxy}}}}}), anyone who reaches a tenant’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/directions.}} prefix reads its tournaments, player names included. A proxy that reserves these reads for certain users does so with a rule on that prefix and on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/rencontres.}}.


\subsubsection{Direction gestures}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:les-gestes-de-direction}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-direction-gestures}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb serve \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}direction}} opens the gestures the workstation performs on a directed tournament and on an event. Without this flag, these routes answer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{404}}, as if absent. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{call}} always serves them.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.create}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournamentId}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.setConfig}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.previewConfig}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}}, the configuration in the engine’s JSON format);

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
registrations: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.enterParticipants}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.addParticipant}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{club}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rating}}; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{section}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{key}}, a latecomer takes a bye slot; with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, the registration keeps the given identifier, refused if it is already taken), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.updateParticipant}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.withdraw}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.reinstate}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.makeAbsent}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.makeAvailable}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.addPair}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.updatePair}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.replaceParticipant}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, the player replaced, who has not played a match yet; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{club}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rating}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{newId}} for the newcomer; a doubles pair is refused), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.replacePair}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, the pair replaced; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{members}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rating}} for the new pair, whose two persons replace the former ones in the directory), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.swapParticipants}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{a}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}}: two players who have not played a match yet exchange places);

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the course of play: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.confirmProposal}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{action}}, as proposed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.get}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.confirmAllProposals}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.startMatch}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.enterResult}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.enterForfeit}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.moveMatchToTable}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.cancelMatch}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.correctResult}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.close}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.reopen}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.addNote}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.attachMatch}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.detachMatch}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
confirming a list: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.confirmProposals}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{actions}}, the proposals as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.get}} shows them) records all of them at the same instant, so that the matches launched together form a single batch, or records none. A proposal held back (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reason}} equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{waiting\_table}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{player\_unavailable}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{player\_busy}}) cannot be confirmed: a list containing one is refused. What the list brings about, the queue after a repechage or the draw of the next phase, is proposed in the response and is never confirmed automatically;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the reason for a refusal: the 400 of a refused gesture carries, when the cause is one of these, a stable code in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{details.reason}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_taken}} (the table is occupied, in this tournament or in another one sharing its room), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{player\_busy}} (a player is in a match of another tournament of the room), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{no\_such\_table}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_outside}} (the table is in none of the tournament’s rooms), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{table\_closed}} (table reserved or kept for someone else), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{proposal\_held}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{proposal\_changed}} (a proposal of the list is held back, or is no longer proposed as listed). The message remains meant for reading, the code for deciding;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the other reasons: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repechage\_pending}} (a draw or a passage to the next phase is listed while a repechage between tied candidates awaits the director’s choice), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{empty\_list}} (empty list), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid\_action}} (a proposal sent back cannot be read) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{engine\_refused}} (the engine’s rules refuse the event, the message says which);

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the rounds of the current phase: in a manually paired phase (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{manual}}), the director places each match with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.startMatch}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}: the latest round; the next one opens it) and each bye with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.placeBye}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round}}), withdrawn with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.cancelBye}}; any other phase refuses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round}}. In a Swiss by rounds (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{swiss\_rounds}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.giveHalfBye}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round}}, required) records that a player will not play that round and takes half a point there, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.cancelHalfBye}} withdraws it while the round is not open;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the event: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.create}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.update}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.attach}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.detach}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.trash}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.setTableOutOfService}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.setBreaks}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the table properties: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.setTables}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tableSettings}}, one entry per table that carries any: number, name, room, reserved, assigned to), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.setEventRooms}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournamentId}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rooms}}, the rooms the competition plays in; none means all tables) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.setTables}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournamentId}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tableSettings}}) for a competition that plays alone.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A tournament gesture returns the full view of the tournament, like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.get}}; an event gesture returns the event. The service then rewrites the display pages in the folder the database designates, as at the workstation. A page that cannot be written (folder gone, disk full) does not cancel the gesture: the response carries a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Direction\sphinxhyphen{}Page\sphinxhyphen{}Warning}} header for each page not written (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournament 3}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontre 2}}), without the server path, and the workstation shows it in its status bar.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A gesture that the rules refuse (empty name, occupied table, tournament that has not started, configuration rejected by the engine) returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}} with the reason. A failure of the daemon or its database returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{500}}, without detail: the reason stays in the daemon’s log.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Simulating a format.} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.simulate}} plays a format through without a tournament or a database: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{config}} (the engine configuration), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players}} (a head count, from 2 to 512, or a list of entrants with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rating}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tables}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{runs}} (30 by default, 200 at most) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}}. The response returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{runs}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{minutesP10}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{minutesP50}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{minutesP90}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{estimatedEnd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peakTables}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matchesPerPlayerMin}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matchesPerPlayerMax}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{warnings}}, a list of codes. The same request returns the same response. The simulation starts each match as soon as it is paired: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{peakTables}} is the number of tables needed so that nobody waits, and the code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tables\_exceeded}} flags a smaller room, whose returned durations are then a minimum. No version and no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{If\sphinxhyphen{}Match}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{run}}, played with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}} of the request, decides: its work is counted, not timed, and a format of which this tournament requires more than an ordinary processor computes in three tenths of a second is refused with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{503}}, code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unavailable}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{details.reason}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{too\_heavy}}, without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Retry\sphinxhyphen{}After}}, as soon as the count exceeds that threshold. The same request gets the same verdict on any machine, whatever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{runs}} is. It is well formed but too heavy: reduce the field, the pools, the lives, the rounds or the format. An admitted format always returns this first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{run}}; the following ones stop two seconds after the computation starts, and the response is then partial: it carries the code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{time\_budget}} and relies on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{runs}} played, whose number depends on the machine. A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{run}} that the engine does not bring to its end is discarded under the code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{run\_failed}}: the figures rely on the others. A malformed or out\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}bounds request returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}}, whatever the load.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The bounds of a simulation are refusals, stated before any computing: 512 players, 200 \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{runs}}, 16 phases, matches to 99 points, 100 lives, 4096 tables, 4096 matches drawn at once by a phase (the pools of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{round\_robin}} as the engine draws them, the field split equally: a single pool of 91 players at most, two pools of 50 for 100 players in pools of 91, pools of 17 for 512 players) and a body of 1 MiB (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{413}} beyond). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.create}} bounds neither the field, nor the lives, nor the pools; the simulation does: nothing in it is sized by the request, and the draw of a large pool, which cannot be interrupted, would hold the processor and the memory outside the budget. Under these bounds, the work decides: a single pool of 40 players, a bracket of 512 or a double elimination of 256 return \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{too\_heavy}}; a single pool of 30 players, a double elimination of 128, a bracket of 256 or 200 players in pools of 4 are admitted. The durations follow the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{min\_per\_point}} of the configuration (8 minutes by default) and, with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}, skip its breaks (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{breaks}}) as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.clock}} does; without a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}}, a break, which is a date, is not counted. Also refused (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}}): a format that plays no match with this field, a simulated tournament longer than a year, and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{start}} whose end falls off the calendar.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The count includes the pairing search of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{swiss\_rounds}}, which the engine counts in steps: a large Swiss whose rounds approach its field, or a club holding more than half the field with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{avoid\_clubs}}, searches long for a round without rematch, and returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{too\_heavy}} on that count, with no bound on the number of rounds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The two computing slots belong to the process, all tenants together: a tenant holding one takes a second only if no other tenant is waiting, and a tenant holding none waits for the next one, three seconds at most. With no slot, the response is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{503}}, code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unavailable}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{details.reason}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{simulation\_busy}}, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Retry\sphinxhyphen{}After}}: the same request can be replayed as is. This wait adds to the computation budget: end to end a simulation can take up to five seconds, and the host sets its timeout above that. A caller who gives up during the wait is not a failure: nothing is written, and the log carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{499}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
While the tournament is not finished, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.clock}} returns, alongside \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{estimatedEnd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{estimatedEndEarly}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{estimatedEndLate}}: the 10th and 90th percentiles of the same forecast.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Version required.} Every read of a tournament or an event returns a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Direction\sphinxhyphen{}Version}} header, and every gesture sends it back in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{If\sphinxhyphen{}Match}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{If\sphinxhyphen{}Match}} (or with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}), the gesture is refused: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{428}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
if someone has written since that read, the gesture is refused: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{409}}. The error’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{details}} field carries the fresh state and its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{version}}: the client re\sphinxhyphen{}reads, then replays its gesture if it is still valid;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
otherwise the gesture is applied and returns the new version in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Direction\sphinxhyphen{}Version}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The comparison is made in the gesture’s transaction, under a database lock (PostgreSQL advisory lock per tournament or per event, SQLite write lock): of two gestures sent on the same read, only one is applied, whether they go through the same daemon, through two daemons on the same PostgreSQL database, or through the workstation and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{call}} on the same file. The gesture is written all or nothing. A tournament played in an event has its event’s version, so a gesture in a sibling competition changes it too. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{directions.create}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontres.create}} target nothing existing and take no version.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Idempotence.} A gesture that carries an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Idempotency\sphinxhyphen{}Key}} header is applied only once: sent again with the same key, it returns the first response, with its headers (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Direction\sphinxhyphen{}Version}} included) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Idempotency\sphinxhyphen{}Replayed: true}}. A double click or a network retry does not enter two results; two simultaneous sends of the same key run the gesture only once. Only a successful response is kept.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The key is bound to the request body: the same key with another body returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{422}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The replay comes before the version check: it returns the kept response without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{428}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{409}}, even if the version has moved since.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Keys live in memory, in each instance of the daemon, for 24 hours, at most 1,000 per tenant: a restart forgets them, and another instance does not know them.

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}si\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}X\PYG{+w}{ }POST\PYG{+w}{ }http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/directions.get\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 1\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}d\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}tournamentId\PYGZdq{}:3\PYGZcb{}\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }grep\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}i\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZca{}direction\PYGZhy{}version\PYGZsq{}}
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}s\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}X\PYG{+w}{ }POST\PYG{+w}{ }http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/directions.enterResult\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 1\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}If\PYGZhy{}Match: \PYGZdq{}…\PYGZdq{}\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}Idempotency\PYGZhy{}Key: t4\PYGZhy{}r2\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}d\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}tournamentId\PYGZdq{}:3,\PYGZdq{}matchId\PYGZdq{}:\PYGZdq{}m7\PYGZdq{},\PYGZdq{}winner\PYGZdq{}:\PYGZdq{}aa\PYGZdq{},\PYGZdq{}scoreA\PYGZdq{}:7,\PYGZdq{}scoreB\PYGZdq{}:3\PYGZcb{}\PYGZsq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The daemon authenticates no one (ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0005). With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}direction}}, anyone the proxy lets through enters results. The engine knows no role (director, referee, reader): a role is a proxy rule, which reserves \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/directions.}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/rencontres.}} for directors, or lets only reads through. Never run \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}direction}} on a reachable daemon without that proxy, even on a club’s Wi\sphinxhyphen{}Fi.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsubsection{Being notified of gestures: \sphinxstyleliteralintitle{\sphinxupquote{/v1/events}}}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:etre-prevenu-des-gestes-v1-events}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-events}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{GET /v1/events}} is a \sphinxstyleemphasis{Server\sphinxhyphen{}Sent Events} stream (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{text/event\sphinxhyphen{}stream}}): one message per validated gesture of the tenant, published after the database write, never for a refused or cancelled gesture. The message says what changed and its new version, not the state: the client re\sphinxhyphen{}reads what it displays, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{If\sphinxhyphen{}None\sphinxhyphen{}Match}}.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{event: rencontre}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontreId}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournamentIds}} (the event’s competitions, before and after the gesture) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{version}};

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{event: direction}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournamentId}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{version}}, for a tournament played outside any event;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{event: transcription}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transcriptionId}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{revision}}; an abandoned or finished draft carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{removed}} (and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matchId}} for Finish).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{removed: true}} signals what no longer exists. The route is served only with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}direction}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}transcription}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}duel}}: without them, the daemon writes nothing it would have to announce, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/events}} answers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{404}}. Like every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/}} route, it requires \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}: a subscriber hears only its own tenant. A tenant holds at most 16 open streams at a time; beyond that, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{429}}. The workstation uses the same service but plugs no bus into it: its gestures are not announced.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournament}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rencontre}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transcription}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duel}} parameters (comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated or repeated identifiers) narrow the subscription: a message passes if it names one of them. A tournament of an event receives the messages of its event. An unknown parameter or an invalid identifier returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}N\PYG{+w}{ }http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/events?rencontre\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{2}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 1\PYGZsq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No history.} The daemon keeps no message. Every stream opens with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{event: resync}}, carrying an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}}: the client may have missed gestures before connecting, or between two connections, and re\sphinxhyphen{}reads everything it displays. The reason is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reconnected}} when the request carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Last\sphinxhyphen{}Event\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{subscribed}} otherwise. A subscriber that is too slow, whose queue of 64 messages is full, is disconnected after the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resync}}: it never delays a gesture. The stream announces a reconnection delay of 3 seconds.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Through a proxy.} A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{: ping}} comment is sent every 25 seconds so that a proxy does not cut a silent stream; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Accel\sphinxhyphen{}Buffering: no}} asks nginx not to buffer it. The stream is not compressed, escapes the timeout of ordinary requests and counts as only one request for rate limiting. Stopping the daemon closes all streams; a subscription requested during shutdown receives \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{503}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple instances.} On SQLite, a single instance holds the database: the in\sphinxhyphen{}memory bus is enough. On PostgreSQL, as soon as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}direction}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}transcription}} is active, each instance relays its actions to the others through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{LISTEN/NOTIFY}}, on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\_events}} channel: a subscriber attached to one instance hears an action validated on another, or issued through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{call}} on the same database. The tenant travels in the notification and the instance that receives it delivers it only to that tenant’s subscribers. Each instance opens two more connections (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{application\_name}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}events\sphinxhyphen{}…}} for listening, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}notify\sphinxhyphen{}…}} for sending); an instance that cannot listen at startup refuses to start. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{call}} announces without listening, and serves its request even if it cannot announce.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any role allowed to connect can emit on this channel, under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rls}} too. A received notification is trusted only if its tenant is valid and its kind known; the rest is logged and ignored. At worst, a forged notification can make a tenant’s subscribers re\sphinxhyphen{}read their data.
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The notification is sent after the database write, like the local message. Two losses remain without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resync}}: an instance killed between the write and the notification, and a shutdown that cannot send in 2 seconds what is left in the queue. The action is validated, but the streams already open on the other instances only learn of it when their client reconnects.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A lost listening connection is re\sphinxhyphen{}established, with a growing delay from 250 ms to 30 s. Actions from other instances that happened during the outage are lost: on recovery, each subscriber of the instance receives a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resync}} with the reason \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{missed}}. A notification too long for PostgreSQL (8,000 bytes), or that an instance could not send, reaches the others as this same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resync}} for the tenant concerned.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The stream \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} values are specific to each instance. A client that a load balancer sends to another instance gains nothing from them: the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resync}} that opens every stream makes it re\sphinxhyphen{}read what it displays.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{The bearoff databases}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:les-bases-de-bearoff}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-bearoff}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The daemon computes its two default tables at start\sphinxhyphen{}up, in the background (TS\sphinxhyphen{}06\sphinxhyphen{}06 for the cube verdict, OS\sphinxhyphen{}06 for the EPC): about six seconds of one core, once, in its data directory — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$XDG\_DATA\_HOME/blunderdb}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}/.local/share/blunderdb}} otherwise. Nothing is downloaded and nothing is embedded in the binary (\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0027-bearoff-databases-are-generated-not-shipped-and-verified-against-gnubg.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0027}). If that directory is read\sphinxhyphen{}only, the tables are held in memory for the life of the process: the service starts, it simply pays for the computation at every restart.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A wider domain is not computed at start\sphinxhyphen{}up — TS\sphinxhyphen{}06\sphinxhyphen{}11 weighs 1.2 GB and takes minutes, which is not something a service decides on its own. It is up to the operator to make it, with the CLI, in the volume the daemon will read:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} generate}
blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }bearoff\PYG{+w}{ }generate\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}ts\PYG{+w}{ }6x11\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}data\PYGZhy{}dir\PYG{+w}{ }/srv/data/blunderdb

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} serve}
\PYG{n+nv}{XDG\PYGZus{}DATA\PYGZus{}HOME}\PYG{o}{=}/srv/data\PYG{+w}{ }blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }serve\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }database.db
blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }serve\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}db\PYG{+w}{ }database.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}bearoff\PYGZhy{}ts\PYG{+w}{ }/srv/data/blunderdb/gnubg\PYGZus{}ts6x11.bd
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first launch lets the daemon find the table on its own in its data directory; the second points to it by path, wherever it is. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}data\sphinxhyphen{}dir}} is an option of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{bearoff}} subcommands, never of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{serve}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb bearoff list \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}data\sphinxhyphen{}dir /srv/data/blunderdb}} says what the volume holds and what each domain would cost; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb bearoff verify}} exits with an error on a corrupt table, which makes it a start\sphinxhyphen{}up probe usable as is. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{cli:cli}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Command Line Interface (CLI)}}}}} for the details.


\subsection{The operator routes}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:les-routes-d-exploitation}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-ops-routes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Two calls do not stop at the tenant making them, and therefore live under a prefix of their own, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST /ops/<family>.<method>}}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/ops/maintenance.vacuum}} (SQLite backend) rewrites the \sphinxstylestrong{whole} file, every tenant’s data included, and holds a write lock for the duration;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/ops/tenant.purge}} (PostgreSQL backend) destroys a tenant’s data, and the tenant it destroys is the one named in the header the caller controls.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The daemon authenticates nobody (see below): a route reachable by one tenant is a route \sphinxstylestrong{every} tenant may call. The prefix exists so the proxy can refuse both with a single rule. \sphinxstylestrong{Never expose} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/ops/}} \sphinxstylestrong{through the public proxy.} Under nginx, the rule fits in one line of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{server}} block; under Caddy, in two lines of the site:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k}{location}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/ops/}\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{403}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{k}{location}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{/metrics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{return}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{403}\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
@closed path /ops/* /metrics
respond @closed 403
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}ops\sphinxhyphen{}addr <host:port>}} option goes further: the two routes then leave the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}addr}} address and are served only on that second listener, to be bound on an administration interface. Without the option they stay on the main listener, and blocking them is the proxy’s business.

\sphinxAtStartPar
These routes require the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}} header like every other one — a purge names the tenant it destroys, and needs that header more than anything else. Only the probes (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/healthz}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/readyz}}) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/metrics}} go without.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is why the denial rule above also covers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/metrics}}: requiring no tenant, it is readable by anyone who reaches the daemon, and it publishes the database size and the work in flight, across every tenant. It is meant to be consulted from the daemon’s own machine, or through a path the proxy reserves for operations. The third thing that must never be exposed is not a route but a listener: the one for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pprof\sphinxhyphen{}addr}}, which has no notion of tenant and hands out a profile of the whole process. It should bind to an administration interface, never published by the proxy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
What did \sphinxstylestrong{not} move under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/ops/}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/gammonnet.sweepStale}}. The catch\sphinxhyphen{}up is expensive but it is scoped to the calling tenant; what bounds it is the rate limit and the in\sphinxhyphen{}flight gauges, not a trust boundary.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The complete contract — every method, its request and its response — is generated from the source and versioned: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{openapi.yaml}} at the repository root (OpenAPI format, schemas included) and its readable annex, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_reference:api-reference}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{API contract}}}}} (one table per family). Both are regenerated by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{go run ./cmd/openapi\sphinxhyphen{}gen}}, and a dedicated test fails if either falls behind the routes actually registered.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1}} request accepts a JSON body (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Content\sphinxhyphen{}Type: application/json}}, or no header at all — a body of another type is refused with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400 invalid}} rather than failing on a confusing JSON parse error); a known method called with the wrong HTTP verb answers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{405}}, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Allow}} header naming the one verb it accepts. Listing methods that take a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} refuse anything past 1000 rows per page (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400 invalid}}) rather than honouring an unbounded value.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every listing family accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{offset}}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.list}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.listIds}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches.list}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{search.find}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.reviewLog}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{comments.listAll}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournaments.list}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collections.positions}}. Both default to zero, which means what it has always meant: everything. \sphinxstylestrong{There is no implicit cap} — a stream is not held in memory, so an unbounded list costs time and bandwidth but never the daemon’s footing, whereas a silent default limit would have a client read a truncated list believing it complete. What the two parameters buy is the ability to page, for whoever wants to.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every TCP connection is bounded in read/write time per request — a generous budget for ordinary calls, a far larger one for streaming routes (NDJSON lists, imports/exports, the gammonNet catch\sphinxhyphen{}up sweep) — and the number of them open at once is capped: past that many, a further connection waits for one of the existing ones to free up rather than every connection unconditionally getting its own thread of execution. A graceful shutdown (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SIGINT}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SIGTERM}}) first cancels every in\sphinxhyphen{}flight import and gammonNet catch\sphinxhyphen{}up — each answers with a trailing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"event":"cancelled"\}}} event instead of having its connection cut with no explanation — before closing the server within the usual grace period. An uploaded import’s temporary file keeps only the extensions the daemon recognises from the original one (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xg}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xgp}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.sgf}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.mat}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.bgf}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ogxm}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.txt}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dbx}}), and every import in flight — across every tenant — shares one global quota of bytes spooled to disk: past it, a new import is refused (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{too many requests}}) rather than letting \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\$TMPDIR}} usage grow without bound.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/imports.json}} reads back a blunderDB JSON export by filling gaps: the analysis it carries is written only on a position that has none yet, never replacing an existing analysis, and the rollouts on both sides are kept.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{search}} family offers three doors onto the same search. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{search.find}} takes the complete filter object, field by field. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{search.query}} takes a query written in the language of the application’s command bar (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{s cube p>30 E>50}}, described in {\hyperref[\detokenize{cmd_mode::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{List of commands}}}}) and streams the same positions; it is the only way to reach, over the network, the filters that have no obvious field — move pattern, comment text, player, date, excluded dice, zones and blots. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{search.parse}} searches nothing: it answers what a query means — the filters it denotes, its canonical form (two equivalent queries share it, which makes a saved search comparable) and its diagnostics.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A query carrying a token nothing recognises is refused (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400 invalid}}, naming the token) rather than run while narrowing the search in silence. A token that is understood but has no effect here — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}}, which switches on the exclusion structure, itself a board rather than text — travels in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}BlunderDB\sphinxhyphen{}Query\sphinxhyphen{}Diagnostics}} header, so that the body stays NDJSON positions for every existing client.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.listFields}} returns, for a page of ids, what a table of positions shows beside the board: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{analysed}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{playedErrorMp}} (the played error, in millipoints), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{date}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matchDated}}, then two lists of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{id, name\}}} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collections}}, in the library’s order, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decks}}, the study decks holding a card of the position, in the order they were created. An empty list is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}{]}}}, never \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{search.page}} returns the same rows when asked for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{listFields}}. The cost is a fixed number of queries per page, whatever its length.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two methods in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions}} family decode a position without storing it: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.fromXGID}} rebuilds a position from an XGID string, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.fromXGP}} from a single\sphinxhyphen{}position \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.xgp}} file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST /v1/exports.sqlite}} exports the whole current tenant — positions, collections, matches, tournaments (with their Direction and Encounter), lessons, transcriptions, aliases, analyses, comments, played moves, filter library and Anki decks — into a SQLite file that the desktop workstation can open as is. The JSON request body is optional; it carries the export options of the export window and of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb export}}, under the same names and read the same way, so that the same set of options writes the same file through all three routes. An absent field keeps its default value, that of the whole library: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{wholeLibrary}}, each \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include…}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeAnkiHistory}} are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{true}}. An \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include…}} option set to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}} removes its family (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeMatches}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeCollections}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeTournaments}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeLessons}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeAnkiDecks}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeFilterLibrary}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeTranscriptions}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeAliases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeAnalysis}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeComments}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includePlayedMoves}}); a list of identifiers restricts it to those items (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matchIDs}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collectionIDs}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournamentIDs}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lessonIDs}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deckIDs}}). With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"wholeLibrary": false}}, only the positions named by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positionIDs}} (or all of them with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{allPositions}}), the matches in which they were played, and what the identifier lists designate are exported; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeCollectionPositions}} adds the positions of the chosen collections, and an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{include…}} option left true without a list still carries its whole family when it needs no named positions (lessons, filter library). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{watermark}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{watermarkNote}} apply a watermark signed with the daemon’s own identity (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}identity\sphinxhyphen{}dir}}) — without these fields, the export carries no watermark; requesting them without a configured identity fails with the code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid}}, like a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{password}}: the daemon does not return an encrypted container. A watermarked export also signs every comment written in the tenant and not yet signed, with the same identity: it is \sphinxstylestrong{one for all tenants}, so the signature attests that the comment comes from this server, not from which tenant or which person (name adjustable with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}identity\sphinxhyphen{}name}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions}} supplies whole positions, saved or not, in place of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positionIDs}}. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{metadata}} is refused: the daemon writes into the file only its creation date and the watermark. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"incremental": true}} exports only what has entered the tenant since the last incremental export under the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{syncCursor}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{default}} if absent), and advances that marker in the tenant when the file is built (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:synchroniser-deux-machines}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Synchronising two machines}}}}}). The marker advances \sphinxstylestrong{before} the client has received the file: an interrupted download cannot be replayed by sending the same request, which would no longer carry those rows. To catch up, request a full export (without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{incremental}}), or an incremental export under a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{syncCursor}}, which starts from zero; since the import is idempotent, this overlap creates no duplicates. On PostgreSQL, a concurrent import can make rows numbered below the marker visible after the fact: a marker is therefore held as safe only once every transaction of the database that was running when it was read has ended, however long it lasts, and each incremental export also returns what the previous one carried. The report header carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"syncHeld": true}} when rows were set aside: the marker has then not advanced. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exportPath}} is ignored. A key that the options do not know, or written with another case (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collectionIds}}), is refused with the code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid}}, which names it. The response carries, in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}Export\sphinxhyphen{}Report}} header, the JSON count of what the file contains, family by family. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST /v1/exports.plan}} takes the same body and returns these counts before any export, with the live collections that would be frozen and the “search” decks whose source would lose a part; it writes nothing. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST /v1/exports.planIds}} returns a page of the identifiers behind one of these counts: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export}} carries the body of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exports.sqlite}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{family}} the family, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{offset}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} the page (1000 identifiers at most).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"omitProvenance": true}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}provenance=false}} on the command line, for export and transfer alike) removes what names the original match: analyses leave without players or played moves and cube decisions, no match, tournament, transcription or alias leaves, and naming a match or a tournament is refused (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Without provenance, a saved query never leaves as written: it leaves rewritten by the query parser — only the tokens it read travel, in their canonical form (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{c}} becomes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cube}}) — or it does not leave. The living collection then leaves frozen on the positions it selects at the source, the saved filter stays behind, and the search deck keeps its positions without its query.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A query that reads what stays at the source does not leave: the match (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pl}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{op}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tn}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{au}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ma}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rd:}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ml}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{md}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pr}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}}), a free text (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t"…"}}), the move played and its time (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{E}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tm}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mg}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dr}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dd}}: without the moves played, the query would select other positions on arrival) or, when comments do not leave, a comment (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{co}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xco}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{co:}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#tag}}). Neither does one that carries an unknown or ignored token (a second \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m"…"}}), or a value outside the expected form: a word in place of a number, an engine after \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ad:}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A ranking against a stored position (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{like<n>}}) does not leave either: it names a row of this database, which designates nothing at the destination; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{like}} alone, on a drawn board, reads only that board and leaves. With the comments, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#tag}} leaves only when a comment that is sent bears it, and an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} list holds numbers only. The source of a search deck keeps, in every export, only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ids}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{command}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}} (the drawn board, without the identifier of the position it comes from), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{library}} and, with the provenance, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{payload}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The file carries neither the producer’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{user}} nor its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{description}}. Comments are free text: they leave only when asked for by name (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"includeComments": true}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}comments}}). The name and description of a collection, like the name of a filter or a deck, are also free text and leave as they are: do not write there what the transfer must keep quiet. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type matches}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type mat}} refuse \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}provenance=false}}: a match is the provenance.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Importing a folder or a corpus} is done with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.batch}}, which goes through the same pipeline as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb import \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type batch}}: same matches, same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{canonical\_hash}} fingerprints, a duplicate is written only once. The call returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"importId": …, "files": N\}}} at once and the import carries on in the background for as long as it takes. The batch comes in one of two forms:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
an \sphinxstylestrong{archive}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.zip}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.tar}}, sent as multipart (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{file}} field); only the importable files are extracted from it; the archive is bounded by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ImportMaxBodyBytes}} (512 MiB by default), its unpacked content at twice that;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a \sphinxstylestrong{path local to the daemon}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"path": "corpus", "recursive": true\}}}, read in the directory the operator opened with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}import\sphinxhyphen{}dir}}. Without that option every path is refused (code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid}}); with it, a path that leaves the directory, symbolic links included, is refused too. The daemon authenticates nobody: naming a directory lets any caller read match files from it. This is the way for large corpora, which are not pushed over HTTP.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A match already in the database is not rewritten, but its analyses deeper than the stored ones replace them; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?skip\_duplicates=true}}, accepted by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.batch}} as well as by a file import, ignores it without taking anything from it except the marks, like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}skip\sphinxhyphen{}duplicates}} on the command line.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Idempotency\sphinxhyphen{}Key}} is accepted: replaying the call with the same key returns the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{importId}} (header \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Idempotency\sphinxhyphen{}Replayed: true}}) without restarting the import. For a batch received as an archive, the key names the batch, not the archive’s content.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two limits come from PostgreSQL. A batch archive is counted at the logical size of its entries (holes of sparse archives included): a sum that overflows, or bytes written beyond what the batch reserved, makes it refused (400) and erases what had been written. The database role must own the tables, or hold \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MAINTAIN}} (PostgreSQL 17): otherwise the statistics of a tenant’s first import are not computed, which the server logs once per process (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{import statistics skipped}}) and which the import measures as slower plans until autovacuum has run. Finally, an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.db}} that analyses more already\sphinxhyphen{}present positions without analysis than the lock table holds (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_locks\_per\_transaction}} × \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_connections}}, about 6,400 at the default settings) fails as a whole with an error that says so (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{out of shared memory}}, SQLSTATE 53200): raise \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_locks\_per\_transaction}} or import smaller files.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each refused file carries a stable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{code}} in addition to its text, in the status as in the report (the import of a single file returns it as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{import\_code}} in its error event): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unknown\_format}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{truncated}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{corrupt}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{too\_large}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{empty}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{internal}}. A duplicate is not an error: the report counts it separately. The import of a single file accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?report=deferred}}: its last event then omits the report, which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.report}} returns on demand.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.batch.status}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"importId": …\}}}) returns the state (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{receiving}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{running}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{done}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cancelled}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{failed}}) and the progress measured by the pipeline: files processed, matches imported, duplicates, files in error, positions, bytes read, rate, estimated time remaining. The first hundred errors are listed with their file, the total is exact. A finished batch stays readable for an hour. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.batch.cancel}} stops it: the groups of files already committed stay in the database, the group in progress is rolled back. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.report}} returns, from the status’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{batchId}}, the end\sphinxhyphen{}of\sphinxhyphen{}import report. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.files}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"batchId": …\}}}) returns the batch log: for each file, its path, size, date, SHA\sphinxhyphen{}256 fingerprint and the result (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{new}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{duplicate}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{enriched}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{error}}) with the resulting match or the message. To continue an interrupted batch, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.batch}} accepts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"resume": <batchId>}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{resume}} field of a multipart upload): files already logged with the same path, size and date are skipped without being read; those with the same content are read but not analysed.

\PYG{+w}{     }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 7\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}F\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{file}\PYG{o}{=}@corpus.zip
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}X\PYG{+w}{ }POST\PYG{+w}{ }http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/imports.batch.status\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{     }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 7\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}Content\PYGZhy{}Type: application/json\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Copying a collection from one tenant to another} goes through the client (reading it in place, without a copy, is the job of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.collectionsList}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-tenants-lus}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Reading several tenants}}}}}): the giving tenant calls \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exports.sqlite}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"wholeLibrary": false}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collectionIDs}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeCollectionPositions}} to take their positions along, without lessons, filters or Anki history (and a watermark, so that the receiver knows where the file comes from); the receiving tenant sends the file to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.db}}. Each request carries its own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}; the proxy decides who is allowed to do either. On import, a collection joins the receiver’s collection of the same name, or is created; its positions are appended to it, without duplicates. A living collection of the receiver gets no position: its query makes its content. An Anki deck is shared the same way, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{deckIDs}}: the receiver studies it from scratch, its cards all new; a deck whose name the receiver already holds is left as it is, cards and schedule included, so importing the same file twice changes nothing. Importing a database in the desktop application follows the same rules.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.db}} also reads back matches with their games and moves (a match the recipient already holds, same fingerprint, is not copied again), tournaments (by name), transcription drafts and aliases, with the dates they bore in the source. A living collection’s query is renumbered onto the recipient’s rows, or frozen when a row it names is missing; arriving on a manual list of the same name, it leaves that list as it is and is reported. The response counts each family: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skippedDuplicates}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournaments}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transcriptions}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{aliases}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{livingCollectionsFrozen}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{livingCollectionsOnManual}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unreadable}} when the received database is too old to carry a family.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{progress}} event of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.db}} arrives before any write and carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total\_positions}}, the number of positions the import will process; each following event repeats it, enough to show \sphinxstyleemphasis{n / N} and a remaining time. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{max\_positions}} parameter (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/imports.db?max\_positions=5000}}) brings in at most that number of positions, taken among the first of the file in the order of their original identifier. A match, a collection, a lesson or an Anki deck that touches a position left out is left out entirely, as is a position that nothing would hold after the import; a later import without a cap therefore brings in complete what was missing. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{done}} event counts what was left out: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions\_left\_out}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches\_left\_out}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collections\_left\_out}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lessons\_left\_out}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decks\_left\_out}}. Cancelled (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.cancel}}) or on error, the import writes no row: the whole merge fits in one transaction. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imports.dbAnalyze}} receives the same file and returns, without importing anything, what it would bring: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positionsHeld}} (those the tenant already holds), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matchesKnown}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collections}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lessons}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{decks}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sourceVersion}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unreadable}}; an unreadable file, or one the import would refuse, is refused there (400), like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{import \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}type database \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analyze}} on the command line.
