\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training}} family keeps the log of the Training tab: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training.save}} adds a session (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exercise}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seedSource}}, counts, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{items}}) and returns its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Idempotency\sphinxhyphen{}Key}} accepted); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training.sessions}} reads the sessions back, most recent first (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exercise}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} optional); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training.numberStats}} aggregates an exercise’s items by number type; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training.missed}} returns the missed positions, each once, most recently missed first (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exercise}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sessionId}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} optional). A Decision item carries its position (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positionId}}), the answer given (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{answer}}) and its cost in millipoints (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{errorMp}}, absent when timed out). The questions themselves are drawn by the client.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training.generateBearoff}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training.generateEvaluation}} draw questions of the Bearoff and Evaluation exercises, with their truth, for a client that has someone work in front of their own board: nothing is kept, the clock and the marking stay with the client. The body is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"pool"}}, the canonical shapes; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"board"}}, the neighbourhood of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}}, which is the seed; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"library"}}, the tenant’s positions listed in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positionIds}}, taken as they stand, one question each), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}} (1 by default, at most 50 for Bearoff and 10 for Evaluation, ignored for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"library"}} which returns one per identifier) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed + count \sphinxhyphen{} 1}} at most 2\textasciicircum{}52). Question \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} is drawn from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed + i}}: the same request and the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}} return the same questions, and question \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} alone is replayed with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}} 1 and the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}} it carries; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}} at 0 draws one, returned in each question. The answer is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"questions": {[}...{]}\}}}, each question carrying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positionId}} (source \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"library"}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{generated}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{refusal}} (a seed outside the domain is a named refusal in the answer, not an error: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notBearoff}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tooFewCheckers}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{emptyBoard}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{noTable}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notAGame}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notMoneyCubeDecision}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notEvaluable}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{plies}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}} and the truth: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{epc}} for Bearoff; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{winChance}} (in percent), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cubeVerdict}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cubeAnswer}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nd}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dt}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dp}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{regime}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{depth}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{epc}} for Evaluation. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"library"}} source reads the tenant (an unknown identifier answers 404); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"pool"}} reads nothing. Bearoff is a table walk of a few microseconds, run on the request. Each Evaluation question, whose truth is computed at 2 plies, is a unit of the shared analysis workers: it waits for its tenant turn and is counted in the analysis quota (which, once exhausted, refuses the call with 429, or cuts short an answer in progress, which then returns fewer questions than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{count}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{openingbook}} family serves the Opening exercise of the Training panel: an opening roll, or a reply, to play at a given score, judged against the book embedded in the binary and computed by blunderDB. The book belongs to no tenant: all draw from the same one and are judged against it, with nothing read from or written to the database. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{openingbook.status}} (body \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}}) returns the number of lines in the book (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lines}}) and the scores it holds (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scores}}, in grid order, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"money"}} for money play). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{openingbook.question}} draws a question; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{roll}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"first"}}, the opening move, by default, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}}, the reply after an opening move tied with the best at that score), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{scores}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{openings}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"31"}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{replies}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"52"}}, for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"second"}}) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}} are optional, an empty list allowing everything and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{seed}} of 0 drawing from the clock. It returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{roll}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opening}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{score}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}} (the board to play), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xgid}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{candidates}} (the number of plays the book ranks), plus \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{openingPlay}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reply}} for a reply. On an empty book, or a restriction that leaves nothing, the response is a success carrying \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"empty": true\}}}, not an error. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{openingbook.grade}} judges an answer: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opening}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{score}} and, for a reply, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{openingPlay}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{reply}} from the question, plus the play made (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{board}}, the board left, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notation}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{board}} winning when both are given); an empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{openingPlay}} judges the opening play. With neither \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{board}} nor \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notation}} (out of time), the verdict is reduced to the correction. It carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{legal}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{notation}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{played}} (the index in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ranked}}, \sphinxhyphen{}1 when the book does not rank that play), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{right}} (the play is tied with the best), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ranked}} (each candidate against the best), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{signature}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{games}} (the rollout’s settings and number of games). A line the book does not hold answers 400. The client logs the session through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{training.save}} like the other exercises, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exercise}} equal to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{opening}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.evaluate}} evaluates a bare position (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{position}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xgid}}), without reading or writing anything in the tenant: with dice, the best moves (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{candidates}}, 5 by default, at most 20); without dice, the cube decision. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ply}} ranges from 0 to 2 (2 by default); a deeper search is the job of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{analyzeMissing}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki}} family gains six methods that extend the spaced\sphinxhyphen{}repetition scheduler (FSRS): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.reviewLog}} (a log of every review — rating and FSRS outcome — powering retention statistics and a faithful history), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.forecast}} (a projection of the number of cards due over the coming days, including overdue cards), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.suspendCard}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.buryCard}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.removeCard}} (remove a card from the review queue temporarily or permanently) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.retention}} (the pass rate measured over a deck’s reviews, read against the target its owner set).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.undoReview}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cardId}}) reverts a card’s last review: the card gets back exactly its state from before that rating (due date, interval, stability, difficulty, counters), the rating leaves the log, and the response is the restored card, with its position. Called again, it goes back one more rating. With no review to undo — card never rated, all its ratings already undone, or a rating recorded before schema 2.42.0 —, it refuses with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{409}} whose message contains “the card has no review to undo”; a card from another tenant is a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{404}}. Like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.reviewCard}}, it accepts an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Idempotency\sphinxhyphen{}Key}}: replayed, it does not undo one rating too many.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.retention}} replaces \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{anki.optimizeParams}}, which nudged the target toward the observed rate and could write it. The retention target is a \sphinxstylestrong{choice} about the load/quality trade\sphinxhyphen{}off, the measured rate is its \sphinxstylestrong{outcome}, and coupling one to the other is exactly the mechanism FSRS’s authors reject. The method only measures, and never writes.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats}} family provides \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats.playerTable}}, which returns one row of statistics per player (matches, wins/losses, counted decisions, overall / checker / cube PR, Snowie Error Rate, errors, blunders and luck) over the matches the given filter retains. As in the graphical interface, this table honours only the filter’s date range, tournaments and match lengths: the player selection and the decision type are ignored, since the table covers every player and already splits checker and cube into separate columns. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{luck\_known}} field says whether luck was measured for that player; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{luck\_rate\_mp}} must not be read when it is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{false}}, unknown luck not being zero luck.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats.report}} returns in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{html}} field the standalone HTML report for the filter passed (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter}}), the one from the graphical interface and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb stats report}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{language}} chooses its language (English by default).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The filter passed to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats}} methods accepts, alongside \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlayerName}}, a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{PlayerAliases}} field: the other spellings the same person signed under. Since a player’s name is typed by hand into every file, one person routinely appears under several spellings, and a filter that keeps only one computes on part of the matches without anything looking wrong. The field is purely additive: the decisions of any of the names are kept. Merging the names in place (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MergePlayers}}) is the other answer, to be reserved for databases you did not receive from someone else — it rewrites everybody’s matches.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Two methods complete parity with the graphical interface: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats.tournamentBadges}} returns, for each tournament in the database, the indicator shown on its thumbnail (PR of the reference player), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches.findByHash}} indicates whether a given match is already present, from the two duplicate\sphinxhyphen{}detection fingerprints — enough to avoid a redundant import before committing to it. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches.duplicates}} lists the pairs of matches that the dice say are identical — same dice under other names, or a truncated then completed version — like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{repair \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}duplicates}}, without merging anything; a pair with the same dice carries its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pairings}}, the aliases to pass to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.alias.set}} for each reading of who is who.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Other spellings of a player or an event are managed by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.alias.list}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.alias.set}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"alias": …, "canonical": …\}}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.alias.remove}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"alias": …\}}}, returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{removed}}) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.alias.suggest}} (the names that differ only by case, accents, punctuation or word order, recording nothing); the same under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{events.alias.*}} for events. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches.mergePlayers}} creates these aliases rather than rewriting the matches. An import records the canonical name (the fingerprints keep the names of the file), and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats.compute}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats.playerTable}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stats.playerNames}} and the player search read all the spellings as a single person. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.main.get}} returns the main player, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.main.plan}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"name": …\}}}) the matches that designating it would swap (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{swap}}) and those it would leave (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{refused}}), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.main.set}} designates it and swaps them in one transaction, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.main.clear}} removes it without swapping anything; a later import places it as player 1. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players.matchIds}} returns the matches of a player under all of their spellings.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{winner}} field of a game, received by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches.createGame}} and returned by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches.games}}, has a single encoding: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} for player 1, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} for player 2, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} for an unfinished game. A client that still sends \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}1}} in gnubg’s sense (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} for player 1, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} for player 2) records the opposite winner.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{analyses.repair}} recomputes an analysis’s denormalised columns (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cube\_error}} among them) from its full analysis, and returns how many rows were \sphinxstylestrong{actually} corrected. Those columns are only a projection: a faulty projection therefore repairs without re\sphinxhyphen{}importing the source files. The operation is explicit and never triggered on its own — neither when a database is opened nor by a migration, the schema not being at fault. An unreadable analysis is left as it is rather than reset to zero. The known case: the non\sphinxhyphen{}doubles labelled “Double No” by gnuBG, misread before version 0.33.0, which carried the error of a double that never took place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{met}} family manages the tenant’s match equity tables: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{met.list}} lists them; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{met.import}} saves one from a gnuBG XML file, either as text (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source}}, already decoded: a file declared ISO\sphinxhyphen{}8859\sphinxhyphen{}1 is re\sphinxhyphen{}read byte by byte) or as raw bytes (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{source\_base64}}, to be preferred for any file that is not UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} is used when the file names none. A table whose values are already held is returned as held, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{already\_held}} true. Only UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8, US\sphinxhyphen{}ASCII and ISO\sphinxhyphen{}8859\sphinxhyphen{}1 are read; any other encoding is refused with a message that names it; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{met.setCurrent}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"id": N\}}}) makes it the current table, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} returning the built\sphinxhyphen{}in Kazaross\sphinxhyphen{}XG2 table; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{met.ofAnalysis}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"position\_id": N\}}}) returns the table with which the position’s analysis was valued, the current table and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{different}}, true when a match analysis was valued with a table other than the current one — it is then left out of comparisons.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_bibliotheque:corbeille}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{trash}}}}} has its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash}} family. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash.deletePosition}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash.deleteCollection}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash.deleteComment}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash.deleteMatch}} delete while keeping what is needed to restore, and return the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} of the trash entry; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.delete}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{matches.delete}} and the other deletions remain permanent. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash.list}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{kind}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{offset}}) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash.count}} read it, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash.restore}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"id": N\}}}) puts an entry back and returns the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id}} of what comes back, with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{warnings}}: what a successful restore could not put back, each with a stable \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{code}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{direction\_slot\_taken}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{direction\_slot\_gone}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournament\_gone}}) and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{message}} in English. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash.discard}} erases one, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{trash.empty}} erases the entries older than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{olderThanDays}} days (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} empties everything) and returns their number (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{purged}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{changeset}} family synchronises two libraries through their journal. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{changeset.export}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cursor}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}) returns a page: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{records}}, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cursor}} to give back as is, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{more}} as long as the exchange is not finished; a page never separates an object from what it refers to. An empty cursor starts over. A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{410}} response says that this journal cannot continue from that cursor (a backup restored elsewhere, a cursor taken before a family was added to the journal): start again from an empty cursor, the import absorbs the repetition. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{changeset.import}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{records}}) merges, the latest write winning, and returns the report: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{added}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{modified}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{removed}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{older}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conflicts}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{missing}} for a reference that could not be placed. A note overwritten by the import stays in the trash. The journal carries positions (with their analysis), matches, collections, notes, lessons, transcriptions, tournaments and Anki decks with their cards and schedule. A tournament travels with its header, its note and its dates; a match’s attachment to a tournament and its place in the list stay specific to each library. The families without a trash (lessons, transcriptions, tournaments, decks, cards) are deleted when a peer trashes them. On a tie in date, each family merges the two contents the same way on both sides and erases nothing the other keeps: the note or description that one side lacks is taken over, two notes are kept together, the furthest review wins. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{skipped}}, in the exported page, counts the journal objects whose content could not be read; a collection whose query designates rows by number (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{id12}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ma3}}) does not carry it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Synchronization server.} The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Synchronization} tab of the settings (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{manuel_interface:synchronisation-distante}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Synchronization}}}}}) keeps the open library in the same state as a remote server, whichever it is, provided it answers the same two calls as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb serve}}, under the address the user pastes (its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<base>}} may carry a prefix, for example \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{https://host/api}}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST <base>/v1/changeset.export}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"cursor": \{…\}, "limit": N\}}} returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{200}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"cursor": \{…\}, "more": bool, "records": {[}…{]}\}}}. The cursor is opaque, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{\}}} starts over from the beginning; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} does not exceed 1000 (the application asks for 500). A record is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"seq", "uuid", "family", "op", "changed\_at", "payload"?\}}}. The server must be able to resume from a cursor it issued, and answer \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{410}} when it can no longer resume one. A server that does not want to carry a record that is too large returns an empty page whose cursor goes past it and which names it: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"skipped": {[}\{"family", "uuid", "size"\}{]}}}. Without this, a single\sphinxhyphen{}record page is served whatever its size.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST <base>/v1/changeset.import}} with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"records": {[}…{]}\}}} (at most 500 records, those of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{changeset.export}}) merges, the last write winning, and returns \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{200}} and the report (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{applied}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{added}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{modified}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{removed}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{older}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{conflicts}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{missing}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsupported}}). A repeated record changes nothing.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every request carries \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Authorization: Bearer <token>}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Content\sphinxhyphen{}Type: application/json}}. The token never appears in the address. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{401}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{403}}: token refused; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{413}} with the code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{payload\_too\_large}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{record\_too\_large}}: upload too large for the server (any other \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{413}}, from a proxy for example, stops the run without skipping anything); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}} with code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{invalid\_body}}: body cut off or too slow; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{429}}: rate limit reached; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{410}} on export: stale cursor; any other failure carries the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"error": \{"code", "message"\}\}}} envelope of the calls above.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The application sends first, then receives, one page at a time. It keeps two cursors per server and per library: the local journal’s (what the server already has) and the server’s (what is already merged here), each advanced once its page is settled. A cursor refused by a journal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{410}}, or stale locally) starts over from the beginning, the import absorbing the repetition. Records received come back on the next upload, which the server absorbs the same way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{413 payload\_too\_large}} or a cut during upload, the application halves the page down to a single record. A single record that the server refuses for its size (explicit code), or that does not go through, is set aside: it is kept with its type and identifier in the synchronization state, retried on every run and listed in the synchronization screen. The same goes for a record that the server declares skipped on export. The server must therefore read a slowly sent body: the read timeout renews as long as the upload progresses.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Three marks can be added to a position: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{changeset.export}} carries all three, export and transfer the drawing and the origin link, but not the label. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.drawing}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.setDrawing}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"id": N, "marks": {[}…{]}\}}}) read and replace its drawing: arrows and squares, 40 at most; an empty list erases it. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.setDerivedFrom}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"id": N, "derivedFrom": \{"fromId": <origine>, "move": "13/7"\}\}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{null}} to erase) declares it a variant of another position; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.derivedFrom}} reads that link and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.variants}} lists its variants. A loop or a missing origin is refused. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.publicId}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.setPublicId}} read and set a label that blunderDB keeps without ever interpreting it.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.analyzeMissing}} triggers the gammonNet catch\sphinxhyphen{}up of the current tenant: write an analysis for every position that has none (\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0013-evaluations-fill-gaps-an-imported-analysis-is-never-overwritten.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0013}, \sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0015-blunderdb-serve-operates-on-a-library-it-does-not-expose-an-evaluator.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0015}). It is a \sphinxstylestrong{library} operation — it reads and writes stored positions and analyses — never a bare evaluator: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb serve}} operates on a library, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet serve}} evaluates a position. The response is an NDJSON stream (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{started}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{progress}}, then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{done}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{error}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cancelled}}), on the same model as the import endpoints; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.analyzeMissing.cancel}} (with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{job\_id}} received in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{started}} event) cancels a running catch\sphinxhyphen{}up and serves either sweep indifferently — a catch\sphinxhyphen{}up or a re\sphinxhyphen{}analysis (below). It is the same operation as the automatic run after an import and the explicit gesture of the graphical interface, and as the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb analyze}} subcommand (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{cli:cli}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Command Line Interface (CLI)}}}}}) — three forms, one logic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.sweepStale}} is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{analyzeMissing}}’s counterpart for re\sphinxhyphen{}analysis rather than gap\sphinxhyphen{}filling: every position whose analysis is entirely gammonNet’s own but stale — an engine version older than the one currently running, or a depth different from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ply}} — is re\sphinxhyphen{}evaluated at the requested depth. The staleness predicate is shared with the same batch in the graphical interface and in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb analyze \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stale}} (no duplicated logic across the three modes); a position carrying an XG, GNUbg or BGBlitz analysis is never touched, whatever its gammonNet content — \sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0013-evaluations-fill-gaps-an-imported-analysis-is-never-overwritten.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0013}’s protection remains unconditional. Same NDJSON shape as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{analyzeMissing}}, and the final event of each of the two routes carries the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{evaluated}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{refused}}/\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{failed}} breakdown: a position gammonNet declines to evaluate (a match score beyond its table’s range, a cube decision the model refuses) counts as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{refused}}, not \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{failed}} — it is never retried in vain on the next pass, unlike a position that genuinely failed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.position}} plays a library position (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positionId}}) by a {\hyperref[\detokenize{cli_analyse:cli-rollout}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{rollout}}}}} and returns, for each candidate, the equity, its 95\% interval and the JSD; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout}} carries the settings (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fast}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{standard}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{standard,ply=1}}…), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{store}} records the finished rollout as a second analysis, beside the one the position carries, which it never replaces. A bare position (an XGID) is refused: the daemon operates on a library. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.filter}} is the batch form of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb analyze \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rollout}}: the positions chosen by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{query}} (the search language) that do not yet carry a rollout with the same settings are played one after the other and recorded as they go, as an NDJSON stream (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{started}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{progress}} after each series of games, then \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{done}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cancelled}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quota\_exceeded}}); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.filter.cancel}} cancels it with its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{job\_id}}. A tenant runs only one batch at a time, rollout or gammonNet. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.list}} reads the recorded rollouts of a position.


\subsection{Correlation and business metrics}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:correlation-et-metriques-metier}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Every request gets a correlation identifier: the one the client (or a reverse proxy) sends in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Request\sphinxhyphen{}Id}} header, otherwise a generated one — either way returned on the same header of the response and added to the request’s closing log line (field \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{request\_id}}). A \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{traceparent}} (\sphinxhref{https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/}{W3C Trace Context}), when present, is relayed as\sphinxhyphen{}is into that same log line — the daemon neither parses nor validates it, and embeds no tracing library: it is a bridge for correlating these logs with a tracing pipeline running upstream, nothing more.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Beyond request volume and latency, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/metrics}} publishes gauges on the work in flight, otherwise invisible for a stuck import or gammonNet batch (one very long request, not many requests):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\_imports\_inflight}} — imports under way, across all tenants;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\_import\_spool\_bytes}} — bytes currently reserved against the import spool quota (see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rate\sphinxhyphen{}limit\sphinxhyphen{}*}} above for the requests\sphinxhyphen{}per\sphinxhyphen{}second counterpart);

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\_gammonnet\_sweep\_inflight}} — gammonNet catch\sphinxhyphen{}up sweeps under way, across all tenants;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\_database\_size\_bytes}} — size of the main SQLite file, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pg\_database\_size}} under PostgreSQL (the whole database, not per tenant, like the connection\sphinxhyphen{}pool gauges below); absent until a first measurement has been published.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A memory or CPU profile of the process is available by starting with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pprof\sphinxhyphen{}addr <host:port>}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{net/http/pprof}}): off by default, and deliberately on an address separate from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}addr}}, since these endpoints have no notion of tenant.


\subsection{Stream compression}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:compression-des-flux}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-docker}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
NDJSON listings repeat the same field names on every line. The daemon compresses them when the client accepts it: send \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accept\sphinxhyphen{}Encoding: gzip}} and the response comes back as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Content\sphinxhyphen{}Encoding: gzip}}. Measured on a match listing: \sphinxstylestrong{13.5\%} of the original size over a thousand lines, 14.6\% over a hundred.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compression changes nothing about the stream being incremental — each record is pushed to the client as before, only compressed on the way. It applies to NDJSON, JSON and text responses only: a database export or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.dbx}} container is already compressed, and re\sphinxhyphen{}gzipping it would only make it bigger. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Accept\sphinxhyphen{}Encoding: gzip;q=0}} refuses it explicitly.


\subsection{A single tenant on SQLite}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:un-seul-tenant-sur-sqlite}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The SQLite backend has \sphinxstylestrong{no} tenant column: all the data sits in the same tables, with no partition. On that backend the daemon therefore refuses any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}} other than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}} — accepting the others would mean serving everyone everybody’s rows behind a header claiming otherwise. A deployment that genuinely has several tenants needs the PostgreSQL backend.


\subsection{Reading several tenants}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:lire-plusieurs-tenants}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-tenants-lus}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A coach who reads their students’ matches, a club that shares a library: the relationship between these accounts lives with the host that authenticates them, never in the daemon. The proxy expresses it with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Read\sphinxhyphen{}Tenants}} header, a comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated list of tenants (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Read\sphinxhyphen{}Tenants: 2, 3}}), which it sets next to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}. The daemon trusts it as it trusts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}} and authorizes nothing itself (\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0063-une-lecture-peut-porter-sur-les-tenants-que-le-proxy-liste.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0063}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The feature is \sphinxstylestrong{disabled by default}, and disabled means refused: until the daemon is started with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}read\sphinxhyphen{}tenants}} (or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BLUNDERDB\_READ\_TENANTS=true}}; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Config.TrustReadTenants}} for a host that embeds the engine), any request carrying a non\sphinxhyphen{}empty \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Read\sphinxhyphen{}Tenants}} is refused (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}}), whatever the route. Enable it only once the proxy is configured to strip any client\sphinxhyphen{}sent value and to set the list itself.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/across.*}} reads look at this header. The full list: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.searchFind}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.matchesList}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.statsCompute}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.playerTable}}; they read \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}} first, then each tenant listed in header order, at most 64 distinct tenants in all. On a tenant from the list, named with the id: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.matchesGet}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.matchMovePositions}} (the positions of a match, move by move, in pages of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} / \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{offset}}) and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.analysesLoadByIds}}; a tenant absent from the list is refused there. Each result carries its tenant of origin (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"tenant": "2"}}), because an id is unique only within its tenant; a position also carries its Zobrist hash (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"zobrist"}}), which designates the same board in every tenant. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}} applies to each tenant; 0 means 1000, and a larger value is refused. In an NDJSON stream, an error on a late tenant arrives as the last line, after the results of the tenants already read: the whole stream then fails.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}s\PYG{+w}{ }http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/across.matchesList\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}Content\PYGZhy{}Type: application/json\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 1\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Read\PYGZhy{}Tenants: 2, 3\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}d\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}limit\PYGZdq{}:20\PYGZcb{}\PYGZsq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every write stays in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}: no route outside \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.*}} reads \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Read\sphinxhyphen{}Tenants}}, and the only one in this family that writes, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.transferPull}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:mode-headless-transfert}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Pulling a copy from a read tenant}}}}}), writes into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}. Without the header, an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.*}} read covers only \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}. A malformed header (a name, an empty element, more than 64 tenants) or one sent on several lines refuses the whole request, whatever the route. On SQLite, which has a single tenant, the list can only contain \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}: the header widens nothing there. These routes are specific to the server: the desktop app and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{call}} have a single tenant.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.*}} request costs up to 64 storage reads, but the rate limit (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}rate\sphinxhyphen{}limit\sphinxhyphen{}rps}}) counts it only once, for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}: size the database and this limit accordingly, or have the proxy bound the list. The access log of an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.*}} route carries the list received (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{read\_tenants}} field). The header is not among the allowed CORS headers: only the proxy writes it, never a browser.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Five reads serve the club and the coach, on the same list (\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0065-club-et-coach-lisent-a-travers-les-tenants-et-n-ecrivent-que-chez-soi.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0065}):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{coach comments}: the coach stores a student’s position in their own tenant (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.save}} under their own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}, same hash) and comments on it (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{comments.add}}); nothing is written to the student’s tenant. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.commentsByZobrist}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"zobrists": {[}...{]}\}}}, at most 1000 hashes) returns the comments that each tenant read has written on these boards, each with its tenant, the position id in that tenant and its origin;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{elsewhere}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.positionElsewhere}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"zobrist": H\}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"position": \{...\}\}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{neighbours}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{maxDistance}}) returns, for each tenant read other than \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}, what it knows about this board: the id of its copy, its analysis, its comments, the matches where it was played and its neighbouring boards. Moves are judged with the thresholds of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}; an analysis made with another equity table is flagged (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{otherMet}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb elsewhere}} performs the same lookup on files; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.objectElsewhere}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"kind": "match", "id": N\}}}, or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tournament}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collection}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{lesson}}) says whether each of these tenants holds that object of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}, under the key a copy would merge it on (the match fingerprint, the name otherwise), with its id and what it contains;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{shared library}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.collectionsList}} lists the collections of the tenants read, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.collectionPositions}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tenant}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collectionId}}) the positions of one of them, each with its hash. The library is read in place, never copied: sharing a collection by file (export then import), by contrast, gives the recipient a copy;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{club ranking}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.clubRanking}} merges the player tables of the tenants read into a single ranking, best PR first, on the given statistics filter (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter.DateFrom}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter.DateTo}} for a period). Each row carries its tenant; a name is never merged from one tenant to another. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{players}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tenant}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} pairs) keeps only those players, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{minDecisions}} drops those with fewer counted decisions; at equal PR the rank is shared, and a row with no counted decision has rank 0. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{filter.TournamentIDs}} is refused there (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}}): a tournament id is valid only within its own tenant. The response is a page (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}, 100 by default, 1000 at most; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{offset}}) with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{total}}, the number of rows of the whole ranking. This is not the season ranking of directed tournaments.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Pulling a copy from a read tenant}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:tirer-une-copie-d-un-tenant-lu}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:mode-headless-transfert}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.transferPull}} copies part of a tenant from the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Read\sphinxhyphen{}Tenants}} list into \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}: it is the command\sphinxhyphen{}line \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transfer}} command ({\hyperref[\detokenize{cli_import_export:cli-transfer}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{transfer — Copy from one library to another}}}}}), between two tenants. The body names the source tenant (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tenant}}, which must appear in the list) and, under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export}}, the selection, with the keys of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exports.sqlite}} body (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{includeMatches}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{collectionIDs}}…); without \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{export}}, the whole tenant is copied. The copy is merged like the import of a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} database: a position already present is recognised by its hash, and a match, collection or lesson already present is not duplicated, so pulling from 2 into 1 and then from 1 into 2 creates no duplicate. The response counts what was read (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exported}}) and what the tenant took from it (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{imported}}). The positions follow the rules of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{transfer}}: as soon as a list of IDs is given, only those reached by the retained families are sent; a collection goes with its members; a named match carries the record of its tournament, not its other matches. An ID that the source tenant does not contain is refused (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}}). To copy collection 3 and its positions, nothing else is needed:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}s\PYG{+w}{ }http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/across.transferPull\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}Content\PYGZhy{}Type: application/json\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 1\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}X\PYGZhy{}Read\PYGZhy{}Tenants: 2\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}d\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}tenant\PYGZdq{}:\PYGZdq{}2\PYGZdq{},\PYGZdq{}export\PYGZdq{}:\PYGZob{}\PYGZdq{}collectionIDs\PYGZdq{}:[3],\PYGZdq{}includeMatches\PYGZdq{}:false,\PYGZdq{}includeTournaments\PYGZdq{}:false,\PYGZdq{}includeLessons\PYGZdq{}:false,\PYGZdq{}includeAnkiDecks\PYGZdq{}:false\PYGZcb{}\PYGZcb{}\PYGZsq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The transfer is always \sphinxstylestrong{pulled} by the receiving tenant, never pushed into another: reads go across tenants and writes only go to one’s own (\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0102-un-transfert-est-un-export-fusionne-par-l-import-natif.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0102}). Nothing is written that says where the copy comes from, in either tenant: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{watermark}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{password}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{incremental}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{metadata}} are rejected (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{400}}), as is a tenant absent from the list or the tenant itself. A transfer counts as an import of the receiving tenant (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}quota\sphinxhyphen{}imports}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}quota\sphinxhyphen{}positions}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}quota\sphinxhyphen{}bytes}}) and is interrupted when the daemon stops.


\subsection{Backup and restore}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:sauvegarde-et-restauration}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-sauvegarde}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Four gestures, depending on what is to be recovered.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Everything, under PostgreSQL} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pg\_dump}} is the tool, and blunderDB has nothing to add:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pg\PYGZus{}dump\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}format\PYG{o}{=}custom\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}file\PYG{o}{=}blunderdb.dump\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}postgres://…\PYGZdq{}}
pg\PYGZus{}restore\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}dbname\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}postgres://…\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }blunderdb.dump
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Everything, under SQLite in a container} — the file is opened in WAL mode (the daemon encodes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{journal\_mode(WAL)}} in its connection string, for every connection in the pool): alongside \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb.db}} live a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}wal}} and a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}shm}}, and the most recent writes are in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}wal}}. Copying the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} alone from a running daemon therefore gives an incomplete file, with nothing to signal it. Two safe ways:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{stop the daemon, then copy the whole volume} — once stopped, the three files are consistent, and it is the volume, not the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} alone, that is the unit to back up;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{do not copy the file at all}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/exports.sqlite}} (below) writes a complete \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} while the daemon is running, and it is the only gesture that requires no interruption.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/ops/maintenance.vacuum}} does fold the WAL back into the main file before rewriting it, but it does not freeze the database: the next write starts a new WAL. It is a compaction command, not a backup method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{One tenant alone} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/exports.sqlite}} writes a tenant’s database into an ordinary \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} file, the one the desktop application opens:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}X\PYG{+w}{ }POST\PYG{+w}{ }http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/exports.sqlite\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}H\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID: 42\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}o\PYG{+w}{ }tenant\PYGZhy{}42.db
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command runs \sphinxstylestrong{on the daemon’s own machine}: it targets the local listener, bypasses the proxy, and therefore sets the tenant header itself. From outside, it is the proxy that is queried, and the tenant is that of the authenticated account — the header is not to be supplied, the proxy strips the client’s before injecting its own:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
curl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}u\PYG{+w}{ }alice:…\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}X\PYG{+w}{ }POST\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }https://blunderdb.example.com/v1/exports.sqlite\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}o\PYG{+w}{ }tenant\PYGZhy{}alice.db
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Putting that file back} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{migrate}} copies it under the tenant you name:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
./blunderdb\PYG{+w}{ }migrate\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}from\PYG{+w}{ }tenant\PYGZhy{}42.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}to\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}postgres://…\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}tenant\PYGZhy{}id\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{42}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{migrate}} refuses to write into a tenant that already holds something, and says what (“128 positions, 3 matches”); \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}on\sphinxhyphen{}conflict skip}} goes ahead anyway and lets Zobrist de\sphinxhyphen{}duplication merge the positions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{migrate}} also copies lessons, with their steps in order; a step points to the collections and positions that were moved.

\sphinxAtStartPar
What \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{migrate}} does \sphinxstylestrong{not} copy, and announces at the end with the exact count: the Anki decks and their cards, the filter library, the search and command histories, and the session state. These are the desktop application’s usage data; the positions they refer to have indeed been moved.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{error and blunder thresholds}, for their part, are copied: they are not usage data but the reading habit the counts depend on, and a tenant that counted differently from the file it came from would make the migration a silent change of meaning.

\sphinxAtStartPar
A tenant sets its own through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST /v1/librarySettings.load}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/v1/librarySettings.save}}. Unlike \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{metadata}}, which is global infrastructure exposed read\sphinxhyphen{}only, the settings table carries a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tenant\_id}} and lives under Row\sphinxhyphen{}Level Security: a tenant writing its thresholds reaches nothing but its own rows.


\subsection{The desktop and the server}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:le-poste-de-travail-et-le-serveur}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-poste-serveur}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The desktop application opens \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} \sphinxstylestrong{files}, not URLs: it never connects to any \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{serve}} daemon, and there is nowhere a field to type an address. The server and the desktop exchange files, in two symmetric gestures:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{from the server to the desktop} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{POST /v1/exports.sqlite}} writes the whole current tenant into a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} the desktop application opens as\sphinxhyphen{}is (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-sauvegarde}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Backup and restore}}}}});

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{from the desktop to the server} — \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb migrate}} copies a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} under the intended tenant (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-migrate}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Migrating a SQLite database to PostgreSQL}}}}}).

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Nothing a tenant stores is visible to another, except through the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.*}} reads, and only on the tenants the proxy lists in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Read\sphinxhyphen{}Tenants}} under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{serve \sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}read\sphinxhyphen{}tenants}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-tenants-lus}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-ref}{Reading several tenants}}}}}). Any other request knows only the tenant the proxy set for it. A coach who wants to see their students’ matches therefore has three paths, all explicit:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
read their matches through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{across.*}}, the proxy listing the students’ tenants;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
open an additional account for them in the proxy, associated with the student’s tenant: it is the proxy’s mapping table, never the daemon, that decides which tenant a session sees;

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ask them for an export — the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.db}} produced by \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exports.sqlite}} or by the desktop application’s export window — and open it on their own desktop.

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Deployment with Docker}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:deploiement-avec-docker}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The repository provides a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dockerfile.serve}} that builds a minimal container image of the daemon: only the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{serve}} binary is compiled (pure Go, with no graphical interface and no CGO, therefore statically linked), then placed into a \sphinxstyleemphasis{distroless} image.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} build}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}f\PYG{+w}{ }Dockerfile.serve\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }blunderdb\PYGZhy{}serve\PYG{+w}{ }.

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} run}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}p\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{127}.0.0.1:8080:8080\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{BLUNDERDB\PYGZus{}DSN}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}postgres://user:pass@host:5432/blunderdb?sslmode=disable\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }blunderdb\PYGZhy{}serve
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The build is run from the repository root, and the image’s default backend is \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{postgres}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The image listens on port 8080 and is configured through environment variables (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BLUNDERDB\_BACKEND}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BLUNDERDB\_DSN}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BLUNDERDB\_ADDR}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{BLUNDERDB\_RLS}}). It declares a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{HEALTHCHECK}} that runs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb healthcheck}} every 30 seconds (a request on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/readyz}} — the \sphinxstyleemphasis{distroless} image has neither \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{curl}} nor a shell): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{docker ps}} shows the container as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{healthy}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unhealthy}}, and Compose or an orchestrator can wait for the daemon to be ready before starting what depends on it.


\subsubsection{Published image}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:image-publiee}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-docker-image}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
There is no need to build the image yourself: every published blunderDB release pushes its own to the GitHub registry (GHCR), under the name \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ghcr.io/kevung/blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}serve}}. Two tags are available: the version number, frozen forever on that image, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{latest}}, which follows the most recently published version. All the documentation writes them as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ghcr.io/kevung/blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}serve:<version>}}: it is a published version number that takes the place of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{<version>}}, and it is that form, never \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{latest}}, that a production deployment pins. The image is provided for \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{linux/amd64}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{linux/arm64}}; Docker picks the host architecture.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} pull}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }pull\PYG{+w}{ }ghcr.io/kevung/blunderdb\PYGZhy{}serve:\PYGZlt{}version\PYGZgt{}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} postgres}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}p\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{127}.0.0.1:8080:8080\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{BLUNDERDB\PYGZus{}DSN}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}postgres://user:pass@host:5432/blunderdb?sslmode=disable\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }ghcr.io/kevung/blunderdb\PYGZhy{}serve:\PYGZlt{}version\PYGZgt{}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} sqlite}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}p\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{127}.0.0.1:8080:8080\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}v\PYG{+w}{ }blunderdb\PYGZhy{}data:/data\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{BLUNDERDB\PYGZus{}BACKEND}\PYG{o}{=}sqlite\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{BLUNDERDB\PYGZus{}DSN}\PYG{o}{=}/data/blunderdb.db\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }ghcr.io/kevung/blunderdb\PYGZhy{}serve:\PYGZlt{}version\PYGZgt{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/data}} is the mount point the image prepares, with its unprivileged user’s permissions, and its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{XDG\_DATA\_HOME}}: the volume mounted there is not only for the database — the bearoff tables are computed there once, in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/data/blunderdb}}, and found again on later startups. Without a volume, they are recomputed on every container start — a few seconds — and the daemon says so at startup if it cannot write them (\sphinxstyleemphasis{could not prepare the bearoff tables; the exact regime will be unavailable}), in which case it serves normally, with only the estimated regime on bearoff positions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The image carries the usual OCI labels (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{org.opencontainers.image.source}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.version}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.revision}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.licenses}}): \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{docker inspect}} tells which commit and which version it comes from. It is built by continuous integration from the repo’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Dockerfile.serve}}, exactly as above; building locally or pulling the published image gives the same binary.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Like the daemon itself, the container performs \sphinxstylestrong{no authentication} (\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-serve-daemon-delegates-authentication.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0005}): it trusts the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}} header exactly as it receives it. It must be placed behind a reverse proxy responsible for authentication, which sets that header itself, and must never be exposed directly to the public Internet. The examples above publish the port on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{127.0.0.1}} only for this reason, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}addr}} likewise binds to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{127.0.0.1}}: the proxy is on the same machine.
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\subsection{Deployment behind an authenticating proxy}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:deploiement-derriere-un-proxy-authentifiant}}\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:headless-proxy-deployment}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-serve-daemon-delegates-authentication.md}{ADR\sphinxhyphen{}0005} makes the reverse proxy \sphinxstylestrong{the whole} of the daemon’s security boundary: it alone authenticates the caller, it alone is allowed to set the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}} header, and it must \sphinxstylestrong{strip} any value sent by the client before injecting the authenticated tenant — otherwise anyone can impersonate any tenant simply by naming it. The threat model fits in one sentence: the daemon assumes a trusted internal network, and whoever reaches it directly is, as far as it is concerned, the tenant it claims to be. The repository ships a complete, ready\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}run example in the \sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/tree/main/deploy}{deploy/} directory. It lives in the git repository, not in the container image: so \sphinxstylestrong{clone the repository}, or download the two files reproduced below together with \sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/deploy/.env.example}{deploy/.env.example} into the same directory.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Compose file puts Caddy — demonstration HTTP Basic authentication — in front of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{blunderdb\sphinxhyphen{}serve}} and PostgreSQL, with Row\sphinxhyphen{}Level Security enabled. Only Caddy publishes a port: the other two services live on a Docker network declared \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{internal: true}}, which has no route to either the host or the Internet, whatever \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ports:}} a later change might add to them.
\sphinxSetupCaptionForVerbatim{deploy/docker\sphinxhyphen{}compose.yml}
\def\sphinxLiteralBlockLabel{\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:id1}}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Example deployment of `blunderdb serve` behind an authenticating reverse}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} proxy — the security model ADR\PYGZhy{}0005 requires and, until now, that no example}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} in this repository actually showed. See deploy/README.md for the threat}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} model and doc/source/mode\PYGZus{}headless.rst for the full walkthrough.}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Try it from the repository root:}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   POSTGRES\PYGZus{}PASSWORD=changeme docker compose \PYGZhy{}f deploy/docker\PYGZhy{}compose.yml up \PYGZhy{}d \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}build}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   curl \PYGZhy{}u alice:demo\PYGZhy{}password http://localhost:8080/v1/metadata.counts \PYGZhy{}d \PYGZsq{}\PYGZob{}\PYGZcb{}\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{}   docker compose \PYGZhy{}f deploy/docker\PYGZhy{}compose.yml down \PYGZhy{}v}

\PYG{n+nt}{services}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Caddy is the ENTIRE security boundary (ADR\PYGZhy{}0005): it is the only service}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} with a published port, it authenticates every request, and it is the}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} only thing allowed to set X\PYGZhy{}Tenant\PYGZhy{}ID — see Caddyfile. Any reverse proxy}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} capable of stripping and re\PYGZhy{}setting a header works equally well; Caddy is}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} used here for its one\PYGZhy{}file config and built\PYGZhy{}in Basic Auth with no extra}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} modules. deploy/nginx\PYGZhy{}tenant\PYGZhy{}proxy.conf shows the equivalent nginx}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} snippet for an existing nginx deployment.}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Caddyfile}}’s HTTP Basic authentication is a demonstration, not a production recommendation: replace it with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{forward\_auth}} to a real identity provider (OIDC, enterprise SSO…), which authenticates and then hands off the identity at the same spot in the file. The two passwords and the two accounts in the mapping table are to be replaced the same way.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhref{https://github.com/kevung/blunderDB/blob/main/deploy/Caddyfile.oidc}{deploy/Caddyfile.oidc} is the OpenID Connect recipe: Caddy queries oauth2\sphinxhyphen{}proxy (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{forward\_auth}} on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/oauth2/auth}}), which answers 202 with the signed\sphinxhyphen{}in account’s address in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Auth\sphinxhyphen{}Request\sphinxhyphen{}Email}}, or redirects to the provider’s sign\sphinxhyphen{}in page. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{map}} block maps that address to the tenant’s integer, and the same \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{header\_up X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID ""}} guard precedes the injection. The oauth2\sphinxhyphen{}proxy service to add to the Compose file is at the top of the file.


\subsubsection{Per\sphinxhyphen{}tenant quotas}
\label{\detokenize{mode_headless:quotas-par-tenant}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A shared instance bounds what each tenant takes from it with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}quota\sphinxhyphen{}positions}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}quota\sphinxhyphen{}bytes}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}quota\sphinxhyphen{}analysis\sphinxhyphen{}seconds}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}quota\sphinxhyphen{}imports}} (without an option, nothing is bounded). Computation time counts every engine computation requested by the tenant: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.analyzeMissing}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.sweepStale}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.compare}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.cubeMatrix}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.evaluate}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.position}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.filter}}. It is counted in CPU seconds: the elapsed time of each computation, plus that of the idle workers over which its search spread, so a computation spread over all cores costs as much as the same work done position by position. Once the day’s time is used up, these routes answer 429 with the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quota\_exceeded}} code. A sweep or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.filter}} in progress keeps what it has recorded and ends on the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quota\_exceeded}} event instead of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{done}}; an interrupted \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.position}} answers 429 and records nothing; an interrupted comparison returns what it has folded with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quotaExceeded: true}} and, in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gathered}}, the number of positions it had to examine. The count resets to zero at midnight UTC and lives in memory: restarting the daemon resets it. The positions quota is checked at the start of an import, which is not interrupted midway: a tenant can exceed it by as much as its imports in progress add. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{positions.save}} and the other single writes do not check it. The bytes quota is checked at the same moment and with the same latitude. Under SQLite, a database holds only one library: the tenant occupies the live pages of the file. Under PostgreSQL, tenants share the tables and no row carries its size: the space of each table (indexes included) is distributed in proportion to the rows, so a tenant holding a third of a table’s rows is counted a third of its space. This is an estimate, which follows the planner’s statistics. Each refusal carries in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{details}} the limit (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quota}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit}}) and the usage (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{used}}). \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tenants.quota}} returns to the calling tenant its limits and its usage: stored positions, bytes occupied (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{storedBytes}}), computation seconds of the day, imports in progress.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quotas are the daemon’s bookkeeping, not a boundary: they apply to the tenant that the proxy has set in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{X\sphinxhyphen{}Tenant\sphinxhyphen{}ID}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Every engine computation goes through a single analysis queue: sweeps (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.analyzeMissing}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.sweepStale}}), evaluations (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.evaluate}}), comparisons (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.compare}}), cube matrices (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gammonnet.cubeMatrix}}) and rollouts (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.position}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.filter}}). It is a set of engine workers (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analysis\sphinxhyphen{}workers}}), each with its own reused searcher, which take positions one by one, going round the tenants that have work. Two tenants sweeping at the same time share the cores instead of each claiming them; an evaluation requested during another tenant’s sweep waits for one position, not for the whole sweep. A search run while workers are idle (a lone evaluation, the end of a sweep) spreads over them, never exceeding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analysis\sphinxhyphen{}workers}} cores; its result does not change by a single bit. With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}analysis\sphinxhyphen{}weights 7=3}}, tenant \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7}} receives three positions per turn when another receives one. The jobs of a single tenant run in the order they arrived. A rollout takes its turn game by game: one tenant’s long rollout does not keep another tenant’s short request from being served before it ends, and its results do not change (they depend only on the settings and the seed). Every position, cell or game computed is charged to its tenant’s quota of computing seconds. While the daemon is shutting down, an evaluation, a cube matrix or a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rollout.position}} rollout still in the queue answers \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{503}} (code \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unavailable}}), recording nothing.

\sphinxAtStartPar
